title: Staged plan: a later stage that enlarges a kept subject books nothing for the increment
description: Found while implementing renovisorissues #53 (hisim-is7w), 2026-09-26. StagedEvaluator._charged_subjects charges an enlarged subject its size increment ((new-old)/new), but _staged_inputs registers the earlier stage's purchase of the same subject as an ExistingAsset with replaced_by_asset_classes=[] (the subject is in the later stage's facts), so the later stage's own evaluation sees the subject as KEPT (installation_verdict), books no year-0 entries, and share x nothing = 0. Reproduced on the synthetic stages: PV 5 kWp bought in stage 1, 8 kWp in stage 2 (from_year 2): charged {'PV': 0.375} for stage 2, and the plan's timeline carries only the stage-1 INVESTMENT of 5000. A reader's quote for such a stage's measure (investment_overrides) is accepted by the staged command (the subject is charged) and then books nothing either. Decide: price the increment (evaluate the enlarged subject as a new purchase and keep the share), or refuse/declare it.
close_reason: fix/staged-instalments: a later stage that enlarges a kept subject buys the increment as its own purchase (subject#increment_stage<k>)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decision (cmf, 2026-09-28): price the increment. The later stage buys the increment as a new purchase (size difference at the database price for that size, escalated to its from_year; a reader's quote replaces it), with its own life and replacements; the earlier purchase keeps ageing.

title: renovisor layers: ElementAreas.resolve misses the TABULA-default area, so an unstated element area leaves embodied CO2 and per-layer figures missing
description: Sibling of renovisorissues #61 (fixed in economics.py _element_area). hisim/renovisor/layers.py ElementAreas.resolve reads <element>_area_in_m2 from the realized Building config, then the request; when the request states no area (allowed, calculation-request §3.4) neither has it, so result.json's embodied_co2_in_kg is reported missing ('no element area') although the Building simulates the TABULA row's scaled area. Fix the same way: read the area from BuildingInformation over the realized Building config, source phrase naming the TABULA default.
close_reason: embodied CO2 uses the area the Building simulates (SimulatedEnvelope, fix/envelope-area-pricing)

title: Measure the part-load open points against the 60 s reference: missed restarts, the heat pump's COP above 63 degC, cycling losses
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §10 (owner, 2026-10-09).

The part-load approach leaves three effects to be measured against the 60 s reference and remedied only if they matter: (1) heating restarts missed inside a coarse step (a controller off on T0 does not restart when draws cool the store during the step); (2) the heat pump's COP above about 63 degC evaluated at T-bar only (remedy: COP along the node's curve within the step); (3) cycling losses for fractions below 1 (EN 14825 Cd for heat pumps, part-load efficiency for boilers). Each remedy applies above the threshold only, so 60 s stays the reference.

title: Component physics defects and fidelity gaps
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md, roadmap/p3_random_findings.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md

Defects and fidelity gaps in the component models and the simulator core, collected while
building the RenoVisor translator (`simulation_issues.md`, 2026-07-05) and while running the
declarative migration. Fidelity items are measurable: everything the translator cannot express
shows up as `ignored`/`approximated` in its mapping report.

title: Guard the window U-value division so a TABULA row with zero window area cannot crash
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 2 ("Same division pattern for windows -- latent crash"), with the
follow-up of item 1

The window U-value is the area-weighted average `(u1*a1 + u2*a2) / (a1 + a2)`. A TABULA row with
`A_Window_1 == A_Window_2 == 0` crashes identically to the door case of item 1.

State of the code (checked 2026-09-20): item 1 is fixed --
`hisim/components/building/information.py` gives the door element
`keep_u_value_when_reference_area_is_zero=True`, and the guard skips the division when the
reference area is zero while preserving the pinned `(u * area) / area` float round trip that
shifts the last mantissa bit for 164 TABULA codes. Item 3 is fixed too
(`_thermal_bridging_conductance_in_watt_per_kelvin` uses a local value instead of writing 0.1
back into the shared dataframe). The window element declares two area columns and no such guard,
so item 2 is the one still open.

Follow-up once fixed, from item 1: `hisim/renovisor/tabula.py::_is_usable` still requires
`door > 0 and window > 0`. The `door > 0` half is already unnecessary; the `window > 0` half
becomes unnecessary with this fix, at which point the band substitution and the expectations in
`tests/renovisor/` can go back to the exact bands.

Testing: cover via a synthetic `buildingdata_ref` row with both window areas zero, and assert a
normal German code's U-value is unchanged.
close_reason: done by #795 (c7b51bce): the window U-value survives zero window areas

title: Derive the country-specific ArcheTypeConfig defaults instead of inheriting German ones
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 14

`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/archetype_config.py` defaults to
`weather_try_region: int = 6`, Aachen coordinates, a German postal code and a DE building code.
Non-German archetypes inherit German defaults for every field the caller does not set, and
nothing warns about the mismatch (a TRY region has no meaning for Dublin). The RenoVisor
translator overrides what it can, but any new field added with a German default silently degrades
non-DE runs.

Suggested fix: make the country-specific fields `Optional[...] = None` and derive them from
`weather_location` / `building_code` when unset; log which defaults were applied.

Testing: construct an IE archetype without the optional fields and assert no German TRY region is
used downstream.

title: Stop the DHW storage temperature running away at 3600 s timesteps
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 15 -- observed crash, listed in the document's own priority 1

Running `household_gas_building_sizer.py` (via the RenoVisor translator, config
`IE.N.SFH.04.Gen.ReEx.001.001`, full year 2019) at `seconds_per_timestep=3600` aborts with
"The water temperature in the DHW water storage is with 98.32 degC way too high or too low."
The same configuration proceeds normally at the default 900 s. The DHW charging control overshoots
when one timestep spans a whole hour (a full hour of heating power is committed before the
controller sees the new temperature): the components are stable at 15 min but not at 1 h, and
nothing validates the timestep range a setup supports.

Why it matters: coarse resolutions are the natural lever for fast batch and screening runs
(RenoVisor previews, building-sizer iterations). Today they fail late -- after component setup
and possibly hours into a batch -- rather than being either supported or rejected upfront.

Suggested fix, either or both: (1) make the DHW storage / heat-source controller timestep-aware,
scaling the hysteresis band or limiting charging power so one timestep cannot overshoot the
target band (`P_max ~ storage_capacity * dT_band / dt`); (2) have setups declare a supported
timestep range and fail fast in `SimulationParameters` validation with a clear message instead of
mid-simulation.

Testing: regression test running the gas building-sizer setup for a winter week at 900 s, 1800 s
and 3600 s, asserting the DHW temperature stays within bounds; if option 2 is chosen, assert the
clear early error instead.
close_reason: The range check read an intermediate convergence iterate; moved to i_doublecheck (fix/dhw-runaway)

title: Make the EMS restore a copy of its state rather than a reference
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states" and "Independent repairs surfaced by the
analyses" (out of scope there, named as a prerequisite for checkpointing)

`hisim/components/controller_l2_energy_management_system.py:665`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restores the state."""
        self.state = self.previous_state

That assigns the reference, not a clone, so after the first restore `self.state` and
`self.previous_state` are the same object and every later `i_save_state` and `i_restore_state`
pair is a no-op on a shared object. Siblings that get it right use `self_copy()` (see
`heat_distribution_system.py:398`).

The epic records why it matters beyond correctness in the convergence loop: `i_save_state` is a
convergence scratchpad, not a checkpoint contract, and this is one of two live bugs proving it;
both have to be fixed on their own merits before checkpoint handover (the seeded-restart tier of
the mid-year oracle) is discussable.

Done when: the restore clones, and a test forces an extra convergence iteration and asserts the
outputs are identical (the epic's M6-shaped state-leak check).

title: Make the heat-distribution controller restore its mode instead of self-assigning
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`hisim/components/heat_distribution_system.py:1180`:

    def i_restore_state(self) -> None:
        """Restore the previous state."""
        self.controller_heat_distribution_mode = self.controller_heat_distribution_mode

The self-assignment restores nothing: whatever the controller did during a rejected convergence
iteration is kept. There is no `previous_...` attribute saved in `i_save_state` to restore from,
so the fix is to save and restore one.

The second of the two live `i_save_state` defects the mid-year analyses surfaced; both are
prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

Done when: the mode is saved and restored, and a forced extra iteration leaves the outputs
identical.

title: Split the building's initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius from the comfort floor
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

`initial_internal_temperature_in_celsius` doubles as the permanent window-opening comfort floor
in the building's free-cooling rule -- a field named "initial" that is silently a model
parameter. The epic names it as the one blocker to untangle before any building-side seasonal
default: changing the initial temperature for a mid-year window would change the comfort rule for
the whole run.

Done when: the two meanings are separate fields, the free-cooling rule reads the comfort one, and
the goldens confirm no behaviour moved at the current values.

title: Calibrate the hplib heat pump to a stated standardized SCOP instead of the Generic fit
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21; numbers below from an EN 14825 bin-method check over the
hplib database on the same day (script not kept, method described here so it can be redone).

The RenoVisor twins heat with `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib`, whose COP is hplib's linear curve fit
`COP = p1*T_source + p2*T_flow + p3 + p4*T_ambient` evaluated every timestep, with `model="Generic"`
(hplib's regression over its whole air/water or brine/water group). There is no way to make the
machine match a stated seasonal COP. A user knows the manufacturer's standardized SCOP (EN 14825,
average climate, at W35 or W55), so the machine should be calibrated to that figure, and the house,
climate, flow temperature and controller then produce the realized seasonal performance factor as
they do today.

Findings behind the design (2026-09-21 check):
- hplib's database carries no SCOP column, only the fit coefficients and the reference point.
- Running the EN 14825 bin method (average climate hours per outdoor-temperature bin, part load
  linear from full at -10 C to zero at 16 C, flow temperature falling from 52 C at A-7 to 30 C at
  A12 for W55 and from 34 C to 24 C for W35, inverter modulation at constant COP down to hplib's
  25 % clamp, backup rod at COP 1 above capacity) over the fit gives Generic air/water SCOP 3.40 at
  W55 and 4.74 at W35; the 366 real air/water rows span 2.95..3.65 (W55, 5th..95th percentile),
  interquartile 3.22..3.42. The device spread is narrow; realized performance is dominated by
  flow temperature and climate, which HiSim already simulates.
- Matching to the nearest database device is rejected: many devices share one SCOP with different
  temperature slopes and some fits are extrapolation artefacts (one row computes 5.57 at W55 but
  3.73 at W35, physically impossible). Calibrate the Generic fit instead.

Design:
1. Component: two optional fields on `MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig`, `standardized_scop:
   Optional[float]` and `scop_application: Optional[ScopApplication]` (Enum W35 | W55, class scope,
   no module constants). Both set or both None; one without the other is a configuration error.
2. Calibration factor k = standardized_scop / bin_scop(generic fit, application, group). COP is
   linear in its coefficients, so every COP the component takes from hplib is multiplied by k and
   the electrical power divided by k; thermal power is unchanged. hplib itself is not modified; the
   factor is applied in `get_cached_results_or_run_hplib_simulation` (or right after it) to COP and
   P_el, including the DHW branches, the heating-rod branch (cop <= 1) left as hplib returns it.
   The EER/cooling path is not scaled (out of scope, say so in the docstring).
3. The bin method lives in a small class in the component module or `hisim/components/` helper
   (e.g. `StandardisedSeasonalCop` with the bin table as a ClassVar tuple, the two flow-temperature
   lines and the sizing convention Pdesign = P_th_ref(A-7/W52) / 0.88 as named class constants with
   the source EN 14825 named in the docstring). It must be deterministic and cheap (26 bins, one
   hplib call each) and run once in `i_prepare_simulation`.
4. Ground source (group 2): same method with the brine source at 0 C in every bin and the same
   flow-temperature lines; the ambient term still uses the bin temperature.
5. Translator (`hisim/renovisor/translate.py`): when the generator is a heat pump and the request
   carries `scop` + `scop_application`, write both onto the hplib config (new `Targets` entries),
   mapping-report `used`; when only one of the two is present, refuse with a `heating.scop.*`
   problem code (fail hard, no guessing); `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` on a heat pump house
   stays listed as not applicable. The economics context (`hisim/renovisor/economics.py`) publishes
   the SCOP as the heat pump subject's technical attribute so subsidy conditions can read it
   (remove the "No SCOP" comment block there).
6. Capability document: field probes for the two new leaves.

Tests (targeted files only, never the full suite):
- bin_scop(Generic air/water, W55) is 3.40 +- 0.05 and W35 4.74 +- 0.05 (pins the method).
- After calibration to 3.0 at W55 the bin method over the calibrated component returns 3.0 +- 0.01.
- A one-day run with standardized_scop set has P_th identical to the uncalibrated run and P_el
  scaled by 1/k in every heating timestep.
- Translator: request with both fields -> config carries them, report `used`; request with one
  field -> exit 2 with the problem code; boiler house with the percent field unchanged.
- Economics: the heat pump subject's attributes carry the SCOP.

Depends on the spec update (the maintainer's bead) because the field names and the W35/W55 enum
must be final before the translator side is written; the component side (steps 1..4) can be built
first against the config alone if the agent wants to start early.
close_reason: Done: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibConfig gains standardized_scop_en14825_w35/_w55; StandardizedSeasonalCop rates hplib's fit by EN 14825 (Generic air/water 3.40 at W55, 4.74 at W35); ScopCalibration solves one factor per stated rating so the calibrated fit rates exactly at them, interpolated in outlet temperature between the rating lines' heat-weighted mean outlets (28.9 / 40.7 C, decision 2026-09-23; real-data check is hisim-x2mu), applied to every heating call before caching (P_th unchanged, compressor electricity / k, rod untouched, cooling untouched). The translator writes a kept heat pump's pair onto hplib; a heating_system measure removes it with the old generator. Economics publishes nothing (physics only, renovisorissues !11), superseding design step 5's attribute.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Design update from contract PR #10 (2026-09-22): the inventory states the SCOP as a pair, heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 and heatpump_scop_en14825_w55, either may be null. Adapt design step 1: config fields standardized_scop_w35 / standardized_scop_w55 (Optional[float]) instead of standardized_scop + ScopApplication. Step 2: with both given, calibrate against both bin SCOPs (e.g. a factor per rating point, interpolated linearly in flow temperature between 35 and 55 C, held constant outside); with one given, a single factor as designed. Still blocked by hisim-epc.27 for the request-schema field names.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Tracked for the other agents on GitLab: https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/iek-3/groups/urbanmodels/renovisorissues/-/work_items/8 (the SCOP field this is blocked on)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23: the request fields are final (#8, renovisorissues !9): house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35 / _w55, either may be absent; W55 <= W35 is guaranteed by the request checks; the pair places the unit at house.heating.flow_temperature_in_celsius. Only the existing pump carries them; a new pump from the heating_system measure keeps the generic fit. When this lands, remove the two not_implemented_yet entries hisim-epc.27 adds.

title: Let a caller specify battery and heat-pump sizes instead of always auto-sizing
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 5

`EnergySystemConfig` (`hisim/building_sizer_utils/interface_configs/system_config.py`) only has
`use_battery_and_ems: bool`; the battery is always auto-sized, and the heat pump is always
auto-sized from the building's heating load. RenoVisor users pick concrete sizes (battery
5/10/15 kWh, heat pump 6/8/10/12 kW) -- the translator marks these `approximated` and lets the
setup size them.

Suggested fix: add optional `battery_capacity_in_kilowatt_hours: Optional[float] = None` and
`heat_pump_thermal_power_in_kilowatt: Optional[float] = None` (None = keep auto-sizing, fully
backward compatible); in the setups, pass an explicit value through to `advanced_battery_bslib` /
`more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib` when present.

Note that under the declarative path the equivalent is a sparse `config:` override on the twin,
which the parametriser already applies -- so check whether the translator's route makes the
`EnergySystemConfig` change unnecessary before doing it.

Testing: extend the setup tests with a config carrying explicit sizes and assert the component
configs received them; keep one auto-sizing test as regression.

title: Make the heating setpoint configurable so RenoVisor's targetTempC can be mapped
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 6 (listed in the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

Building-sizer setups hard-code `building_set_heating_temperature_in_celsius = 20.0` (and 25.0
for cooling), e.g. `household_heatpump_building_sizer.py` lines ~122-124. The user-chosen
living-room setpoint (12-28 degC in the RenoVisor UI, default 21) is ignored; every simulation
heats to 20 degC. Setpoint strongly affects heating demand (rule of thumb ~6 %/K), so this is one
of the biggest fidelity gaps for "your house today" baselines.

Suggested fix: add `set_heating_temperature_in_celsius: Optional[float] = None` to
`ArcheTypeConfig`; setups use it when present, falling back to the current constants.

Related: challenges.md C15 records that the `change room temperature` measure writes two fields
-- the building set-point and the HDS controller set-point (M11).

Testing: setup test asserting the building config receives the configured setpoint; an
integration assertion that a higher setpoint yields higher annual heating demand. Translator: map
`targetTempC` to the new field and flip its report status to `used`.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP. new_room_temperature stays on the not-implemented whitelist and greyed out; every twin heats to the recorded 20 degC for the MVP.

title: Make boiler seasonal efficiency and design flow temperature configurable
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 9 (the document's own priority 2, "quick wins")

The gas/oil/pellet/wood setups use fixed component defaults, and `heat_distribution_system.py`
handles the flow temperature internally. RenoVisor's expert fields
`heating.seasonalEfficiencyPct` (e.g. an old oil boiler at 78 %) and `heating.flowTempC` are
dropped. Baseline fuel consumption for old boilers is therefore optimistic, which understates the
savings of switching away from them.

Suggested fix: an optional efficiency override wired to the boiler component configs; an optional
design flow temperature wired to the heat-distribution controller (also improves heat-pump COP
realism, item 5).

Testing: setup test that a lower efficiency raises annual fuel energy proportionally.

title: Add per-element U-value overrides for roof, wall and floor to the building config path
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 7; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C12, C13 and Q10

`BuildingConfig` has `window_u_value_in_watt_per_m2_per_kelvin` and `door_u_value_...` overrides
(and `hisim/components/building/information.py` honours a configured U-value per element through
`EnvelopeElement.configured_u_value_field`), but `ArcheTypeConfig` has no envelope fields and the
setups never set them. RenoVisor sends detailed envelope data (per-element construction /
insulation ids and expert U-value overrides); the translator can only express "how renovated is
it overall" via the TABULA refurbishment variant (.001/.002/.003), a three-step scale.

Suggested fix, incremental: (1) add optional per-element U-value overrides (roof, wall, floor,
window, door) to `ArcheTypeConfig` and pass them into `BuildingConfig` in the setups -- the
building component already supports window/door overrides, so extend it to roof/wall/floor;
(2) later, a derivation table (construction + insulation + added mm of material -> U-value) so
measures translate into concrete post-retrofit U-values.

Challenges Q10 settles the precedence: the inventory wins per element, TABULA otherwise, and the
report says which. C13 flags one thing to check while doing it: the floor's transmission factor
becomes a fixed 0.5 when a floor U-value is configured -- check that against a suspended floor
over a ventilated crawl space.

Testing: building-component test comparing heating demand with and without an override; setup
test that the override reaches `BuildingConfig`.
close_reason: Completed: the v2 translator writes facade, roof, floor, window and door U-values from the request into the Building config (hisim/renovisor/translate.py; tests/renovisor/test_translate.py::test_every_element_u_value_lands_on_the_building), merged as #778

title: Make ventilation and airtightness configurable (n50 and heat recovery)
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 8; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C15 (M3) and Q15

`hisim/components/building/` handles infiltration and ventilation internally; the setups only set
`enable_opening_windows = True`. RenoVisor's `air_sealing` measure (target n50 air-change rate)
and `ventilation` measure (MVHR with 75-92 % heat recovery) have no counterpart, so deep-retrofit
packages are under-represented (only via the TABULA variant bump).

Suggested fix: expose an infiltration rate (n50 or air changes per hour) on
`BuildingConfig`/`ArcheTypeConfig`, and add a mechanical-ventilation-with-heat-recovery option
(effective ventilation heat loss reduced by the recovery efficiency).

Challenges Q15 decided the three optional `BuildingConfig` fields (infiltration, shading, air
change / heat recovery) are not built for the MVP; `OUTSIDE_SHADING`,
`SHALLOW_AIR_TIGHTNESS_MEASURES`, `DIY_SEALING_OF_AIR_LEAKS` and `VENTILATION_SYSTEM` stay
`NoEffect` and are reported. This issue is the post-MVP work that closes them.

Testing: heating demand decreases monotonically with lower n50 and with higher heat-recovery
efficiency; the energy balance stays closed (`i_doublecheck`).

title: Make solar thermal an optional, sizeable flag rather than two dedicated setups
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 10

`household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` and
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py` are the only solar-thermal setups, so an
oil- or electric-heated house with (or adding) solar thermal cannot be simulated with solar
thermal; the translator drops it with a report note. Collector area and storage volume are also
fixed by the setup rather than configurable (`solarThermal.collectorAreaM2`, `storageLiters` are
ignored).

Suggested fix: either add solar-thermal variants for the remaining heating systems or -- cleaner
long-term -- make solar thermal an optional flag handled inside each setup, with optional
collector area / storage volume fields. Under the declarative path the natural spelling is a
variant group on the recorded twins.

Related: challenges.md F10 records that the solar-thermal files wire the collector to DHW only,
so `DHW_ONLY` is the one supported supply mode; the other two catalogue values are refusals.

Testing: marker test per new combination; assert DHW energy from the boiler decreases when solar
thermal is enabled.

title: Model electric vehicles in every building-sizer setup, not only the one with a car
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 11

`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py` is the only building-sizer setup with a car; none of
the others model vehicles. RenoVisor models all vehicles (fuel cost and CO2 of the status quo, EV
charging load interacting with PV/battery/tariff) and the translator ignores the whole `vehicles`
array. An EV can shift several MWh/a onto the household meter, so PV/battery sizing conclusions
are skewed for EV owners.

Suggested fix: add an optional `electric_vehicles` list (annual km, kWh/km) and instantiate the
existing car / car-battery components when present, following
`household_heatpump_car_building_sizer.py`.

Blocked in part by `roadmap/p3_random_findings.md` F-9: `Car.__init__` requires
`data_dict_with_car_information` computed from the occupancy instance at setup time, so `Car`
cannot be built from configuration alone and the car setup is unrecordable (EF-33). Owner
decision 2026-08-30: leave unrecorded and name it a class-conversion gap.

Testing: setup test asserting total electricity consumption grows by about km x kWh/km; check the
EMS still converges.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23 (from hisim-l07.12): before a RenoVisor request can run the car twin, generic_car.Car and advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery need a cost facts source (Irish device rows with sources plus adapter entries), and the owner has to decide whether the car is priced at all or treated as the household's own. tests/renovisor/test_twin_cost_declarations.py fails until then if the car twin is added to BaseFiles.

title: Represent an east-west PV split instead of approximating it as one east-facing array
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 12

`ArcheTypeConfig` has a single `pv_azimuth` and the setups build one PV array. RenoVisor offers
`east_west` roof orientation, common for terraced houses; the translator approximates it as a
single east-facing array (azimuth 90 degrees), which underestimates evening generation and
distorts self-consumption.

Suggested fix: allow a list of (azimuth, share) tuples -- or a simple `pv_split_east_west: bool`
-- and build two `PVSystem` instances with half the capacity each.

Related: challenges.md Q16 decided PV sizing reads roof form and orientation from new inventory

title: Decide the LCOH denominator's source so levelized_cost_of_heat stops being null on RenoVisor documents
description:
Source: ~/shared_todos/todos.md H2 (frontend, engine v20260920-1)

Observed: plan.totals.levelized_cost_of_heat_in_euro_per_kwh is null in both stage slots of the staged economics document, on every RenoVisor calculation.

Root cause: LCOH = NPV annuity / annual_heat_demand_in_kwh (calculators/aggregation.py); a missing or zero denominator omits the KPI. The denominator reaches the engine only through the declared EconomicContext (bridge _merge_context, non-negative scalars) - the simulation extract never sets it. The RenoVisor translator builds the EconomicContext BEFORE the simulation runs (run.py attaches it beside the parameters), so it cannot know the heat demand, and it states none. The engine then omits the KPI rather than dividing by an invented figure - correct per cost-spec, but the frontend wants the number.

The simulation does produce a candidate: the Building component's "Theoretical heating demand" KPI (kWh, from the TheoreticalThermalBuildingDemand channel, building.py get_kpi_entries).

Decision needed (owner):
1. Semantics: is the LCOH denominator the building-side theoretical (useful) heat demand or the generator-side delivered heat? cost-spec says "annual useful heat demand".
2. Placement: engine-side extract (bridge reads the Building KPI, declared context still overrides) benefits every run and keeps the seam promise; renovisor-side attach after the run would be two-phase and stale for re-pricing.

Done when: the denominator's source is decided, implemented, and a staged run on the mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both stage slots (or the decision is "stay null" and the frontend is told so).
close_reason: Decided with Noah 2026-09-23: the LCOH divides by the useful heat the simulation measured (Building TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand + SimpleDHWStorage ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW), extracted engine-side into economic_inputs.json and annualized with simulated_period_fraction; a declared EconomicContext.annual_heat_demand_in_kwh still wins. The mockup pair publishes a non-null LCOH in both evaluations.

title: Staged: a stage that replaces an earlier stage's purchase writes it off as new (age at plan year 0, not at its own from_year)
description:
Source: hisim-dutz/hisim-nl6j work (worktree agent-y0, feat/year-zero), 2026-09-26.

Each stage k is evaluated over the whole horizon from plan year 0, and what it charges is shifted by
from_year_k. When stage k replaces an asset an earlier stage j bought (installation_year
plan_year_zero + from_year_j, origin STAGE), resolve_replaced_asset measures the replaced asset's
age at plan year 0: max(0, year0 - (year0 + from_year_j)) = 0. The replacement actually happens at
plan year from_year_k, when the asset is from_year_k - from_year_j years old. So the sunk cost
(written-off book value, decision-neutral, reported) is the full like-for-like price, and the
anyway-cost test sees the whole service life remaining, so no anyway credit is due even when the
earlier purchase is near the end of its life. Before the year-0 anchor the same case measured
year0 - (weather_year + from_year_j), right only by accident.

The first-replacement schedule of such an asset is now unfloored (ExistingAsset.age_for_replacement),
this path was left floored on purpose. Fix idea: resolve the replaced asset's age at the charging
stage's own from_year (year0 + from_year_k) for a STAGE asset, and pin it with a hand-computed test.
close_reason: a later stage's replacement of an earlier stage's purchase writes it off at its real age (ExistingAsset.stated_age_in_years, fix/year-zero-review)

title: CI takes 32 min per push on 20 shared GitHub slots while the institute's 20 self-hosted runners sit idle
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27 (ci-usage run 36305724420, tests run 36303671417, golden-check run 36303671424, golden-year run 36305904351), requested by Noah because CI keeps getting longer.

A push to a pull request takes 32 min until every check is green, and on a busy day considerably longer. Measured on the main push of 2026-09-27 07:37 UTC:

| workflow | wall | jobs | bound by |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| tests | 32.3 min | 9 | `pytest (base)`: 31.2 min, 7,277 tests in one process |
| golden-check | 11.2 min | 24 | 22 matrix jobs, 6 to 254 s of simulation each plus ~1 min fixed overhead, queued up to 5.7 min |
| golden-yaml-check | 10.8 min | 24 | the same 22 setups again as recorded twins |
| quality | 4.9 min | 6 | prospector 4.8 min |
| the rest | <= 3.1 min | 4 | |

Three structural facts under those numbers:

1. **Every push fires 67 jobs, and the organisation is on the GitHub Free plan: 20 concurrent jobs for the whole org.** Every job runs on GitHub-hosted 4-core runners (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, runner group "GitHub Actions") at ~25% CPU. The 20 self-hosted runners the institute operates are idle: no workflow names them. On 2026-09-11/12 (5,000 jobs a day) the median wait for a golden-check runner was 15 min, the 90th percentile 36 to 40 min.
2. **The base shard grew sixfold in three weeks**: 4.8 min (2026-09-05), 12 min (2026-09-20, staged economics), 22.8 min (2026-09-26, path verification), 31 min (2026-09-27). extendedbase went from 2.4 to 11 min on 2026-09-15 with two `test_p3_parity` EMS-sizer tests at 220 s each.
3. **Inside the 30-minute base shard** about 10 min are six rebuilds of the RenoVisor capability document (~100 s each in CI), about 10 min are the 36 `test_verify.py` tests at ~18 s each, and an estimated 7 min are the stray-file guard's two `git status --untracked-files=all` calls per test (14,500 per run). The tests themselves take about 3 min.

Order of payoff: the base-shard content (no infrastructure), then the golden matrices, then xdist inside the shards, then the self-hosted runners. Together the tests workflow drops from 32 to about 7 min (bounded by two single tests, see the child issue), the golden gates from 11 to 17 min down to about 4 min, and a push from 67 jobs to about 25, which is what stops the queueing on busy days.

The `ci-usage` job summary ("holding a runner without using it", "jobs that got slower") is the instrument to watch the effect on.

title: Build the RenoVisor capability document and translation map once per test session instead of six times
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417, `pytest (base)` slowest-durations block; parent epic.

The base shard rebuilds the RenoVisor capability document six times per run, about 100 s each in CI (446 probes through validate, apply and translate):

- `tests/renovisor/test_capabilities.py`: the module-scoped `document` fixture (103 s setup), and `TestTheDocument::test_two_builds_of_one_state_are_byte_identical` builds it again (99 s).
- `tests/renovisor/test_map.py`: the module-scoped `page` fixture renders the map, which builds the document (98 s setup); `test_rendering_twice_produces_the_same_page` and `test_writing_it_somewhere_else_leaves_the_committed_one_alone` render again (99 s each).
- `tests/renovisor/test_report.py`: `TestHiSimCommit::test_the_capability_document_stays_valid_without_a_commit` builds it once more (98 s).

To do: build the document and the rendered page once per session (a session-scoped fixture in `tests/renovisor/conftest.py`, or a process-level memo on `CapabilityDocument.build()` / `TranslationMap.render()` that the determinism tests reset explicitly). The three "two builds are identical" tests then compare the shared build with one deliberate second build, not one second build each. The report test that patches the commit lookup needs the build to happen under its patch, so that one keeps its own build or patches before the session fixture is first used.

Done when: the base shard's `--durations` block shows one ~100 s capability build, the byte-identity tests still compare two independent builds, and `tests/renovisor/test_map.py` still fails when the committed page is stale. Expected saving: about 8 min of the base shard.
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Shorten the four single tests that bound the tests workflow once the shards run in parallel (220 to 328 s each)
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417 (`--durations` blocks of the utsp, extendedbase2 and extendedbase shards); parent epic.

After the shards run in parallel, four single tests bound the tests workflow:

| test | shard | call time |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `tests/test_lpg_connector_scaling_with_local_lpg.py::test_occupancy_scaling_with_local_lpg` | utsp | 328 s |
| `tests/test_hisim_main_python.py::test_initialize_from_python_with_module_config` | extendedbase2 | 297 s |
| `tests/test_p3_parity.py::test_the_table_still_spells_the_participant_targets_the_ems_sizers_actually_grow[household_electric_heating_building_sizer]` | extendedbase | 220 s |
| the same for `household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer` | extendedbase | 218 s |

The local-LPG test deliberately runs pylpg from cold to prove the local install delivers (roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md F1), so it cannot use the inputs cache; it could run a shorter simulated period or a smaller household set if the scaling assertion stays meaningful. The `test_hisim_main_python` test runs a full setup through `hisim_main`; check what it needs to prove and whether a week suffices (its sibling without optional arguments takes 144 s for the same reason). The two parity tests belong to the temporary P3 rig, which P6 deletes (hisim-b3b.22); if that is soon, leave them.

Done when: no single test in the suite takes longer than 120 s, or each one above 120 s has a comment saying why the period cannot be shorter.

title: Memoise HiSimCommit._git and ProbeSet.build(): two git subprocesses per probe and a 2 s probe-set build per verify test
description:
Source: profile of `ProbeRunner.run()` on main (90640d87) on 2026-09-27; parent epic.

Two costs recur once per probe and once per verify test:

- `hisim/renovisor/report.py` `HiSimCommit._git` runs `git -C <root> rev-parse --short HEAD` as a subprocess, and `HiSimCommit.of()` is reached twice per probe through `MappingReport.to_json`. Over 40 probes: 18.6 s with the real git call, 14.7 s with it stubbed; on the older tree the two subprocesses were 12.3 of 26.9 s. The commit does not change during a process.
- `ProbeSet.build()` takes 2.3 s and is called by every `test_verify.py` test through the `_probes` helper (36 tests), and by every `CapabilityDocument.build()`.

To do: memoise both for the life of the process (`functools.cache` on `_git`, or a class-level slot keyed on `ROOT`; a cached, frozen probe tuple for `ProbeSet.build()`). `tests/renovisor/test_report.py` patches `subprocess.run` and the environment to exercise the three lookup routes, so the memo has to be resettable (`cache_clear()` in those tests, or a fixture that clears it).

Done when: one `git rev-parse` per process in a probe run and one probe-set build per process; `test_report.py`'s commit-lookup tests still pass by resetting the memo. Expected: about 20% off every probe run and about 80 s off the verify tests.
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Share one translation artefact cache across tests/renovisor/test_verify.py (36 tests at 18 s each)
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, tests run 36303671417 (`pytest (base)` slowest-durations block); parent epic.

`tests/renovisor/test_verify.py` has 36 tests at 18 to 47 s each in CI, about 10 min of the base shard. Each test builds its own `VerificationRunner`, whose `ArtefactCache` translates the anchor and the probe's request from cold, and most tests ask for the same handful of named probes (AZIMUTH, SCOP, THICKNESS, ...).

To do: share one `ArtefactCache` (or one runner) across the module through a module-scoped fixture, so the anchor and each named probe are translated once; tests that deliberately break a probe or patch the translator keep a fresh runner. Depends on the memoised `ProbeSet.build()` and `HiSimCommit._git` (sibling issue) for the rest of the per-test cost.

Done when: the verify tests together take under 2 min in CI and every test still exercises its own verdict (a shared cache must not let one test's refusal leak into another's).
close_reason: ci/renovisor-test-speed: capability document and map built once per session, git lookup and probe set memoised, verify tests share one translation cache

title: Replace the per-test git status stray-file guard (14,500 subprocesses per base run, unsafe under xdist)
description:
Source: `tests/conftest.py` `guard_against_stray_files` (autouse, function scope); CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; parent epic.

The stray-file guard runs `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` before and after every test: 14,500 subprocesses per base run. Measured locally (Windows, warm) at 410 ms per call, so 36 trivial tests take 31 s; in CI the "others" shard shows 131 sub-second tests taking 10 s, which puts the two calls at roughly 60 ms per test, about 7 min of the base shard. It is also the one thing that makes the suite unsafe under pytest-xdist: workers' status calls would see each other's files in flight.

To do: keep the guarantee (no test leaves a file git would track) at a cheaper granularity. Options, in order of preference:
1. module scope: one status before and after each module, the failure names the module (attribution to the test is then a local re-run of that module);
2. session scope with a per-worker snapshot, so xdist workers compare against their own start state;
3. keep function scope only for tests that declare they write outside `tmp_path` (a marker), the rest run under the module guard.
Whichever is chosen, the `_result_dir` exclusion and the diagnostics in `_stray_file_diagnostics` stay. The write guard from #837 (every file a run writes lands in its result directory or the cache) already covers what the runtime writes, so the per-test check is now guarding test code, not HiSim.

Done when: fewer than 1,000 git status calls in a base run, the guard still fails a test (or its module) that drops a file into the tree, and nothing in it depends on the worker being alone in the checkout. Blocks the xdist issue.
close_reason: stray-file guard at module scope: ~418 git status calls per base run instead of ~14,700 (ci/stray-guard-module)

title: Run every pytest shard with pytest-xdist on the runner's four cores, coverage through pytest-cov
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; resource-monitor lines of tests run 36303671417 (every shard 23 to 26% of 4 cores); parent epic.

Every pytest shard is one process on a 4-core runner. With the stray-file guard reworked (blocking issue), run each shard with `pytest-xdist`: `-n 4 --dist loadfile` (a module's tests stay on one worker, which keeps module fixtures and the LPG-profile cache behaviour as today). Expected from today's durations: base from ~6 min (after the content fixes) to 2 to 3 min; extendedbase from 11.5 to about 4 min (the two 220 s `test_p3_parity` tests then run side by side); system-setups from 5 to 2 min. The tests workflow is then bounded by two single tests at 5 to 6 min (see the sibling issue on those tests), about 7 min instead of 32.

Details to settle:
- coverage: `coverage run --parallel-mode -m pytest -n 4` does not follow xdist workers; switch to `pytest-cov` (`--cov=hisim --cov-report=` plus `COVERAGE_FILE`), which starts coverage in each worker and writes the parallel data files the `combine coverage` job already merges. Add `pytest-xdist` and `pytest-cov` to `requirements.txt` so the test image carries them (the image rebuilds on that file).
- the inputs cache `hisim/inputs/cache` is written atomically already (`scripts/record_all_setups.py` runs four children against it), so concurrent workers are safe there; the results directory is per test via `ResultPathProviderSingleton` and `tmp_path`, check the 15 test files that set the provider themselves.
- memory: the shards peak at 2 to 6 GiB per process (`pytest (extendedbase)` 6 GiB); 4 workers of extendedbase would exceed the 16 GiB runner, so give that shard `-n 2` or move the heavy tests apart. The resource monitor prints the peak per job.

Done when: every shard runs with more than one worker, `combine coverage` still produces the same report, and the workflow's wall time is under 10 min on a quiet runner.
close_reason: done by #850 (2ef5d6fb): shards run with pytest-xdist and pytest-cov

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Implemented on ci/xdist (uncommitted): workers per shard in the matrix: base 4, buildingtest 4, system-setups 4, extendedbase 2, others 2; extendedbase2, postprocessingoptions and utsp 0 (one module / one test each, so --dist loadfile cannot spread them; extendedbase2 and utsp also peak at 11.3/11.5 GB cgroup). Deviation from the Done-when: those three shards stay single-process. extendedbase stays bounded by test_p3_parity.py (~540 s in one module under loadfile); splitting its two 220 s parametrised cases into their own modules (or hisim-60sv.10) is what would let -n 2 overlap them. Local base run: 6:05 sequential -> 2:09 with -n 4; coverage same file set and statements, 82 more lines hit under xdist (cold per-process caches).

title: Collapse the 48 golden matrix jobs into a few multi-pair jobs that run four pairs at once and the YAML twin alongside
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27, golden-check run 36303671424 and golden-yaml-check run 36303671382 (jobs API step timings); parent epic.

`golden-check` and `golden-yaml-check` are 22 matrix jobs each, one per week pair, plus discover and summary. Per job the simulation is 6 to 254 s (sum 1,895 s), while the fixed cost is about a minute: container init 20 to 27 s, checkout 5 to 30 s, package install, `hisim-cache` save 14 to 16 s. That is 44 runner-minutes of overhead per push, 36% of the two workflows' runner time, and the jobs wait up to 6 min for one of the 20 slots, which is what makes the workflows take 11 to 17 min for 4 min of work. Each job uses one of 4 cores.

To do:
1. `scripts/golden_check.py` already runs every pair when `--setup`/`--param` are absent; give it `--jobs N` like `record_all_setups.py` (subprocess per pair, results collected into the one `ComparisonReport`) so one job runs several pairs at once.
2. `scripts/golden_matrix.py`: emit shards instead of pairs (`--shards 4` balances the pairs by their last measured duration or by a weight in `golden_config.json`), each matrix cell a list of pairs.
3. Run the recorded YAML twin (`--mode yaml`) in the same job right after the Python setup: same container, same inputs cache, the two workflows become one with 4 to 5 jobs. Keep the workflow name `golden-check` or update `golden-year.yml`'s `workflow_run.workflows` list and `scripts/ci_prereqs_done.sh`, which name the prerequisites.
4. Memory sets the parallelism: week pairs peak at 1.2 GiB (four per runner), full-year pairs at 6 GiB (two per runner), so `golden-year` goes from 8 jobs to 4 with the same wall time, and `golden-update.yml` follows the same shape.
5. `hisim-cache` scope becomes the shard, so a pair that moves between shards recomputes its LPG profiles once; acceptable.

Done when: a push fires about 8 golden jobs instead of 48, the week tier finishes in under 5 min on a quiet runner, a diverging pair still fails the summary and still uploads its deviation report, and the golden-year gate still fires.
close_reason: done by #848 (70fa71c8): golden gates run their pairs in a few shards

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Implemented uncommitted in worktree agent-ci6 (branch ci/golden-shards): golden_check/golden_update --pairs/--jobs (child process per pair), golden_matrix --shards (lane-balanced by measured 'seconds' in golden_config.json), golden-yaml-check folded into golden-check (4 week shards, python then yaml), golden-year 4x2, golden-update sharded. Needs a real CI run to confirm wall time and memory.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decisions applied (uncommitted, agent-ci6): golden-check shards run Python and YAML twins in one pool (golden_check.py --mode both, golden_matrix.py --with-yaml), est. 237-254 s simulation per week shard; YAML twins gate golden-year (stated in golden-check/golden-year headers and ci-monitoring.md).

title: Publish the labels, specs and Docker availability of the 20 self-hosted runners (needs org admin)
Run the tests shards, the golden matrices and the freshness gate on the self-hosted runners
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; Noah confirmed the institute's 20 self-hosted runners are idle; parent epic.

Once the runner labels and specs are known (blocking issue), point the heavy workflows at the fleet: the `tests` shards, the golden matrices and `energy-system-freshness`, leaving the small jobs (`quality`, `docs-build`, `worked-examples`, the golden-year gate) wherever they are cheapest. Self-hosted runners are not counted against the plan's 20 concurrent jobs, so this removes the queueing on busy days outright, and machines with more than 4 cores allow a higher xdist worker count.

Things to carry over:
- `container:` jobs need Docker on the runner; the `git config --global --add safe.directory` step stays.
- `actions/cache` works on self-hosted runners but stores in GitHub's cache (10 GB per repo); if the fleet shares a disk, the `hisim-cache` action could restore from it instead.
- `.github/actions/resource-monitor` reads cgroup v2 `memory.peak` and `cpu.stat`; check that it still reports on the fleet (the `note` line says when it could not), and `RegressionRules` in `scripts/ci_usage_report.py` assumes 16 GB for the "near the limit" flag, which must become per-runner.
- a self-hosted runner keeps state between jobs: results directories and the inputs cache under the workspace persist, so a job must not depend on a clean checkout beyond what `actions/checkout` guarantees (the freshness gate records into a throwaway directory already).
- `golden-year.yml`'s fork guard already keeps fork pull requests off the token-carrying job; a self-hosted runner must never run a fork's code, so the fleet's runner group should be restricted to non-fork events, or the heavy workflows keep the same guard.

Done when: the heavy jobs show the fleet's runner name in the jobs API, the queue time in the ci-usage report drops to seconds on a busy day, and the resource monitor still prints a peak-memory line for them.

title: Path filters so documentation-only pull requests skip the simulation gates
description:
Source: CI wall-time analysis of 2026-09-27; parent epic.

Every push runs the simulation gates even when it touches nothing they can see. Add `paths-ignore` to `tests.yml`, `golden-check.yml`, `golden-yaml-check.yml` and `energy-system-freshness.yml` for `docs/**`, `roadmap/**`, `**/*.md`, `.github/ci-monitoring.md` and the beads file, and `paths` to `docs-build.yml` so it runs on `docs/**`, `hisim/**` and `requirements.txt` (its header explains why a change under `hisim/` can break the build). Mind the branch protection: a required check that does not run because of a path filter blocks the merge, so either the required checks list changes with it or each filtered workflow keeps a trivial job that reports success (GitHub's documented pattern).

Done when: a documentation-only pull request fires under 10 jobs and can still be merged.

title: Model a range cooker (house.heating.cooking_range)
description:

title: Building takes the largest b_Transmission of an element's sub-elements, so walls to unheated spaces count as outside walls
description: information.py _element_u_value_and_adjustment_factor area-weights the TABULA sub-elements' U-values but takes max(b_Transmission_*) as the element's adjustment factor. 42 wall sub-elements of the generic rows (001-003) have 0<b<1 with area>0 (walls to unheated spaces); they are counted with b=1, overstating their heat loss. Fix: conductance = sum_i U_i*A_i*b_i per sub-element (or an area-weighted U*b), which changes Building results for those rows (goldens re-blessed with owner approval). Found 2026-09-26 while explaining the adjustment factor for the RenoVisor retrofit_status work (#838). Owner: bead only, decide later.

title: Economics: an element of a refurbished TABULA variant without installation_year is dated to construction_year
description: Since calculation-request !24 a request can state retrofit_status usual_refurb/advanced_refurb without describing the elements. The economics then dates every element without installation_year to the building's construction_year, so a facade insulated two years ago counts as 50 years old: its like-for-like replacement comes early and its sunk-cost credit is wrong. Decide a rule (e.g. a stated retrofit year, or no replacement/credit for variant-defaulted elements) and bring it to the economics spec.
close_reason: undated envelope elements (incl. refurbished TABULA variants) take the mid-life default, reported approximated (feat/reference-fabric)

This answers an element of a refurbished TABULA variant without installation_year too (the variant says renewed, not when). Implemented uncommitted in worktree agent-fab.

title: Re-vendor measures.yaml after contract PR #10: material options, three new ones, the room-temperature rename
description:
Source: review of renovisor-api-contract PR #10 (`new-yamls`, commits c5d3e5f and b51a4e1, merged
2026-09-22 as ffe1304). HiSim pins `measures.yaml` and `openapi.yaml` at 5181aa5 (2026-09-17).

What changed upstream that HiSim's frozen catalogue (`hisim/renovisor/request.py` CatalogueTable)
and the translator have to follow:

1. **`material` options carry no `values` any more.** The option is declared (`name`,
   `access_level`) and its values are generated from the `materials.yaml` rows whose `measures` key
   names the measure; the values are the rows' `asp_id`s. HiSim reads the material as an object
   (`asp_id` + properties) and checks only the conductivity, so validation is unaffected, but the
   frozen table's ENUM lists ("EPS", "XPS", "EPS Foam", ...) no longer mirror the file.
2. **Three measures gained a `material` option:** `cavity_wall_insulation`,
   `basement_internal_insulation`, `top_floor_ceiling_insulation`. These are exactly the three
   `FixedMaterials.BY_MEASURE` stands in for (`hisim/renovisor/constants.py`), so the fixed table
   and its `approximated` notes go: a request names the material like for every other layer. The
   table's two ids are stale anyway (`eps_beads_cavity` -> `eps_beads`,
   `stone_wool_flexible_insulation_blankets` -> `stone_wool`).
3. **`change_room_temperature.new_room_temperature` is now `new_room_temperature_in_celsius`**
   (the unit-suffix fix of C1 item 4). Touches `apply.py`, the capability range table in
   `capabilities.py`, the frozen table, tests and the translation map.
4. **`openapi.yaml` was split:** `HomeInventoryInput` moved to a new `homeinventory.yaml`, referenced
   relatively. The vendored `openapi.yaml` is non-authoritative; decide whether to vendor both files
   side by side (they are meant to ship together) or drop the non-authoritative copy.
5. **The `building_components` vocabulary is gone from `materials.yaml`.** HiSim's `placement`
   values (`external_wall_external`, `basement_ceiling`, ...) were that vocabulary; they keep working
   as HiSim's own names (economics `EnvelopeAssets.BY_PLACEMENT`, subsidy conditions), but no
   upstream list anchors them now. Say so where they are defined.

Also note: `calculation-request.md` §3 (table at lines 345-356, the material column) and §12
still describe the old option values and `measure_material_values`; that is the contract
owner's text, reported, not edited here.

Done when: `python -m hisim.renovisor.contract.refresh` has re-vendored `measures.yaml` (and the
openapi decision is taken), the frozen table equals it, `FixedMaterials` is gone, the option rename
is followed everywhere, capabilities and the translation map are regenerated, and
tests/renovisor pass.
close_reason: Done: measures.yaml and openapi.yaml re-vendored at contract ffe1304, homeinventory.yaml vendored beside openapi.yaml (non-authoritative). Frozen catalogue follows (ValueType.MATERIAL for the generated material options; three new ones; new_room_temperature_in_celsius); T-CAT reads an absent value_type as MATERIAL on the material option only. FixedMaterials removed: the three measures require the request's material and move approximated -> supported (tally 18/4/10). Translation map regenerated. Contract-side leftovers in /home/cmf/contract-pr10-review.patch. The mockup was deliberately not re-vendored (that is PR #795's).

title: Report an increasing/decreasing monotone declaration that is flat on every base, so a vacuous contract is visible
description:
Found in the review of PR #899 (2026-10-08).

Evidence: heating/gas_condensing_boiler's monotone entry `heating_threshold_in_celsius` -> `Total Gas consumption (energy)` of Boiler, direction increasing, is flat on the 1 January test day. Every heating limit of the range 10-22 °C lies above the day's mean outside temperature, so each base gives one value at all four sweep points (measured 128.8, 92.6 and 184.9 kWh from the bases s000, s001 and s002). hisim/energy_system/assemblies/testing/checks.py (`check_monotone`, `offending_pair`) accepts equal steps for increasing and decreasing, so the entry passes while checking nothing. D24 calls monotone "the cheap test that catches wrong-sign physics"; a sweep that never moves cannot catch it.

PR #899 added a moving sweep to the gas boiler (`power_in_watt` -> `Standby heat loss of Hot water storage` of Buffer: 0.2, 1.3, 2.0, 2.6 kWh), so that contract is no longer vacuous, but the harness still does not report a flat declaration. #900's four boilers (oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen) copy the same flat threshold entry.

To decide: fail or warn, and where the aggregation lives (each base's sweep is its own pytest test today, so "flat on every base" needs the results of all of one declaration's sweeps). A sweep flat on one base stays allowed, since a KPI may saturate there.

Done when: an increasing or decreasing declaration whose KPI is equal at every point on every base is reported with its assembly, parameter and KPI.

title: Verify the levelized cost of heat against literature values
description: Source: owner request 2026-09-24. The levelized cost of heat (result.json levelized_cost_of_heat, since #812 / hisim-4p86 divided by the useful heat the run measured: Building.TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand plus SimpleDHWStorage.ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW) has not been checked against published values. Run representative twins (gas boiler, air/water heat pump, oil, biomass; a detached SFH, e.g. the IE mockup house and a DE archetype) and compare the LCOH in euro per kWh of useful heat with literature ranges for the same country and year basis (e.g. SEAI or Fraunhofer ISE / BDEW heating cost comparisons, the Levelised Cost of Heat studies of the EU heating-and-cooling strategy). Record the sources, the assumptions each uses (lifetime, discount rate, energy prices, whether subsidies and the anyway share are in), and HiSim's numbers beside them; explain every difference outside the ranges or open a bead for the cause. title: Mid-year simulation windows: start_date is ignored by every profile
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md

Mid-year simulation windows are January in disguise. Every profile-driven component indexes its
year-long profile from timestep 0 as if that were 1 January, whatever `start_date` says: weather
(all six data sources), PV, building solar gains, LPG occupancy, cars, smart devices, the CSV
loader, and the heating-season gates of the heat-pump and CHP controllers. Measured: a July week
in Aachen yields 37 kWh of PV where the true July offset yields 426 kWh (11.5x), written to disk
under a July-stamped index. The parity rig's July window is fenced pending this epic.

This epic collects the PR plan (PR1..PR8+), the window contract, the cache epoch, the split
oracle and the independent repairs the analyses surfaced.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10, re-verified on the hydronic stack (simulator-warm-start, #914) while benchmarking part load: household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer at 900 s from 2021-06-01 to 2021-06-08 gets January's weather (outside temperature mean 1.3 °C, GHI 16 W/m2), 10.8 W mean irradiance on the collector and 0 kWh of collector heat; the same week inside a full-year run gets 1051 W and 19.0 kWh. The collector's own sun position follows start_date, so it combines a June sun with January irradiance (hisim-9g2.7). No new bead: this epic and its PR plan cover it. Part-load and solar benchmarks therefore run full years from 1 January.

title: Warn when the simulation year does not match the weather file's data year
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 13

`hisim/components/weather.py`'s `LocationEnum` carries NSRDB 2019 files for IE/GB/... and DWD/TRY
files for German locations; setups default to `year=2021`. The weather file's year and the
`SimulationParameters` year are independent, so simulating year X with weather of year Y silently
misaligns weekdays and (for leap years) day counts. The RenoVisor translator hard-codes 2019 for
this reason, but nothing in HiSim checks or documents the constraint.

Suggested fix: `Weather.i_prepare_simulation` should log a warning (or raise, behind a flag) when
the requested simulation year does not match the data year of the selected weather file; expose
the data year on `LocationEnum` entries instead of parsing it from filenames.

This sits next to the mid-year window epic: the same "which calendar does this profile speak"
question, from the year side rather than the offset side. The epic's leap-year refusal (PR2) is
the decidable half.

Testing: unit test that a mismatched year triggers the warning; no behaviour change otherwise.
close_reason: PR A+B of the #57 step 2 epic (feat/weather-year-ab)

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Absorbed by hisim-wps1.2 (PR B of the #57 step 2 epic, cmf 2026-09-27): INFO log + record note, not a WARNING; close with it.

title: Settle the contradictory initial-state defaults for storages, the EV and hydrogen
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "Initial states (storages, thermal mass, batteries)" and
"Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses" (out of scope there, trigger: when the
season-aware storage seed lands)

Measured contradictions recorded by the analyses: the buffer storage starts at a hard-coded
35 degC while its dataclass default is 25 degC; the EV state of charge is 0 in one place and 0.5
in another; the hydrogen storage is 80 % full in one package and empty in the other -- arbitrary
twice over. DHW storage at 60 degC is season-neutral and correct; battery SOC 0 settles in a PV
day; about 25 controllers start "off" with their minimum idle time blocking the first 15-60
minutes, which is a season-neutral start artefact.

The epic's decision: keep the defaults and document the measured per-component transient, plus
exactly one season-aware change -- the buffer / space-heating storage seeds from the
heating-season gate, so outside the season it starts at ambient 20 degC instead of 35 degC (a
buffer nobody has charged sits at room temperature, the one derivation defensible in a sentence).
Warm-up prefixes are rejected on the measured evidence.

Done when: each component's initial value has one definition, the contradictions are gone, and
the season-aware buffer seed lands with its goldens.

title: PR1: one window contract, YEARLYFORECAST renames and the dead smart device deleted
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR1, "The window contract (one chokepoint)"
and "Independent repairs surfaced by the analyses"

First PR of the mid-year epic: establish the single window chokepoint, rename the
`YEARLYFORECAST`-shaped names to window names, fix the plot labels, and delete the dead
`generic_smart_device` (zero references, raises `KeyError` on first call -- deleting it also
retires the independently broken `convert_lpg_timestep_to_utc` and the test that pins its wrong
output).

Blast-radius rule for the whole epic: PR2 and PR4+5 must not move a single January golden (offset
0 on 1 January is each PR's own cheapest proof).

Done when: there is exactly one place that decides a run's window, and the renames and deletion
are in with no golden movement.

title: PR2: an offset primitive the weather adopts, plus the leap refusal and the four anchors
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR2, "The design: B' -- the profile owner
resolves one offset against its own frame", "Caches: the epoch" and "Independent repairs"

The offset primitive plus the weather adopting it; the leap-year refusal (the offset lookup is
where "this source cannot serve this date" is decidable); the DWD_15MIN reader, which sizes its
index from the run's duration instead of the file and is the one reader that cannot be sliced
until anchored; deleting the dead building solar-gain cache (delete, do not fix the `hasattr`
typo -- repairing it would serve stale entries past every check and add a sixth window-sensitive
cache); the four unit anchors; and building the oracle harness. Bumps the cache epoch.

The four unit anchors, in `tests/`: first-timestep identity against the source's own labels; the
DST phase pins (260 550 / 260 610 / 260 640 and a December mirror); each weather reader's
`index[0]` pinned (the six sources use three different anchors -- Berlin 00:30, Berlin 00:00
after the padding row `Weather.interpolate` prepends, and UTC 00:00, which is exactly why
"resolve against the delivered frame" is the rule); and the cold-then-warm cache equality
assertion.

The harness is `scripts/midyear_oracle.py`, modelled on the parity rig (per-run empty cache
directory, one process, one printed verdict table, a tolerance flag that shouts when nonzero),
reusing `ResultComparison` verbatim -- its index check refuses a misaligned slice for free.

Done when: PR2 moves no January golden and the oracle runs.

title: PR3: rewrite convert_lpg_data_to_utc as localize, convert, slice
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR3

`convert_lpg_data_to_utc` is rewritten as localize -> convert -> slice. This changes January
numbers too: the current code starts every window at source row 60 and fabricates the final hour.
It is therefore the deliberate January re-bless of the epic and ships alone, so the golden diff
has exactly one cause. Bumps the cache epoch.

Depends on PR2 (the offset primitive).

Done when: the conversion is date-correct, the January goldens are re-blessed in one commit whose
message names this as the single cause, and nothing else is in the PR.

title: PR4+5: the LPG connector owns occupancy and cars in all three modes, gates go day-of-year
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR4+5 -- MUST SHIP TOGETHER

The LPG connector owns the window offset for occupancy and for the cars, in all three data
acquisition modes, and the seasonal gates (the heat-pump and CHP controllers' heating-season
checks) go day-of-year. These must ship together, or a July window heats the house. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR3.

Blast-radius rule: must not move a single January golden -- offset 0 on 1 January is the PR's own
cheapest proof.

title: PR6: the solar thermal collector consumes the weather's window instead of its own sun
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR6 and "Independent repairs surfaced by
the analyses"

The solar-thermal collector drops its naive-UTC duplicate sun position and consumes the weather's
published window. This is one of the two places that honour the date today, which is what makes a
mid-year run incoherent rather than correct -- the collector sees a genuine July sun (apparent
zenith 27.7 degrees) wired to January irradiance. Three solar-thermal goldens move. Bumps the
cache epoch.

Depends on PR2.

Done when: there is one sun position per run, and the three goldens are re-blessed.

title: PR7: lift the July fence in its five sites and bless the first true July goldens
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR7; the fence is recorded in
`scripts/p3_parity_matrix.py` and R11.5 as amended 2026-09-06

Lift the fence in its five sites -- the parity workflow's hand-kept window options among them,
which nothing derives from the code -- invert the fence test into "July differs from January",
add the `july_week` parameter set to `scripts/golden_config.json` and bless the first true July
references.

This is what unfences the parity rig's July window, which P6 of the declarative plan needs to
confirm the stack green "over every runnable window".

Depends on PR4+5 and PR6.

title: PR8+: every stateful component expresses its complete state as startup configuration
description:
Source: roadmap/midyear_start_epic.md, "The PR plan" PR8+ and "Validation: the split oracle"

A series, one component per PR. Run the full year once, read every stateful component's state at
the window start (the battery's SOC on 1 July, the storage temperatures, the thermal-mass
temperature, the controllers' modes and timers), hand those to the window run as startup values,
and the whole comparison becomes an exact gate: with its complete mid-cycle state handed over,
even a bang-bang controller continues on the very limit cycle the year run was on, so the one
column no warm-up could ever buy back (`WaterMassFlowHDS`, permanently 16.7 % out) joins the gate
too.

What it costs is completeness -- a partially seeded component just re-imports its transient --
and not every component can express its state as configuration today (controller idle timers, the
meters' cumulative sums, the EMS's internals are not config fields). So the seeded tier grows
component by component: a column moves from the oracle's report tier to the exact gate the moment
its component's full state is expressible as startup configuration. The cumulative meter columns
move immediately, gated on first differences instead of levels.

This is checkpoint handover at the configuration level, which is why it shares its prerequisites
with the two `i_save_state` repairs (the EMS reference restore and the HDS self-assignment).

The series moves no golden at all: startup values default to today's constants, and each PR's
proof is its component's columns going exactly to zero in the seeded oracle.

Depends on PR7.

title: Publish exclusive lower/upper bounds in the capability document once the shared schema declares them
description: Source: PR #807 review, owner decisions 2026-09-24. The capability document now publishes the request schema's own numeric bounds (read from calculation-request.schema.json at build time); a bound the schema states as exclusiveMinimum (floor and living area > 0, roof U-value > 0, SCOP > 1, solar thermal area > 0) is omitted for now, because the strict measure-capabilities.openapi.yaml (ImplementedField) knows only minimum/maximum. A renovisorissues MR adds exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum to ImplementedField. Once it is merged and the RenoVisor stack has landed: re-vendor (python -m hisim.renovisor.contract.refresh <contract> --specs <clone>) and publish exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum where the request schema declares them; extend the schema-vs-published test.
close_reason: Re-vendored measure-capabilities.openapi.yaml 0.4.0 (cc54813, !18). RequestSchemaBounds publishes every bound under the schema's own keyword (minimum/maximum/exclusiveMinimum/exclusiveMaximum); the document validates against the strict schema. test_capabilities: schema-vs-published test covers all four keywords, a test pins the exclusive ones (floor area, roof U, SCOP, collector area, pv/battery power). HiSim neither publishes nor checks the schema's version string. 0.4.0 added the exclusive keys to ImplementedField only, so options with an exclusive schema bound still publish none.

title: Rust conversion ideas
Profile a representative run and publish the time breakdown
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Step 0 -- "Measure before
changing anything"

Two or three setups (one minutely full year, one 15-minute short run, one with MPC), broken into:
timestep loop, third-party library calls (pvlib/hplib/bslib/windpowerlib), input parsing,
postprocessing, external waiting (UTSP/LPG). This is a day of work and it is the gate on every
performance argument in the companion feasibility document -- including whether Tier 1 should be
reordered around whatever actually dominates.

Payoff now: it will almost certainly find optimizable Python nobody has looked at.
Payoff for a port: it converts "10-50x on the loop" into an Amdahl ceiling for the whole run.

title: Stop the byte surgery that appends to component_connections.json
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2

`component.py:447` seeks to `st_size - 1` and overwrites the closing bracket of
`component_connections.json` to append an entry. Buffer the connections and write the file once
when wiring completes.

Payoff now: an interrupted run stops leaving a syntactically broken JSON file behind.

title: Make the convergence criterion explicit, configurable and unit-aware
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 2; and
roadmap/rust_ideas/rust_simulator_spec.md option O8, "Per-output tolerance vector"

`component.py:194` compares every output against a hardcoded absolute 1e-4 -- watts, joules,
kelvin, euros and dimensionless ratios on one scale -- and the forced-convergence thresholds
(above 10 iterations forced, above 100 raises, `simulator.py:266-270`) are hardcoded next to it.
At minimum make all three configurable and document the choice; ideally scale per unit.

O8 states the targeted form: replace the single absolute 1e-4 with a per-output (or per-unit)
tolerance supplied at construction. It is the cheap fix for the real defect measurement M4 looks
for -- an absolute threshold applied across incommensurable units, where a counter at 1e9 needs
1e-13 relative and would fail on every iteration, silently forcing the 10-iteration cutoff on
every timestep.

Caution from O8: it changes iteration counts and therefore results. Needs a one-time golden
re-bless and a stated policy, per the parity-policy decision.

Payoff now: the tolerance becomes a modelling decision that can be justified, and the "runs
converge but nobody knows how tightly" question gets an answer.

Gated on measurement M4.

title: Give i_save_state and i_restore_state explicit state structs instead of deepcopy
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Five component modules `deepcopy` themselves or their state each iteration. An explicit small
state object is faster in Python and removes the "which attributes are state?" ambiguity.

Payoff now: measurable -- this runs once per component per convergence iteration per timestep.

Related: the two live `i_save_state` defects (the EMS restoring a reference and the
heat-distribution controller self-assigning) are exactly the ambiguity this removes, and the
mid-year epic names both as prerequisites for checkpoint handover.

title: Inject the cache backend, the clock and the RNG instead of monkeypatching them in tests
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

22 test files use `monkeypatch`, 8 of them around `utils.get_cache_file`; without that patching,
runs are order-dependent through the shared on-disk cache, and `conftest.py` scrubs
`HISIM_CACHE_*` around every test. Turn these into constructor parameters.

Payoff now: order-independent tests, less autouse machinery, and the stale-cache class of false
failures loses its main route in.

This also matches the AGENTS.md guideline that monkeypatching is to be avoided in shared
fixtures, and the seeded-RNG precedent of `RandomNumbers`, whose seed became a configuration
field in P3 so a system description can say what a run will do.

title: Write an owned, versioned cache-key serializer with a stable field order
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

The cache key is `sha256(dataclasses_json output + sim-params string)`, so field order, float repr
and enum spelling from a third-party library are load-bearing for about 319 MB of committed cache
and every cross-machine share. Write an owned key serializer with a stable field order, a schema
version in the key, and a test that pins the exact string for a fixture config.

Payoff now: upgrading `dataclasses_json` or `pyhumps` stops silently invalidating every cache
entry in the fleet.

Related: the producer-fingerprint keys of the cache service solve the other half (what code
produced the content); this one is about what identifies the request.

title: Audit the sixty exact float comparisons in component control flow
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

Roughly 60 `== 0`-style comparisons sit in component control paths
(`water_mass_flow_rate == 0`, `control_signal == 0.0`, `delta_t == 0` patched to `1e-8`).
Replace with documented epsilons and re-bless the goldens once.

Do this in Python, where re-blessing is cheap and reviewable, rather than discovering it during a
port where the change is indistinguishable from a translation bug.

title: Move module_selection.py out of hisim/inputs and stop reading data at import time
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`hisim/inputs/photovoltaic/module_selection.py` is Python inside `hisim/inputs/`, and it reads PV
module databases at import. Relocate to `hisim/components/` and make the read lazy.

Payoff now: import time, and the data directory becomes purely data.

title: Prune requirements.txt of the three declared but unimported packages
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3

`seaborn`, `plotly` and `html2image` are declared but imported nowhere under `hisim/`, `tests/`,
`tools/`, `scripts/` or `system_setups/`; there are commented-out pins (`pvlib`,
`windpowerlib`, `wetterdienst`) and a migration TODO.

An accurate dependency list is a prerequisite for reasoning about the domain-library gap at all,
and the commented-out pvlib pin is named separately in the Tier 1 adapter item as a risk of its
own.

Note that `pyhumps` already left with the scenario-JSON writer (P4 F-9), so the list has drifted
since the survey.

title: Converge on the energy-system YAML as the only way to describe a system
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Converge on one
front end"

At the time of the survey there were three ways to describe a system: 23 setup functions in
`system_setups/*.py`, 22 `.scenario.json` twins and 28 `.energy_system.yaml` files, with
byte-identity freshness gates keeping the generated ones in sync. Per the declarative-energy-
