comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: not part of the MVP; the MVP ships with the data marked as AI draft / to be reviewed. Labelled human: a person does this, implementation agents skip it.

title: Decide the uncertainty-band curation and whether bands reach service lives and emissions
description:
Source: cost_spec.md section 11, Phase 1 uncertainty questions Q23, Q24, Q25, Q26;
cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions" Q25 (bands beyond money -- service lives and emission
factors stay exact in v1)

Q23 -- sources and curation of the min/max bands: who defines the ranges per component type and
energy carrier, and are they maintained as explicit values (proposal, seeded from the spread of
the already-cited sources) or as symmetric +/- x % rules? Entries without a reviewed band stay
degenerate (min = best_estimate = max) rather than getting an invented one.

Q24 -- is the envelope semantics (full correlation toward cheap/expensive, section 3.9)
sufficient for the intended studies, or do some need statistical quantiles? Quantiles would
require distributions plus sampling via the scenario layer -- currently a non-goal.

Q25 -- extending bands beyond money: service lives and emission factors carry at least as much
uncertainty as prices. Proposal (taken provisionally in code): keep them exact in v1, because a
lifetime band changes the replacement structure of the timeline, not just amounts. Revisit after
phase 3.

Q26 -- KPI surface for bands: are the optional `value_min`/`value_max` fields on `KpiEntry`
(section 7.3) enough for the webtool and the RenoVisor frontend, or do bounds need to be separate
KPI entries for the existing plotting pipeline?

Related: `UncertainValue.__sub__` semantics changed while building the comparison view
(cost_module_issues.md 26) -- the delta band is the envelope of the three slot deltas, so
"minimum" reads "best-case delta", not "LOW-world delta".

title: Decide the remaining phase 3b to 5 cost-spec questions on tariffs, allocation and scenarios
description:
Source: cost_spec.md section 11, the questions not covered by a provisional default in
cost_module_issues.md

Q9 (Phase 4) -- income data in RenoVisor requests, needed for income-dependent schemes: privacy
handling. Accept an income band enum rather than an amount?

Q11 (Phase 5) -- which allocation rulesets in v1 beyond `DE_2024`? AT has no modernization-levy
analogue (much simpler ruleset); is a generic `EU_SIMPLE` ruleset -- landlord pays
capex/maintenance, tenant pays energy -- the right fallback for other countries? Ireland now has
data and no ruleset.

Q13 (Phase 5) -- tenant-electricity models (Mieterstrom) for PV in rented buildings: v1 assigns
feed-in revenue to the landlord. Is that acceptable for the intended studies?

Q16 (Phase 3b) -- spot price data: which series ship in the cost database (EPEX day-ahead DE/AT
per simulation year)? Check redistribution licensing. The provisional answer taken in code: no
licensed EPEX data is shipped; a synthetic reference profile generator is provided for tests plus
a documented CSV loader for user-supplied series.

Q20 (Phase 3c) -- default shipped scenario set: which axes and levels constitute the standard
low/central/high bundle (interest, per-carrier escalations, CO2 path), and from which sources?
This is the public face of every study.

Q22 (Phase 3c) -- should the RenoVisor response include the full scenario cube or only the
robustness summary plus tornado data? Proposal: summary by default, full cube behind a request
flag, because of payload size.

Q29 (Phase 1 provenance) -- does the RenoVisor/webtool response need embedded provenance for end
users, or is the stored ledger plus the `explain` CLI sufficient? Proposal: sufficient.

title: Decide what happens to scenario_cube.csv now that scenario_evaluation is gone
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 22; cross-read with roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-25

cost_module_issues.md 22 says `scenario_cube.csv` is written in the long format the spec
prescribes so the existing `scenario_evaluation` aggregation can consume it, but no ingestion
code was added on the `scenario_evaluation` side -- "that module aggregates across runs and should
adopt the cube in its own PR".

needs-triage: that module no longer exists. P4 F-25 records that
`hisim/postprocessing/scenario_evaluation/` was moved to `obsolete/` in #541 (2026-08-10) and
left the repository entirely with the rest of that tree in #590. So the cube's intended consumer
is gone and the note in cost_module_issues.md is stale.

Decide: give the cube a consumer, keep it as an export for outside tooling, or retire it with the
pyam export question (F-25).

title: Tighten the deliberately generous plausibility thresholds as experience accumulates
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 26 (report layer, 2026-07-07)

Plausibility thresholds live in `cost_database/plausibility_checks.json` and are deliberately
generous -- they catch unit mix-ups, not modelling disagreements. The source says to tighten them
as experience accumulates.

Done when: the thresholds have been revisited against the runs since 2026-07-07 and either
tightened or confirmed with a dated note.

title: Refactor the economics package for size and maintainability, without losing functionality
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Refactor the economics package so it is smaller and easier to change, without losing any
functionality. Performance is not a goal (the engine runs in milliseconds). Rough target:
code ~19.6k -> 12-13k lines, docstrings ~19k -> 9k, package ~47k -> 22-25k lines.

Phases (children of this epic):
- A, no behaviour change: tests/goldens/cost_summary.md and lifecycle_report.html must stay
  byte-identical, and the invariant tests stay green.
- B, declarative formats: serialization and the staged parameter reader.
- D, deeper structure: the timeline-build calculators, retiring the adapter, a time-aware
  evaluator in place of the staged splice.

Phase C (one chart backend instead of both the SVG and matplotlib layers) is deliberately not
filed yet; it waits for the owner's decision on the PNG set.

The safety net for every child is test_economics_report_goldens.py plus the
test_economics_invariants*.py files. Run targeted test files only, not the full suite.

title: A: Trim the economics docstrings to plain what/example/why/Args form and drop history and review codes
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase A, no behaviour change. Do this first: it touches every file, and the other A items would
conflict with it.

hisim/economics has 1,263 docstrings, median 12 lines; 259 are 20 lines or longer. 136 tell
history ("used to", "review finding 14", "owner decision", "PR #...", "before W4.3"), and the
code carries about 700 internal review codes (W4.3, Q26 F4, R7, V9, D27). That is the essayistic
style the house docstring rule excludes.

Trim each docstring to: what it is -> an example where useful -> a short why -> Args/Returns/Raises.
Keep the § references to cost_spec.md. Drop history, review codes and restated rationale (git and
beads keep them). Also shorten the module docstrings (the package README keeps the tour).

Done when: no docstring recounts history, internal review codes are gone, pure comment/docstring

title: D: Write the design note for a time-aware evaluator that prices staged plans without splicing
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document). Baseline: 46.8k lines in hisim/economics (19.6k code, 19.3k docstrings, 1.8k comments), 42k lines of tests.

Phase D, deeper structure. Design note first; the implementation is a separate issue.

StagedEvaluator (staged.py, a 1,413-line class) prices a staged plan by evaluating every stage
over the whole horizon and then splicing the timelines. The splice has to recompute engine
mechanisms after the fact: re-dated replacements, residual values from the plan's last
installation (_residual_entries), the re-levelized replacement reserve
(_staged_reserve_flows), the CO2 splice (_splice_co2) and an equivalent annual heat demand
(_equivalent_annual_heat), and it hand-builds a LifecycleCostResult (_aggregate).

Alternative: make the core evaluator time-aware. Each subject carries its install year; billing
determinants carry the years in which they are active; a normal run is a one-stage plan. The
residual, reserve, CO2 and heat-cost mechanics then run once, in the engine.

Write a design note (roadmap/economics/) that covers: the input model (per-subject install year,
per-stage billing and active years, register ageing), subsidies per stage year and the price basis
per stage, what changes in EvaluationInputs/economic_inputs.json, which E-spec §1.3 invariants
carry over (one-stage plan == plain evaluation, entry for entry), and a migration path that keeps
tests/economics/test_staged*.py and tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py as the oracle.
Answers the owner question on replacing the splice.

description:

Owner decision: replace the staged splice with a time-aware evaluator?

staged.py prices a plan by splicing per-stage evaluations and recomputing residuals, reserve, CO2
and heat demand after the fact. A time-aware core evaluator (install year per subject, billing
active per year range) would do this once, in the engine, and delete most of the splice
machinery, but it changes EvaluationInputs and economic_inputs.json and is the riskiest item of
the refactor. The design-note issue lays out the details; this question records the go/no-go.

title: D: Remove the renovisor imports from hisim.economics so the engine no longer depends on the translator above it
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document).

Layering inversion: hisim.economics is a lower layer than hisim.renovisor (the translator calls
the engine), but economics imports renovisor. The only imports of hisim.renovisor outside
hisim/renovisor are:
- hisim/economics/__main__.py:161-163: MainSubjectError, MainSubjects, MeasureSubjects
  (renovisor/economics.py), MappingReport (renovisor/report.py) and CatalogueTable
  (renovisor/request.py), all used by the 600-line StagedCli class of the `staged` subcommand,
  which reads each stage's RenoVisor mapping report and measure list.
- hisim/economics/staged_document.py:626: a function-local import of renovisor.report.HiSimCommit
  for the document's engine/commit block.
As a side effect, importing the economics CLI pulls in renovisor and, through its vocabulary,
component modules (import hisim.economics.__main__ takes about 1.3 s).

Fix the direction:
- Move the RenoVisor-specific half of `staged` (reading mapping reports, measure subjects, main
  subjects, the catalogue table) into hisim/renovisor, and let economics take a neutral per-stage
  record (stage directory, year, label, measures as plain data). Whether the command stays
  reachable as `python -m hisim.economics staged` or moves to `python -m hisim.renovisor staged`
  is an owner decision to take in the PR (the backend calls it; check before renaming).
- Move HiSimCommit (or the part staged_document needs) to a neutral module below both, e.g. under
  hisim/ utilities, and import it from there in both packages.
- Put StagedCli in its own module (economics/staged/cli.py or the renovisor side) instead of
  __main__.py.

Done when: grep finds no hisim.renovisor import under hisim/ outside hisim/renovisor,
tests/economics/test_staged_cli.py and tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py pass, and the
staged command's behaviour and exit codes are unchanged.

title: Add a TIERED_PER_UNIT benefit kind so the SEAI solar PV grant is paid pro rata
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H16

Observed: the engine's benefit kinds are `SHARE_OF_ELIGIBLE_COST | BONUS_SHARE | LUMP_SUM |
PER_UNIT | TAX_CREDIT | REDUCED_VAT | SOFT_LOAN | OPERATIONAL`. None expresses "an amount per
unit that changes by tier and is capped": `PER_UNIT` has no cap and no tiers, `LUMP_SUM` does not
scale. SEAI's solar PV grant is exactly that shape -- 700 EUR/kWp up to 2 kWp, 200 EUR/kWp up to
4 kWp, capped at 1 800 EUR, paid pro rata -- so `IE.json` approximates it with four `LUMP_SUM`
steps on `measure.technical_attributes.peak_power_in_kwp`. The steps are exact at 1, 2, 3 and
4 kWp and understate everything between them (a 2.5 kWp array is paid 1 400 EUR instead of
1 500 EUR).

Done when: a `TIERED_PER_UNIT` benefit kind exists in `hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py`
with a tier list and an overall cap, the solver values it, and the four `IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_*`
schemes collapse into one that reproduces the page's own example (2.5 kWp -> 1 500 EUR).

This is a HiSim engine change, not a contract one.
close_reason: Done: BenefitKind.TIERED_PER_UNIT with TieredPerUnitBenefit {tiers[{up_to|null, amount_per_unit}], cap_in_euro|null}, validated at load (non-empty, ascending, only the last open, no negative amount or cap, cap not below the first tier's full value); the solver values it on ComponentCostFacts.size (kWp for PV, confirmed: PVSystem power_in_watt * 1e-3, the same number as the peak_power_in_kwp attribute) and clamps it to the eligible basis. IE.json: the four IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_* steps are one IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV (Warmer Homes' exclusions repointed); README_IE.md and the source note updated. 1->700, 2->1400, 2.5->1500, 3->1600, 4+->1800; validate exits 0; the end-to-end staged run passes.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-09-20: MVP. Specification:
1. hisim/economics/subsidies/catalog.py: BenefitKind.TIERED_PER_UNIT with payload TieredPerUnitBenefit {tiers: [{up_to: number|null, amount_per_unit: number}], cap_in_euro: number|null}; tiers ascending by up_to, the last may be open (null). Value for size s: sum over tiers of amount_per_unit * (min(s, up_to_i) - up_to_{i-1}) for the covered range, capped at cap_in_euro; unit is ComponentCostFacts.size's unit (kW for PV — confirm the PV facts' size is kWp and that the translator's peak_power_in_kwp attribute agrees).
2. Solver: value it like PER_UNIT but with the tier sum; clamp to eligible cost as every lump sum is; validation refuses unsorted tiers, negative amounts, a cap below the first tier.
3. IE.json: the four IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV_* schemes collapse into one IE_SEAI_SOLAR_PV with tiers [{up_to: 2, amount_per_unit: 700}, {up_to: 4, amount_per_unit: 200}], cap 1800, same eligibility; README_IE.md and the sources note drop the step approximation; questions file unchanged.
4. Tests: 1 kWp -> 700, 2 -> 1400, 2.5 -> 1500 (SEAI's own example), 3 -> 1600, 4 and above -> 1800; the catalogue validate command exits 0; the end-to-end staged run still prices the mockup.

title: Reconcile annual by_group Subsidies against plan.subsidies[] reporting undetermined
description:

(frontend agent, 2026-09-20, engine v20260920-1)

Observed: `annual[0].by_group.Subsidies` is -6 015 in the plan while `plan.subsidies[]` is one
`undetermined` row with `amount_in_euro: null` and the note "subsidy_mode NONE, nothing was
awarded". The two parts of one document contradict each other, and the V1/V2 charts draw a credit
that V8 says does not exist.

H7 says the engine's flat subsidy shim is "never published as a grant" -- but it is published in
the year-0 group and in `by_group` / `totals.npv`. Which one is wrong?

Related: cost_module_issues.md item 25 records that the flat shim exists because Ireland had no
subsidy catalogue, and the H8 catalogue now exists.

or `subsidies[]` reports it, and a test pins whichever rule is chosen.
close_reason: Fixed: a staged plan with no catalogue is priced with subsidy_mode NONE (StagedEvaluator.priced_under, used by evaluate, the staged CLI and StagedDocument), so the flat shim no longer reaches by_group/totals; StagedDocument.write refuses a document whose Subsidies stack disagrees with its awarded subsidies[] rows (assert_subsidies_reconciled: every subsidy event names an awarded scheme, and the stack total equals the rows per slot). Also fixed: awarded amounts are keyed by (scheme, subject), so one scheme funding two measures no longer reports its combined total on both rows. Tests: tests/economics/test_staged_document.py::TestSupportIsStatedOnce, tests/renovisor/test_staged_economics.py::test_the_subsidy_stack_is_the_awarded_rows.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Specification (2026-09-20): a document must not book a subsidy it also calls undetermined. Root cause to confirm: each stage's own evaluation applies the engine's flat subsidy shim (a *_net perspective with no catalogue) and writes SUBSIDY timeline entries that the splice carries into the plan's by_group and totals, while plan.subsidies[] is built from the solver decisions (none). Fix: when the staged run resolves to no catalogue, evaluate every stage with subsidy_mode NONE so no shim entry exists (step 10 section 1 already decided the shim is never published); when a catalogue is in force, by_group Subsidies per year must equal the sum of awarded subsidies[] amounts booked in that year. Add that reconciliation to StagedDocument.write's checks (like the band-order check) so a mismatch refuses the document instead of shipping it. Tests: synthetic plan without catalogue -> by_group.Subsidies is 0 in every year and totals carry no subsidy; with the synthetic catalogue -> the awarded grant equals the group's entry in its year; the end-to-end mockup document reconciles.

title: Decide whether the legacy battery capex unit bug is kept until phase 7
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 20a ("Latent legacy bug -- battery capex size"), referenced in code
as issue #21, with its consequence recorded in item 27

`advanced_battery_bslib.get_cost_capex` computes
`size_of_energy_system = config.custom_battery_capacity_generic_in_kilowatt_hour * 1e-3`, i.e. it
prices a 10 kWh battery as 0.01 kWh. The adapter declares the physically correct kWh size, so the
parity report shows a deliberate, explained discrepancy for batteries (cost spec section 9.7:
legacy bugs are documented, not silently reproduced).

Item 27 measured it on a real full-year run: Battery legacy 12.16 EUR vs new 12 159.42 EUR,
visible in every shadow run since the engine was reordered to run before the legacy opex/capex
blocks.

Decision needed at cutover: does the legacy KPI keep the bug until phase 7?

title: Staged ageing register dates stage purchases from the weather year, not the price basis year
description: hisim/economics/staged.py _staged_inputs dates an asset an earlier stage bought as installation_year = stage.inputs.simulation_year + from_year (spec economics-hisim-spec.md §1: installation_year = simulation_year + from_year_j). simulation_year is the WEATHER year (renovisorissues #57), while the engine ages every register asset against the price basis year (context_resolution.py age_in_years(price_basis_year)). For a RenoVisor plan (weather 2019, price basis 2026) an asset bought by a stage at year 3 is dated 2022 and is 4 years old at year 0 of the next stage's evaluation, so its replacement and residual value move ~7 years early. Anchor should be the plan's basis/start year (price_basis_year + from_year, or plan_start_year + from_year), with the spec line changed. Left out of #57 PR 1 (document only) on purpose; changes money in multi-stage plans with from_year > 0.
close_reason: plan year 0 = plan_start_year, else the price basis year: stage purchases dated year0 + from_year (feat/year-zero)

title: RenoVisor translation layer and contract
Post-MVP: write LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR as the emitter and price it approximated
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H3

Observed: a package run sending `heat_distribution.type_of_system: low_temperature_radiator`
produces `HeatDistributionController.config.heating_system: FLOORHEATING`, and the option is
reported `not_implemented_yet` with the note "No cost row for a low-temperature radiator in the
cost database yet; modelled as surface heating".

H3's argument: the physics target exists (`LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR`,
`heat_distribution_system.py:38-50`) and drives the heat pump's COP, so the physics must be
written regardless of pricing; the missing cost row is an economics-side `approximated`, not a
translation gap.

HiSim agent's finding (2026-09-19): the current behaviour is the project owner's explicit
decision of the same day ("put it as not-implemented"), because
`hisim/economics/adapter.py::_hds_facts` returns `None` for `LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR` on purpose
(its own test asserts it) and cost-spec D7 then aborts the whole evaluation: writing the physics
target makes every heat-pump package with that emitter exit 5 with no `lifecycle_costs.json`.
Accepting H3 needs an economics-side change first -- the adapter must degrade to an
`approximated` price for that emitter instead of aborting.

Also confirmed en route: a heat pump on `conventional_radiator` runs the buffer to 90 degC.

Needs the owner's decision. Until then the substitution stands and
`TestTheLowTemperatureRadiatorBlocker` fails the day a cost row exists.

Done when: `LOW_TEMPERATURE_RADIATOR` is written for every generator; the option's status is
`used` (physics) with the cost gap surfaced by the economics engine; T-CAP and the mapping report
agree; the probe `heating_installation.type_of_system=low_temperature_radiator` in a heat-pump
house asserts the target.

title: Land the capability-document determinism change (translator.generated_at dropped)
description:
Source: /home/contract-proposals/todos.md H18 (marked `[-]`: decided, PR pending)

Observed: two builds of the same commit (5a6a4ef) with cache-identical final layers produced
capability documents of 61 982 and 81 311 bytes, same 32 measures, same version fields. It
matters because the backend stores the document per version and serves
`GET /{version}/measures` with a strong ETag that is the hash of the file plus
`Cache-Control: immutable`, so re-registering the same commit yields a different ETag for
equivalent content.

Decision taken (2026-09-19): `translator.generated_at` is dropped from the document, the CLI
(`--generated-at` is gone) and the shared specs (`measure-capabilities.md`, `.openapi.yaml`,
`calculation-request.md`, `translator-implementation-spec.md` section 10.2); a test compares two
builds byte for byte. The work sits on branch `renovisor-staged-economics` on top of the
staged-economics work, PR pending.

What could not be reproduced, recorded so nobody re-chases it: locally two runs differ in nothing
but the timestamp (82 629 bytes each with it neutralised), so the 61 982 vs 81 311 bytes the
backend saw was not the clock. The likely cause is two different code states behind one reported
commit, or a probe run that behaved differently in the image.

Done when: the determinism PR is merged and the byte-for-byte test runs in CI.
close_reason: Completed: translator.generated_at was dropped in PR #779 (commit 536dc265, merged to main as b0c2f043); the capability document is byte-identical across builds, pinned by tests/renovisor/test_capabilities.py::test_two_builds_of_one_state_are_byte_identical

title: Carry measures[i].cost, installation_year, applicant and scop into the request schema
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md F7 and F10 (frontend section, HiSim's half), and the
step-10 / step-12 notes under H7

HiSim reads four additive request fields that the vendored
`hisim/renovisor/contract/calculation-request.schema.json` still rejects, so they are implemented
and unreachable:

* `measures[i].cost {min_in_euro_per_m2, max_in_euro_per_m2, source}` -- without it every
  envelope subject of every real request is `unpriced: true` and
  `result.json.costs.investment_breakdown.envelope_material` is absent with the reason "the
  request carries no material price". The frontend copies `materials.yaml` `measure_costs` into
  it. HiSim already refuses a band with `min > max`, a negative price or a non-finite one as
  `measure.cost.band_invalid`, a code minted HiSim-side because section 7 of the contract does
  not carry the block yet.
* `house.<block>.installation_year` -- without it every existing asset is dated to
  `construction_year` and reported `defaulted`.
* an `applicant` block -- read when present; it carries `receives_means_tested_benefit`,
  `first_time_buyer` and `managed_full_retrofit`, without which every welfare, first-time-buyer,
  One-Stop-Shop-only and loan row of the Irish catalogue comes out `undetermined`.
* `house.heating.scop` -- the engine's subsidy conditions read a heat pump's seasonal performance
  factor as a technical attribute and neither the schema nor the recorded twins state one, so any
  scheme keyed on SCOP stays undetermined for every RenoVisor calculation. Alternative: a
  decision that no Irish scheme uses it.

Done when: the shared `calculation-request.schema.json` carries the four, HiSim re-vendors it,
and the end-to-end test shows a priced envelope subject and a dated existing asset.
close_reason: Done: the shared calculation-request.schema.json carries measures[i].cost, the ten installation_year leaves, living_area_in_m2 and applicant (renovisorissues !8), HiSim re-vendors it (specs at 93b7d70) and #789's readers are carried onto it; the end-to-end staged run prices the facade subject and dates the boiler. house.heating.scop left out: the SCOP is the W35/W55 pair of hisim-epc.27.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Owner decision 2026-09-20: MVP. Specification:
1. SimulationParameters gains cache_directories: List[str] (default: the package's current cache location, so nothing changes for existing callers). A CacheLocations helper (class-scope constants, in the module that owns the cache path today) answers read(path_relative) = first directory holding the file, in order, and write_directory() = the first entry; every caching component goes through it — survey the six caching components hisim-hi1.2 names (building/TABULA, weather, PV, solar thermal, car, LPG/UTSP) and any other hisim/inputs/cache writer.
2. The RenoVisor run (hisim/renovisor/simulation.py) fills it from the environment variable HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES (os.pathsep-separated, absolute paths) when set; the realized simulation record and calculation.json state the directories used. Cache directories are exempt from the output-location cleanliness rule (R13.4) and from the 'no artefacts outside results/' test rule — document that in AGENTS.md.
3. Tests (base): two directories, a file present only in the second is read, a new file is written to the first; unset variable = today's behaviour. End-to-end (system_setups): the mockup baseline run twice with a temporary cache directory, the second run finds the cache (assert by file mtime or a log line), results identical.
4. Backend side (file as a B item in specs/todos.md): mount a persistent volume and pass HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES; hisim-hi1.8 (move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs) becomes the natural default location and depends on this.

title: Confirm translator.commit is filled once the backend writes hisim/COMMIT into the image
description:
Source: /home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H6, H13 and H17 (one thing under three ids)

Observed: `mapping_report.json` carries `{"version": "2.0.0", "commit": null,
"hisim_commit": null}`, and `capabilities.py` validates the capability document against a schema
requiring `translator.commit` to be a string, so a null was fatal: the probe exited 1 and the
backend registered the version `broken`. The cause was `HiSimCommit.of()` shelling out to
`git -C /app rev-parse --short HEAD` in an image whose Containerfile fetches shallow and deletes
`.git`, which forced the backend to ship the `git` binary (~100 MB) plus an 8 KB fabricated
`.git` holding only HEAD -- 1.65 GB instead of 1.55 GB purely for provenance.

HiSim's half is done. `HiSimCommit.of()` in `hisim/renovisor/report.py` now reads the file
`hisim/COMMIT` next to the package, then the `HISIM_COMMIT` environment variable, then git as the
last fallback, and it feeds the mapping report, the capability document and
`economics_result.json` alike; the repository's `Dockerfile` writes that file from a
`HISIM_COMMIT` build argument; and the capability document now emits `"unknown"` instead of
`null`, because the vendored contract schema types both commit fields as strings.

What is left is not HiSim's code. The backend does not build with HiSim's Dockerfile (it
generates its own Containerfile), so the `ARG HISIM_COMMIT` there is irrelevant to the released
images; the backend agent writes `hisim/COMMIT` in its build stage from the SHA it already
resolves. Once it does, the `.git` stub and the runtime git binary can go.

Done when: a released image's `mapping_report.json` and capability document both carry a real
commit, verified on a run, and the three shared-todo boxes are ticked.
close_reason: Backend confirmed on image v20260923-1 (HiSim 75877861): capability document, mapping_report.json and economics_result.json all carry commit 7587786 without git in the image (renovisorissues #10).

title: Carry heat pump SCOP and its W35/W55 application in the house inventory spec
description:
Source: owner conversation 2026-09-21 on heat pump efficiency; the maintainer of the RenoVisor house
inventory spec (calculation-request.schema.json and calculation-request.md in
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/) will carry the fields, HiSim does not write that spec.

Today the request has `house.heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent` (1..400) and HiSim applies it to
boilers only. For a heat pump the translator lists it as not implemented and the twin's hplib
defaults stand. The field also does not say which number a heat pump user would enter: SCOP x 100
(about 300..500) or the ErP label's eta_s (about 120..200), which differ by a factor of about 2.5.

What HiSim needs the spec to carry for a heat pump (existing one in `house.heating`, and the same
shape on the `heating_system` measure options for a new one):
- `scop`: number > 1, the manufacturer's standardized seasonal COP per EN 14825, average climate.
- `scop_application`: enum `w35` | `w55`, the sink temperature the label refers to (low-temperature
  or medium-temperature application). Without it the number cannot be placed on the curve.
- Ground source: same two fields; the standard's brine bins apply. Nothing extra.
- The boiler keeps `seasonal_efficiency_in_percent`; the spec should say the percent field is not
  meant for heat pumps.

This also settles the `house.heating.scop` item in hisim-epc.14 (subsidy conditions read the SCOP as
a technical attribute): one field serves both the physics and the economics.

Done when: the shared schema and the request document carry the two fields with the meaning above,
and HiSim has re-vendored the schema (hisim-epc.14 covers the re-vendoring routine).
close_reason: Done: the request carries house.heating.heatpump_scop_en14825_w35/_w55 (renovisorissues !9, re-vendored at 93b7d70); HiSim refuses them on a heating that is not a heat pump (heating.scop.not_a_heat_pump) and a W55 above W35 (heating.scop.w55_above_w35), lists both as not_implemented_yet (tracked hisim-4g9.15) and probes them on a heat pump. Physics only (decision 2026-09-23): nothing is published for subsidies, since no grant is ever decided for the pump already in the house.

So the pair replaces scop + scop_application, which is better for HiSim: two rating points place the unit at its design flow temperature. title: Have the physics owner review the fifteen TO BE REVIEWED constants of the translator
description:
Source: hisim/renovisor/constants.py (15 sites marked TO BE REVIEWED);
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H11; roadmap/renovisor/implementation/step8_reconciliation.md
and step10_staged_economics.md

`hisim/renovisor/constants.py` says in its own module docstring that every default it holds is
marked TO BE REVIEWED. The fifteen marked sites, by line, are: default insulation thicknesses per
build-up (:70), the country-pack U-value fallbacks (:88), the two conductivity defaults (:123,
:127), `NEW_WINDOW_U` (:164), `NEW_DOOR_U` (:173), the DHW-pipe insulation stand-in (:215), the
ventilation/heat-recovery defaults (:224), `DesignTemperatures.BY_COUNTRY` (:246-253; IE -3 degC
after I.S. EN 12831 / SEAI heat-pump sizing guidance, NL -10 degC after NEN 5060 / ISSO 51), the
heat-recovery interpolation bounds (:281), and the `AnywayShareByPlacement` shares (:357, :365).

H11 records why the design temperature in particular matters: HiSim #771 moved it to the weather
(`Weather.for_location` requires `heating_reference_temperature_in_celsius`; the building reads
it as a sizing fact), TABULA cannot supply it (`Theta_e_Base` is the 12 degC heating-degree-day
base for every country, `Theta_e` the annual mean), and a country without a reviewed constant is
a translator error rather than Aachen's -7 degC.

Done when: each constant is either confirmed with its source or replaced, and the TO BE REVIEWED
marker is removed from the ones that were reviewed.

title: The Building warns that HeatingByResidents/HeatingByDevices are not connected although they are
description: Source: renovisorissues #35 (backend, 2026-09-23), checked 2026-09-25. Every RenoVisor run (and the household_heatpump_building_sizer twin) logs 'the HeatingByResidents input is not connected. Internal heat gains from occupants default to 0 W' (and the same for HeatingByDevices), yet component_connections.json carries both links from UTSPConnector and Building_InternalHeatGainsFromOccupancy equals the connector's residents + devices (511 W mean on a January run). The warning is emitted before the energy system's connections are resolved. Fix: log it only when the input is still unconnected after wiring (find where the Building emits it, and where the energy-system loader resolves default connections). Answer #35 with the PR.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/building-gains-warning (uncommitted): the check ran in i_prepare_simulation, but Simulator.run_all_timesteps resolves source_output in connect_all_components after preparing every component, so it warned on every run. Moved to a once-only check on the first simulated timestep (Building.warn_about_unconnected_internal_heat_gains). New tests/test_building_internal_heat_gains_warning.py (wired: no warning; unwired: one warning per input, 0 W). One-day household_heatpump_building_sizer run: warning gone, 142 result files byte-identical. occupancy_identity note is correct (only generic_car reads it). Answer renovisorissues #35 with the PR.

title: RenoVisor baseline stage is awarded the IE heat-pump central-heating grant for its existing radiators
description:
Surfaced by the renovisorissues #50 fix (existing_heating now in the RenoVisor subsidy context).

Staged run of the vendored IE mockup (gas boiler -> air-source HP), baseline (no measures) and package, both year 0:
IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE is now AWARDED -2000 EUR in stage 0 (baseline) as well as in stage 1, both rows with measure_id None.
Before the fix both rows were UNDETERMINED (asking building.existing_heating.asset_class), which masked this.

Causes (pre-existing, not introduced by #50):
1. The heat distribution system is not in the RenoVisor existing-asset register (DeviceAssets.ALL has only pv_system and battery), so the simulated radiators are measure_kind INSTALL in every stage (calculators/subsidy_application.py: REPLACE iff replaced_asset), including the do-nothing baseline.
2. IE.json's central-heating scheme applies_to heat-distribution asset classes and conditions only on actor, year, dwelling type and existing_heating.asset_class != HeatPump; nothing requires that a heat pump is installed in the same stage.
3. The stage-1 distribution row carries measure_id None although the package's heating_installation measure installs it (result.subjects has no entry for the distribution component).

Effect: the baseline is credited a grant it would never get; the package-minus-baseline delta for this scheme nets to 0 instead of -2000.
close_reason: Resolved by registering the existing equipment (renovisorissues #48, owner decisions 2026-09-26): the heat distribution system, buffer, hot-water cylinder and meters are ExistingAssets of every stage, so the do-nothing baseline keeps its radiators, books no investment and no longer meets IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE at all; heating_system keeps the radiators, so an oil/gas plan without heating_installation gets no central-heating row either; a heating_installation measure replaces the emitters (REPLACE) and the grant is awarded once, on stage 1, with measure_id heating_installation. Left for the owner, catalogue unchanged: the scheme still has no condition that a heat pump is installed with the emitters (cause 2).

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Follow-up (owner decisions 2026-09-26, same worktree): cause 2 is now fixed in the catalogue too. IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_CENTRAL_HEATING_HOUSE/_APARTMENT require package.installed_asset_classes contains HeatPump (new computed condition root package.*, filled per evaluation by EconomicEvaluator from the §4.1 installation verdict); IE_SEAI_HEAT_PUMP_UNIT_HOUSE/_APARTMENT require building.existing_heating.asset_class != HeatPump. heating_installation alone on an oil/gas house: central-heating row ineligible; with heating_system in the same stage: awarded once.

title: The solar collector's hot-water circuit carries twice the heat it books, and its controller's switch-on test needs a collector temperature that is not the circuit's supply
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.3, §5.5, D4; hisim/components/solar_thermal_system.py (SolarThermalSystem.i_simulate, SolarThermalSystemController.get_controller_state).

The collector books Q_coll(T_in) but pumps m = Q/(c dT_n) at T_out = T_in + 2 dT_n, so its water carries 2 Q into the tank (dT_n = 10 K is the collector's inlet-to-mean difference). With the tank a mixed node (stage C), the tank books what the water carries: over 2021 at 900 s the gas solar twin's collector books 227.7 kWh and the tank receives 455.4 kWh from it. Stage C leaves the collector unconverted.

Spec §5.3 says: pump owner at the flow sized for dT_n, T_sup = T_ret + Q(T_ret)/(m c) (so T_out = T_in + dT_n), controller keeps start values. Two things the spec leaves open: (1) the efficiency law evaluates the collector at its mean T_in + dT_n, which for a linear profile means T_out = T_in + 2 dT_n, so the spec's outlet halves the lift the efficiency law assumes; (2) the controller switches the pump on when CollectorTemperature - T0 > 10 K and reads CollectorTemperature from the collector's outlet. With T_out = T_in + dT_n = T_in + 10 K the test becomes T_bar > T0 and the pump would almost never start; an idle circuit (T_sup = T_ret) never starts it.

Options: (a) spec as written for the circuit (m = Q/(c dT_n), T_sup = T_bar + dT_n) plus a separate collector-temperature output for the controller, evaluated at T0 (T0 + 2 dT_n while Q(T0) > 0, the value the controller reads today); (b) keep the outlet T_in + 2 dT_n and size the flow for it, m = Q/(2 c dT_n), with the controller-facing outputs evaluated at T0 as in (a) (the controller's 0.01 kg/s minimum flow then switches at twice today's collector heat unless restated); (c) as (a) but compare the collector's heat at T0 instead of a temperature. Recommendation: (b), consistent with the efficiency law, plus T0-evaluated controller inputs (D4). Blocks hisim-lt0b.23.
close_reason: Decided by the owner 2026-10-09: the collector's outlet stays T_in + 2 dT_n and its flow is sized for 2 dT_n, so its water carries exactly the booked heat; its controller reads T0-evaluated inputs (spec §5.3 corrected). Done in 31ec2ee3 on hydronic-stage-c; the solar twins close per step and both circuit ends agree (tests/test_dhw_chain_twins.py).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Correction (2026-10-10, review of hydronic stage C, finding F12.4): the close reason says the controller reads T0-evaluated inputs. The code merged in stage C has the controller read the collector's outputs evaluated at the tank's step mean, with only the full-tank stop on T0 (spec §5.3). On 2026-10-10 the owner removed the switch-on comparison and the collector-temperature output (finding F4): the controller now reads the flow the collector heat at the step mean needs (minimum-flow stop) and the tank's start-of-step temperature (full-tank stop).

title: Let the solar pump run only the part of a step it can deliver, so collector yield and the backup's fuel or electricity agree across step lengths
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.3 and §9.5 C (owner, 2026-10-09). Due before RenoVisor's solar thermal results are relied on: RenoVisor runs at 900 s.

The solar pump decides once per step: it switches on at the tank's step mean when the collector has heat there and runs the whole step, and it stops for the whole step once the tank started above 60 °C (the stop stays on the start temperature T0, owner 2026-10-09, because on the step mean it has no fixed point). The DHW chain otherwise agrees across step lengths, but the houses with a solar collector do not: at coarse steps the tank sits hotter for longer (whole-step charges of the backup generator, whole-step pump decisions), so the collector runs at a hotter inlet and less often, and the backup makes up the difference.

Evidence, full year 2021, predefined occupancy profile, 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s:
- household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer: collector yield -7.0 % / -23.5 %, the boiler's hot-water gas +1.3 % / +4.3 %, the tank's net heat +0.18 % / +0.50 %.
- household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer: collector yield -15.2 % / -15.1 %, the heat pump's hot-water electricity +9.2 % / +43 %, net heat +0.16 % / +0.58 %.

Task: let the solar pump run only the part of a step it can deliver (for example the fraction of the step until the tank reaches its 60 °C stop, or until the collector heat at the rising tank temperature falls below the minimum flow), so the collector yield and the backup's fuel or electricity agree within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s, without steps ending at force_convergence. Done when: the two solar twins meet that over a full year, the strict per-step closure test (tests/test_dhw_chain_twins.py) still passes, goldens re-blessed.

Approach (owner, 2026-10-09): the part-load run fraction above the step-length threshold, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md, prototype part 3; builds on hisim-naze.

title: The heat pump's hot-water electricity depends on step length: whole-step charges into hplib's near-COP-1 range
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §9.5 C (owner, 2026-10-09). RenoVisor runs at 900 s, where the residual is +1.73 %.

With the hot-water supply capped at the controller's set temperature (t_max plus the energy manager's raise) and the charge ending within 0.5 K of it, the heat pump's hot-water heat agrees across step lengths, but its electricity does not. household_heatpump_building_sizer, full year 2021, predefined occupancy profile, against 60 s: hot-water heat +0.09 % at 900 s and +0.27 % at 3600 s (net of stored heat +0.10 % / +0.38 %), hot-water electricity +1.73 % at 900 s and +18.1 % at 3600 s.

Cause: the controller decides on the tank's start temperature for a whole step (D4), so at 3600 s a charge runs an hour, often to the raised 70 °C target, and the cylinder sits hot. 62 % of the hot-water heat at 3600 s is made with a return above 63 °C, where hplib runs near COP 1 (its heating-rod mode), against 20 % at 60 s; the hot-water COP is 2.44 at 3600 s against 2.87 at 60 s. The energy manager's raise also switches inside a step (hisim-4g9.28, hisim-4g9.31), and under force_convergence the controller holds a raised set temperature.

Same whole-step cause as hisim-fxix.11 (the solar pump): letting the heat pump run only the part of a step its charge needs may solve both. Done when: the heat pump's hot-water electricity agrees within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s over a full year, the strict per-step closure test still passes, goldens re-blessed.

Approach (owner, 2026-10-09): the part-load run fraction above the step-length threshold, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md, prototype part 2; builds on hisim-naze.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10, memoryless rule (part-load-heatpump, #916), full year 2021 against 60 s: heat pump twin hot-water electricity -1.17 % at 900 s and +13.0 % at 3600 s (the pass-counting search: -1.21 % / +6.0 %), forced steps 4504 / 2082; 206 of 1129 partial steps converge at 900 s, 51 of 596 at 3600 s, because the energy manager's raise switches the target between passes. Stays open.

title: The heat-pump-and-solar twin aborts at 3600 s: the capped heat pump and the tank's step mean form a 2-cycle the 0.5 under-relaxation cannot damp
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), owner decision 2026-10-09.

household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 3600 s (predefined occupancy profile), aborts with "More than 100 tries in time step 4426" (July). The heat pump's hot-water supply is capped at its controller's set temperature, so its heat is m c (T_set - T̄): with the heat pump on and the collector charging, the tank's step mean flips between 45.6 °C and 61.9 °C, a 2-cycle of the node's fixed-point map with a slope of about -3.5. The node's acceleration (hisim.hydronics.accelerated_node_mean) under-relaxes a residual that changes sign with weight 0.5 (owner-pinned, 2026-10-04), which damps only slopes above -3 (error factor 1 + 0.5 (F' - 1) = -1.25 here), and force_convergence freezes the controllers but not the node.

Tested in a scratch copy only: a secant step between the two bracketing iterates (x - r (x - x_prev) / (r - r_prev) when r r_prev < 0) makes the year complete (484 forced steps; hot-water electricity +14.2 % and collector yield +0.02 % against 60 s). The owner kept 0.5 for now (2026-10-09). 60 s and 900 s complete; no CI test runs this twin at 3600 s over July (the resolution test runs January). Done when: the twin's year at 3600 s completes without lifting the pinned parameter unilaterally, or with the owner's decision on the oscillation branch.

title: Above the part-load threshold the memoryless rule does not settle where a device is evaluated between its controller and the tank (boiler and collector twins)
description:
Source: the memoryless part-load rule (roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §4.3, branch hydronic-part-load, #915 to #918; agent measurement 2026-10-10).

The L1 controller pairs the ratio its device reports it ran (PartLoadRatioRunDhw) with the tank's end temperature it reads in the same pass. The two belong to the same run only in the cyclic evaluation order controller -> device -> tank. The boiler twins (gas, oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen, gas + solar) and the collector in both solar twins list the device before its controller and the tank after both (device -> controller -> tank): there the device has already run the controller's newer ratio when the controller reads the tank's answer to the older one. In x = ln r the iteration is then x_k = x_{k-1} - x_{k-2} + c, whose roots lie on the unit circle: the ratio circles its fixed point with a period of six passes and settles only by chance.

Measured, full year 2021 (spec §11), twin order / every part-load controller moved before its device: gas twin 1013 / 46 forced steps at 900 s and 679 / 50 at 3600 s, hot-water gas against 60 s +0.27 % / -0.00 % and +0.18 % / -0.01 %, mean passes 4.26 / 3.42; 5 of 739 partial boiler steps converge at 900 s in the twin's order, 718 of 759 with the controller first. Gas + solar: collector -11.9 % / -1.7 % at 900 s and -9.6 % / +0.4 % at 3600 s, forced steps 1193 / 121 and 839 / 212. The gas twin at 60 s with the controller moved: every column within 1e-12 relative, but not bit-identical. The DHW chain test expects the failure of a file whose forced steps all run a part-load ratio, and the part-load twin test expects the gas twin to have no converged partial step.

Options (owner decision):
(a) Order: every L1 controller before its device in the setups, the recorded and grouped twins and the assemblies' member order. Simple; moves 60 s results by about 1e-12 (below the golden tolerance of 1e-9, but not bit-identical) and needs a re-record.
(b) A port that tells the controller which flow the tank's reading answers: the tank republishes the mass flow it integrated per charging circuit (as it already republishes the inflow temperature), and the controller pairs T_end with r_run * m_tank / m_device. Order-independent and 60 s bit-identical, but every part-load controller reads two more ports, wired per circuit.
(c) Accept the forced steps.

Recommendation: (a), since a controller commanding before its device is the natural order and the change at 60 s is float noise; (b) if bit-identity at 60 s must hold.

title: The memoryless part-load rule alternates where the draw takes more than the rise the step still needs (electric heater beside space heating)
description:
Source: the memoryless part-load rule (roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §4.3, §11; branches hydronic-part-load to part-load-hds, #915 to #918; agent measurement 2026-10-10).

The rule takes the store's start temperature T_start as its end temperature at ratio 0. With a draw, the end temperature at ratio 0 lies below T_start by d, and the plain iteration's error is multiplied by -d / (T_aim - T_start) per pass: it alternates, and it diverges into a two-cycle between 1 and a small ratio (whose end temperature falls below T_start, which the rule answers with 1) once the draw takes more than the rise the step still needs. This is independent of the evaluation order (hisim-fxix.16).

Measured, full year 2021: the electric-heating twin (controller evaluated before its heater) tops the tank up beside space heating at 45 °C in a third of its winter steps; 730 of its 900 s steps and 883 of its 3600 s steps need a forced pass (the pass-counting search: 212 and 200), and its hot-water electricity against 60 s moves from +0.01 % / -0.07 % to +0.12 % / +0.74 %. Traced example, 10 January 17:30 at 900 s: T_start 44.99 °C, target 45 °C, the ratio alternates 1 / 0.024 until the forced passes.

Options (owner decision): (a) accept; (b) a convergence aid on the ratio, which decision 13 of the spec rules out today; (c) a better stand-in for the end temperature at ratio 0 that the store can publish as a port quantity without a model behind it (none is known).

title: A whole-step full-power hot-water charge overheats the energy-conserving DHW tank past 90 °C: at 3600 s, and at 900 s for a small tank or a large generator
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5.1, §5.2, §7, D1, D2, D4.

With the DHW tank a mixed node (stage C), a generator's hot-water heat is no longer lost in the tank's mass mixing. Controllers decide on the tank's start-of-step temperature T0 (D4), so a charge runs the whole step. A full-power charge then overshoots whenever the step is long against the tank and the generator is large: the boiler holds its lift (D1: T_sup = T_ret + dT, P_th fixed), the hplib heat pump holds its 5 K lift (D2), and the tank leaves the 0..90 °C plausibility range, which fails the run.

Measured:
- tests/test_water_storage_temperature_check.py::test_the_gas_house_keeps_its_storages_in_range_for_a_winter_week[3600] (Irish 1960 gas house via RenoVisor, first January week 2019) reaches 102.6 °C (marked a strict xfail on the branch); household_heatpump_building_sizer, full year 2021 at 3600 s, reaches 96.0 °C. 900 s and 1800 s stay in range for the recorded twins and that RenoVisor house.
- At 900 s the assembly test contracts (pytest -m assemblies, tests/assemblies/test_library_contracts.py) fail on the samples at the edge of their parameter boxes: dhw/indirect_cylinder at its minimum 100 l beside the 40 kW partner heat pump (90.4 °C), heating/wood_chip_boiler at its largest power (96.1 °C, and the power sweep), heating/air_source_heat_pump s002 (hot-water electricity 20.3 kW above its 20 kW bound, and a buffer sweep at 92.3 °C): 61 failures, all of this kind. The assemblies CI job fails on the branch until this is decided.
- At 3600 s the generators' hot-water heat (net of the tank's stored heat) is 1.2-1.6 % above 60 s, mostly the standby loss of the hotter tank; the stage C done-when asks for 1 %.

Options: (a) a maximum supply temperature per generator (a boiler's high limit, the heat pump's maximum outlet; e.g. the controller's 70 °C hot-water flow set point), the generator throttling to T_sup = min(T_ret + dT, T_max) like the district-heating substation (§5.4); for the boiler this needs the fuel for the booked heat, the inverse law D1 dropped; (b) declare the overshooting cases outside the supported envelope: keep the 3600 s test xfail and narrow the assembly parameter boxes (smallest cylinder, largest boiler) to what stays in range at 900 s; (c) circuit laws (hisim-4g9.22). Recommendation: (a) for every generator with a fixed lift (boiler, electric heater, heat pump), since it is a physical limit the spec's "within its limits" (§5) already names; it reopens D1's fuel law for the throttled steps only.
close_reason: Decided by the owner 2026-10-09: every fixed-lift generator throttles at a maximum supply temperature (GenericBoiler 80 °C, ElectricHeating's hot-water side 80 °C, the hplib heat pump's hot-water side 75 °C), the throttled heat is m c (T_max - T_ret) and its fuel or electricity follows through the generator's own law (spec §5, D1 amended). Done in 29cf73a4 on hydronic-stage-c: the 3600 s gas house and heat-pump twin stay in range, pytest -m assemblies passes (2807 passed).

title: A one-day run with every post-processing option exceeds 5 GB of memory
description: Source: write-guard survey, 2026-09-26. A one-day run with all post-processing options (PDF report, network charts, ...) peaked above 5 GB and was OOM-killed on the 22 GB agent box (it took the Claude processes down with it); the moderate option set peaks at 1.7 GB. Profile which option allocates the memory (likely plots/PDF/network charts over the full result frame) and bound it; CI's 16 GB runners hide it.

title: The envelope elements' installation_year is reported used but changes nothing at the anchor
description: Source: tier-1 path verification findings (no effect), 2026-09-26. house.building.{roof,floor,window,door}.installation_year are reported used by the economic context, yet the economic context (and energy system) is identical for two values at the anchor (no envelope measure). Check what the year feeds when no measure touches the element (the register's envelope rows; mid-life rule leaves envelope at construction year) and either make the use visible or report the status honestly (e.g. used only when a measure replaces the element).
close_reason: Envelope installation_year is used only when the element has a register row (an area) and a measure replaces/insulates it: the engine reads a row's age only for a replaced asset (sunk cost, anyway credit); a kept envelope row matches no cost subject. Otherwise the builder records it on EconomicContextResult.unread and the translator replaces the early used line with approximated + a note naming where the value lands (kept row: recorded on the register row, read by no cost line; no area: no row, read by nothing). Verifier: 28 -> 20 findings (8 roof/floor/window/door no_effect gone).

title: Build the tier-1 path-verification runner and CI report (renovisorissues #30)
description: Frontend ask: https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/iek-3/groups/urbanmodels/renovisorissues/-/work_items/30. specs/path_verification_spec.md §9 step 1: a runner in hisim/renovisor/verify/ over the anchor request and the ProbeSet skeleton probes, stages 1-3 of §4, the §5 report as a HiSim CI artifact; the spec then says where the frontend reads it. WAITING FOR HUMAN APPROVAL.

Step 1 implemented on feat/path-verification-tier1 (hisim/renovisor/verify, python -m hisim.renovisor verify, workflow path-verification.yml, artifact path-verification-report).
