title: Compute the buffer-less distribution loop quasi-steady above its turnover criterion, so generator and pipe water need no fixed point
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §6.3, §7, §11 part 4 (owner, 2026-10-09). Replaces the circuit laws (hisim-4g9.22) as the planned remedy for the buffer-less loop (hydronic spec D3).

Without a buffer the distribution system's pipe water turns over in minutes, so at 900 s generator and pipe water need about 16-24 iterations to agree (about 60 at 3600 s) and the result is biased by about 0.5 K. Above the turnover criterion (a = m_design dt / M_pipe > 1, and dt above part_load_above_seconds) the loop is computed quasi-steady within the step: the radiators deliver the building's demand, the generator covers it plus the pipe water's change of stored heat (a lift-holding generator by its part-load fraction, a district-heating substation directly), and the temperatures follow algebraically, with no fixed point between generator and pipe water. Below the criterion the loop keeps its dynamic behaviour, the reference.

Done when: 60 s results unchanged; the district-heating twin over a full year at 900 s and 3600 s agrees with 60 s within 1 % on delivered heat and the district-heating bill (bill = delivered heat + the pipe water's change of stored heat, hisim-9uoo.12), with no forced steps at 900 s.

title: Caching correctness and the cache service
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md, roadmap/cache_service_spec.md, roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8

Everything about how HiSim caches computed inputs: the six components that use
`hisim.utils.get_cache_file`, the producer-keyed cache service (phase 1 landed for weather, PV
series and building solar gains), the legacy caches that still key on configuration alone, the
non-bit-exact PV CSV round trip, the pylpg serialisation workaround, and the cache service's own
open questions.

title: Read the building-sizer cache directories from the environment instead of cluster paths
description:
Source: simulation_issues.md 4

All `system_setups/household_*_building_sizer.py` hard-code FZJ cluster paths, still on main
(checked 2026-09-20):
`cache_dir_path_simuparams = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/hisim_inputs_cache/"` and
`cache_dir_path_utsp: Optional[str] = "/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/lpg-utsp-cache"`.

On any machine that is not the cluster these paths silently do not exist and caching is disabled
-- every run recomputes LPG profiles and weather inputs, which dominates runtime for short
simulations. The RenoVisor use case runs one simulation per request, so cold caches hurt every
single request.

Suggested fix: read the cache directories from environment variables (e.g.
`HISIM_UTSP_CACHE_DIR`, `HISIM_INPUTS_CACHE_DIR`) or from `SimulationParameters`, with the
cluster paths as documented defaults. One shared helper instead of a copy in each of the eleven
setups.

Related: `roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/grouping_worklist.md` names the two
`/benchtop/2024-k-rieck-hisim/` existence probes as environment couplings a recording has to pin;
and the RenoVisor container needs a declared cache-directory list anyway.

Testing: a setup-level test that sets the env var to a temp dir and asserts the occupancy config
picks it up; run one of the fast marker tests twice and assert the second run hits the cache.

title: Run the cold-versus-cached protocol over all six caching components
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13 ("Every component that caches, not just this one")
and section 10 ("How to verify a fix")

The worst fault of the pylpg investigation (Fault D, section 6) is a caching pattern: a key taken
from what the caller asked for, contents produced by what the code actually did. Nothing about it
is specific to load profiles, so the verification protocol belongs to every cached component, and
each needs its own answer to one question -- can this cache ever be filled with something other
than what its key describes?

Six components use the shared helper `hisim.utils.get_cache_file`:
`loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py` (occupancy profiles; Faults A-D, the only one that
rewrites its own configuration), `generic_pv_system.py` (a year of AC power ratios; second
confirmed defect, see the CSV round-trip issue), `weather.py` (weather series; feeds nearly every
setup), `building/building.py` (building physics), `solar_thermal_system.py` (collector output)
and `generic_car.py` (car profiles; its data originates from the occupancy, so Fault D can reach
it second-hand).

What the sweep should produce, for each of the six in that order: run the protocol, and record
whether run 1 and run 2 agree bit for bit. Where they differ, establish which of the two is right
-- the cached or the computed value -- because that decides whether the fix is in the writer or
the reader. Then answer, per component, whether every input that changes the result is part of
the key. A cache whose key omits a relevant input is Fault D wearing a different hat.

PV is expected to fail today, which makes it the first thing to measure rather than a surprise to
discover.

title: Stop the PV cache round-tripping float64 through CSV text
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 13, "The PV cache does not round-trip exactly"; with
the consequence recorded as roadmap/p3_random_findings.md F-32

`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/pv_system.py` writes its cache with `database.to_csv(...)`
(:514) and reads it back with `pd.read_csv(...)` (:485) -- a text round trip of float64 data. So
a cached PV run and an uncached one are not the same run.

P3's parity work already ran into it: giving both sides of a comparison one cache directory let
the second run read the first run's PV output back out of the CSV, which both masked a real
configuration difference and invented a false one. That was worked around there by giving each
side its own empty cache; it is not fixed. F-32 generalises it: any A/B comparison of two HiSim
runs on one machine has this hazard.

Done when: the PV cache round-trips bit-exactly (parquet, npy, or a full-precision text format),
and the cold-versus-cached protocol passes for PV.

title: Key the solar thermal and car caches on their producer code, not configuration alone
description:
Source: roadmap/p4_random_findings.md F-8 (fixed for three producers), closing paragraph;
roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 12 (the survey)

Phase 1 of the cache service landed three producers that key on their own code:
`hisim/components/weather/calculation.py` (`weather_series`),
`hisim/components/generic_pv_system/calculation.py` (`pv_series`) and
`hisim/components/building/solar_gains.py` (`building_solar_gains`). Each key is a fingerprint of
the producer module's source and of every `hisim` module in its transitive import closure, plus
the third-party versions in it and the calculation's DTO.

Two legacy caches still key on configuration and simulation parameters alone:
`solar_thermal_system.py` (pvlib solar positions, so a pvlib upgrade is what would be invisible)
and `generic_car.py` (an LPG export resampled by our own `resample_meters_driven`). Both are
future producers; the survey in section 12 of the cache spec lists them.

Why it matters, from F-8: before the producers, a physics change (the zenith clamp of #628, which
moves 33 KPIs on a cold cache) was invisible to the golden gate, because CI restores
`hisim/inputs/cache` from the previous run and the restore key hashes only the files that decide
where an entry is filed, not the ones that decide what is in it.

Done when: both caches are producer-keyed and an edit to either producer misses the cache.

title: Delete the whole-calculation pylpg lock once the cache service removes the need for it
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 9, F13 ("shipped in #611, and meant to be deleted")

Since F12 did not end the sqlite contention and the remaining shared route was never found, the
lock F10 introduced is held for the length of a calculation, so local LPG runs serialise. Of the
twenty-two system setups four run local profiles, so eighteen keep their parallelism and four
take turns -- and those four were contending with each other in any case.

The document is explicit: this is a workaround for a defect in a third-party binary, and it
should be deleted rather than maintained. The cache service (PR #584) removes the need to
generate the same profile repeatedly at all, which is the real answer; when it lands, the
serialisation goes with the need for it. The lock's docstring says so too, so whoever finds it
does not mistake it for design.

Done when: the cache service makes repeated generation unnecessary and the whole-calculation lock
is removed, keeping F10's install lock.

title: Find the shared path by which two pylpg calculations still reach one sqlite database
description:
Source: roadmap/pylpg_flakiness.md section 14, open question 4

With F12 in place each calculation runs its own executable beside its own `profilegenerator.db3`,
and one still died with `database is locked`. Some path -- an absolute location compiled in, a
temp directory, a user-profile location -- is shared and was not found. F13 serialises around it.

The document records it as "recorded rather than pursued": the question only matters if the
serialisation ever has to be lifted before the cache service makes it moot.

needs-triage: this is an investigation with no owner and a named reason not to do it. Close it
with the F13 lock removal if the cache service lands first.

title: Answer the four open questions of the cache service spec
description:
Source: roadmap/cache_service_spec.md section 13, "Open questions"

1. Blob size cap and total quota -- needs measured sizes of the largest current `.cache` files
   (UTSP full-year minutely results are the likely maximum).
2. Does the internal endpoint require read auth? Recommendation: no -- friction for zero gain
   inside the institute network.
3. Which weather subset stays bundled in the repository for offline-after-install use?
4. Should the RenoVisor container prewarm at build time (bigger image, instant start) or at first
   start (small image, slow first request)? Recommendation: build time for weather datasets,
   first-start for opportunistic entries.

Related: the deferred cache writes of section 12 (PV non-predictive, building and solar thermal
fill their cache late) go with the producer migration.

title: Move the generated cache out of hisim/inputs so it stops masquerading as input data
description:
Source: roadmap/rust_ideas/hisim_rust_recommended_cleanup_steps.md, Tier 3, "Separate tracked
reference data from generated cache"; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md C26

`hisim/inputs/` holds about 319 MB of git-tracked reference data; on a working copy it reaches
1.7 GB because generated caches live in the same tree. Move the cache out of `hisim/inputs/`, and
consider distributing the reference data as a versioned package or download.

Payoff now: clone size, and -- the operational half -- cache from one branch stops masquerading
as input data in another, which is a known source of false "pre-existing" test failures.

C26 says the same from the container side: `hisim/inputs/cache/Building_<hash>.cache` is on disk
on main right now, and the cache's location must be an explicit declared directory, not the
working tree.

Done when: no generated cache lives under `hisim/inputs/`, and the default location is declared.

title: Let a window's or door's frame, panes and coating reach the Building beyond the U-value
description:
Source: hisim-bc02 (owner request 2026-09-26): every entry of hisim/renovisor/not_implemented_yet.yaml names the bead that would let it be deleted.

Entries: paths house.building.window.frame_material, .glazing_panes, .low_emissivity_coating, house.building.door.frame_material, .glazing_panes; measures window_replacement.frame_material, door_replacement.frame_material (notes: the U-value carries the whole window/door). The Building reads one U-value per opening and the TABULA g-value; panes and coating also set the solar transmittance, and the frame material the frame share. Decide which of these the Building should read, wire them, delete the entries.

title: Part-load run fraction for the space-heating buffer once it is a node
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §6.2 (owner, 2026-10-09).

Once the space-heating buffer (SimpleHotWaterStorage) is a node (hydronic stage D, hisim-fxix.5), its charging generators (GenericBoiler and MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib on their space-heating circuits) run the part-load fraction to the buffer's set temperature above the threshold, as the hot-water cylinder does. Done when: the boiler and heat-pump twins' space-heating heat and fuel or electricity agree within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s, 60 s unchanged.

title: Economics plan: the reader's quoted price per measure (investment_overrides), renovisorissues #53
description: Owner decisions 2026-09-26: plan-block key investment_overrides [{stage, measure_id, amount_in_euro, source}]; every priced catalogue measure accepts it. The quote replaces the measure's MAIN subject's year-0 investment (generator for heating_system); the measure's other subjects (e.g. the buffer) take 0 investment in that stage, but keep their lifetimes and database-priced replacements. Subsidies computed on eligible cost follow the quote; later replacements stay at database prices; the quote is exact (no band). Echo: the quote on the measure, the subject's price marked reader_quote with its source. Via investment_cost_override_in_euro + override_source. Schema v6 together with #54, after #839, #58 and the year-0 anchor PR (hisim-dutz/nl6j).
close_reason: investment_overrides: the reader's quote per measure, schema_version 6 (feat/quotes-and-caps)

title: Price Irish PV feed-in as the Clean Export Guarantee, with a sourced rate and its own provenance
description: Source: renovisorissues #47 investigation, owner decision 2026-09-26. energy_prices_IE.json's ELECTRICITY_FEED_IN (0.10/0.15/0.20 EUR/kWh 2026, 0.05/0.08/0.12 2035) is an AI estimate, and hisim/economics/calculators/energy.py (~136-157) models every feed-in as an EEG-style FIXED_TARIFF held nominal for 20 years. Ireland pays exports under the Clean Export Guarantee: supplier-set, market-linked rates (roughly 0.15-0.24 EUR/kWh in 2024-2026), not a guaranteed 20-year tariff. Model the IE feed-in kind accordingly (a market/escalating rate), source the rates (CRU, supplier tariffs), and give the feed-in rate its own provenance record (energy.py's docstring calls the missing provenance 'the one remaining gap of the energy path'), so economics_result.json can say where the price comes from.

title: Review the heat-pump buffer sizing of 50 l per kW
description: Source: renovisorissues #48 investigation, owner decision 2026-09-26 (bead only). simple_water_storage.py's _buffer_volume_in_liter sizes the space-heating buffer at 50 l/kW with SIZE_ACCORDING_TO_HEAT_PUMP (the heat-pump twins) and 20 l/kW for general heating systems. Current planning guidance is mostly 10-25 l/kW (some manufacturers 40-50 l/kW). A ~1,000 l buffer for a 21 kW heat pump drives investment and storage losses. Review the law with sources; changing it changes simulation results and golden references.

title: Publish total primary energy in result.json after the MVP (renovisorissues #28)
description: Frontend ask: https://jugit.fz-juelich.de/iek-3/groups/urbanmodels/renovisorissues/-/work_items/28. result.json has final energy only; the frontend wants primary energy per carrier with the country's primary-energy factors and provenance, or a decision that HiSim never publishes it. WAITING FOR HUMAN APPROVAL before any work (opened by another agent).

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Decided with Noah 2026-09-23: NOT in the MVP; the frontend hides the figure until then. When built: TOTAL primary energy (renewable included, the Irish DEAP convention), no credit for exported PV (only energy bought, like emissions_in_kg_co2_per_year), unit kWh per year for the whole house (e.g. primary_energy_in_kilowatt_hour_per_year), never per m2 so it is not read as a BER. Factors must be reviewed and sourced per carrier and country before shipping (SEAI DEAP manual for IE; no placeholder or MOCKED factor). Likely home: a sourced primary-energy factor beside emission_factor_in_kg_per_kwh in cost_database/energy_prices_<CC>.json, computed per carrier from the cost engine's bought kWh like CO2. Answered on renovisorissues #28.

title: Wire the solar thermal collector into space heating so dhw_and_space_heating is simulated
description:
Source: hisim-bc02 (owner request 2026-09-26): every entry of hisim/renovisor/not_implemented_yet.yaml names the bead that would let it be deleted.

Entries: path house.solar_thermal_system.supplies (except dhw_only), measure solar_thermal_system.supplies=dhw_and_space_heating (note: The collector is wired to the hot-water storage only; modelled as dhw_only). Found for hisim-l56w: both solar-thermal twins (household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer.grouped, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.grouped) wire SolarThermalSystem and its controller to the SimpleDHWStorage only, and their grouping has no variant or group for a space-heating connection; the component's default connections and its controller read SimpleDHWStorage alone. Needs a controller that can feed SimpleHotWaterStorage (its secondary-generator inputs), a setup that records it, a variant in the twins, and the translator selecting it; dhw_only then becomes used.

title: Add an evacuated-tube solar thermal collector preset
description:
Source: hisim-bc02 (owner request 2026-09-26): every entry of hisim/renovisor/not_implemented_yet.yaml names the bead that would let it be deleted.

Entry: path house.solar_thermal_system.collector_type (except flat_plate; note: No evacuated-tube preset; modelled as flat_plate). SolarThermalSystemConfig offers preset_flat_plate only. Add an evacuated-tube preset (collector efficiency curve) and select it from the leaf; flat_plate then becomes used.

title: Add a liquefied petroleum gas fuel so LPG boilers stop running as natural gas
description:
Source: hisim-bc02 (owner request 2026-09-26): every entry of hisim/renovisor/not_implemented_yet.yaml names the bead that would let it be deleted.

Entries: path house.heating.type_of_system (its conventional_lpg_heating and condensing_lpg_heating values; the same entry also covers ground-source and hybrid, hisim-ztt7 and hisim-epc.20), measures heating_system.type_of_system=conventional_lpg_heating and =condensing_lpg_heating (note: No LPG fuel in HiSim; modelled as gas). Needs an LPG fuel entry (emission factor, price) and a generic_boiler preset, as hisim-epc.19 does for HVO.

title: The staged engine shares one provenance ledger across stages and writes cost_provenance.json
description: Source: renovisorissues #52 investigation, owner decision 2026-09-26. economics-backend-spec.md §2.3 lists cost_provenance.json as an artifact of every economics job, but python -m hisim.economics staged writes none. Each stage is evaluated with a fresh ledger (staged.py ~448, evaluator.py ~975-1010) and the plan result reuses per_stage[0].ledger (staged.py ~1352), so the spliced entries of stages >= 1 carry provenance ids from another ledger. Pass one shared ledger to every stage's evaluate and have staged write it as cost_provenance.json; test that every provenance id in economics_result.json resolves in it. Needed before the #52 stated energy prices can cite their REQUEST provenance in a file.
close_reason: One ProvenanceLedger is shared by the reference, every stage and the spliced plan (StagedEvaluator.evaluate passes it to each stage, _aggregate carries it, StagedResult.ledger exposes it); the staged CLI writes it as cost_provenance.json beside --out via the new exports.write_provenance_ledgers (same format as an ordinary run). Tests in test_staged.py (TestOnePlanOneLedger) and test_staged_cli.py; no golden or schema change.

title: Refuse an empty HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES and treat a single cache_directories string as one directory
description:
From the PR #795 review (findings about the cache-directory code of #792, merged on main). Owner decision 2026-09-24: a separate small PR against main.
1. hisim/renovisor/simulation.py ~150-161: HISIM_CACHE_DIRECTORIES set to a separator-only value (':' or '::') filters to an empty list and then directories[0] raises a raw IndexError; refuse it by name like the relative-path case.
2. hisim/simulationparameters.py ~99: SimulationParameters(cache_directories='/data/cache') does list(...) and splits the path into one-letter directories (also from a *.simulation.yaml with a scalar); accept a single string as one directory, and check every entry is absolute where the list is built (the explicit cache_directory argument and CacheLocations are not checked today).
Not in scope (review noise or refactors): duplicated HISIM_CACHE_DIR override logic, the second environment variable, os.access as root, the skipped read-only-seed tests under root, the manifest test name.

title: Compute the three mocked RenoVisor KPIs instead of publishing HiSim's placeholders
description:
Three fields of result.json's `kpis` block are still MOCKED constants rather than computed:
`disruption_days_by_level` ({none: 6, minor: 12, moderate: 5, major: 0}), `indoor_air_quality` (3)
and `thermal_insulation_effect` (3), both of the last two on the contract's shared Rating 1..5.
Since 2026-09-25 they are HiSim's own placeholders in `hisim/renovisor/kpis.py` `MockedKpis`
(decision A12), no longer read from the contract's openapi.yaml, which HiSim stopped vendoring
(hisim-4p3n); the values are the contract's own examples.

Replace each by a computed value, or by an absent field with its reason (R8), and delete its row of
`MockedKpis`:
- disruption_days_by_level: from the package's measures (per-measure duration and disruption level,
  e.g. a table per catalogue id), which needs a source for the durations.
- indoor_air_quality: e.g. from the ventilation and air-tightness state of the renovated house and
  the simulated humidity/CO2 if HiSim ever models it; otherwise absent.
- thermal_insulation_effect: e.g. graded from the envelope's mean U-value (H_T') before and after
  the package, on Rating 1..5, like the comfort grades (GradeScale in constants.py).
The energy_label stays null by decision (no BER/DEAP procedure).

title: Cost module data and sources
Move the meters' >1 maintenance rates into fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 1

The legacy capex dict has meter maintenance rates above 1: `ELECTRICITY_METER: 2.4` and
`GAS_METER: 1.8` in DE/2024, i.e. 240 % and 180 % of investment per year. They encode absolute
yearly fees, not rates. They were migrated 1:1 into `devices_DE.json` for parity, but they
violate the sanity range a maintenance rate should have.

The new schema has `fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year` for exactly this. A data PR should
move 240 EUR/a resp. 360 EUR/a there and zero the rate -- a deliberate, visible KPI delta.

The AT entries (0.2 / 0.15) look like the same confusion with different magnitudes (a
"20 EUR/month" comment against a 0.2 rate).

Item 25 records that the new AI-estimate entries for 2026/2035 already put the metering fee in
the right field, so this closes the pre-2026 rows.

Done when: the meter rows carry the fee in `fixed_operation_cost_in_euro_per_year`, the rate is
zero, and the KPI delta is blessed deliberately.

title: Replace the rough per-m2 AI estimates for envelope embodied CO2
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 12, "Still open"; roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md section 11 F5

The envelope embodied CO2 values of the thirteen envelope `ComponentType`s are rough per-m2 AI
estimates.

Related open question from the RenoVisor side (challenges.md F5): embodied CO2 of the Irish
example is negative (-2 224 kg) because the materials dump gives wood fibre -174.8 kg CO2-eq./m3
with biogenic storage netted in at A1-A3. The question to the materials team -- does
`embodied_co2_in_kg` want storage netted in or reported separately (the dump has both columns)? --
has to be answered before the numbers mean anything.

Done when: the thirteen envelope classes carry sourced embodied-CO2 values and the biogenic-
storage convention is stated.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP; every figure it touches is marked as an estimate in the provenance file. Labelled human: data sourcing by a person.

title: Set energy_related_cost_share from reviewed data instead of shipping 1.0 everywhere
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 12 decision (a), and item 32 note (a)

`energy_related_cost_share` is implemented as the coupled-cost (Ohnehin-Kosten) mechanism but
shipped as 1.0 everywhere -- user-acknowledged as "a bit of a hack, but good enough to start".
The credit logic is tested via scenario overlays and activates the moment reviewed shares land in
the data.

Why it matters, from item 32: with the interim 1.0, a like-for-like envelope credit equals nearly
the full measure cost, so the "vs doing nothing" frame is only as honest as that share. In the
German worked example this produces the year-2 spike of 58 kEUR of ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT.

Done when: reviewed shares per envelope measure land in the data and the 1.0 default is gone or
documented as the fallback for unreviewed entries.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-20: post-MVP; every figure it touches is marked as an estimate in the provenance file. Labelled human: data sourcing by a person.

title: Close the fourteen PRICED component classes that no cost facts source can price
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md 34 (2026-09-08, stack part 8/8 review)

Fourteen component classes declare `cost_relevance = CostRelevance.PRICED` while nothing can
produce `ComponentCostFacts` for them -- no `get_cost_facts()` of their own and no entry in
`adapter.FactsExtractors.BY_CLASS_NAME`. Each fails `Simulator.check_cost_declarations` before
the first timestep of any run that asks for lifecycle costs, and would fail the postprocessing D7
check if it got that far. Closing one means two things: a `devices_<COUNTRY>.json` row with real
sources in `sources.json` for the device type it is priced against, and an adapter entry (or a
hook) mapping its config to that asset class and a size.

Grouped by the device type the cost database lacks:

* CHP -- `advanced_fuel_cell.CHP`, `generic_chp.SimpleCHP`. No CHP device type exists at all.
  This is why `system_setups/dynamic_components.py` fails fast under all options: it wires two
  CHPs and the run is refused before the first timestep.
* Fuel cell -- `generic_fuel_cell.FuelCell` (the reversible cell moved to `obsolete/components/`
  under D-25 on 2026-09-11).
* Electrolyzers other than the migrated one -- `generic_electrolyzer.GenericElectrolyzer`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.AdvancedElectrolyzer`. The `ELECTROLYZER` device type now
  exists, so these two need an adapter entry each -- but only after someone checks that their
  configs state a rating in kW and that an industrial PEM price is the right one.
* Hydrogen storage -- `generic_hydrogen_storage.GenericHydrogenStorage`,
  `generic_electrolyzer_and_h2_storage.HydrogenStorage`. No hydrogen-storage device type.
* Mobility -- `generic_car.Car`, `advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery`. No car or car-battery
  device type; the stationary `BATTERY` entry is not a vehicle pack.
* Wind -- `generic_windturbine.Windturbine`. No wind device type.
* Air conditioning -- `air_conditioner.AirConditioner`, `simple_air_conditioner.SimpleAirConditioner`.
  No air-conditioner device type.
* `simple_heat_source.SimpleHeatSource` -- a case of its own. Its config declares its own
  `investment_costs_in_euro`, `lifetime_in_years` and `device_co2_footprint_in_kg`, so it needs
  no database row; what it lacks is an asset class, because `SimpleHeatSourceType` says how the
  source behaves (constant power / constant temperature / brine) and never which fuel it burns.
  Deliberately left without an adapter entry rather than mapped by guess.

A class scan finds a fifteenth, `simple_water_storage.SimpleWaterStorage`, excluded because it is
an abstract base that is never instantiated.

Done when: every PRICED class has a facts source, or its declaration changes.

comments.author: noah
comments.text: MVP scope (2026-09-20): only the mobility pair matters for RenoVisor — household_heatpump_car_building_sizer wires generic_car.Car and advanced_ev_battery_bslib.CarBattery, so a request with an electric_vehicle block cannot run COMPUTE_LIFECYCLE_COSTS today. Close those two first (car and car-battery device rows for IE with sources, adapter entries); the CHP, fuel cell, electrolyzer, hydrogen, wind and air-conditioner classes are outside the MVP.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-23, decided with Noah: out of the MVP. RenoVisor never selects a twin with an unpriceable class: the car twin and the air-conditioner twin are the only ones, and an EV and an air conditioner are not_implemented_yet (D-C). tests/renovisor/test_twin_cost_declarations.py now fails when a twin BaseFiles can select has a class check_cost_declarations would refuse, and fails once the car pair or the air conditioner gains a facts source. The car pair's pricing moves to hisim-4g9.8 as a question.

title: Settle who curates the subsidy catalogues and the localized question texts
description:
Source: cost_spec.md section 11, Phase 4 questions Q8, Q31, Q32 and Q33

Q8 -- catalogue curation process: who verifies scheme files and how often? Schemes change
quarterly. Proposal: `catalog_snapshot_date` per file, a CI check that warns when older than 12
months, and scheme files carrying `legal_basis` + `url` for auditability. Scope v1 to DE + AT,
add FR/IT on demand. (IE has since been added as an AI placeholder -- see the IE.json review
issue.)

Q31 -- question catalog curation (section 5.7): who writes and reviews the localized question
texts? The wording is user-facing and legally sensitive ("Denkmalschutz" vs "erhaltenswerte
Bausubstanz" are different legal categories a layperson may conflate). Which languages ship in
v1? Proposal: de + en.

Q32 -- questionnaire default posture (section 5.7): start with zero questions and progressively
disclose via the optimistic upper bound (proposal), or ask the full computed question set upfront
in the RenoVisor flow? Affects the frontend UX contract, not the engine.

Q33 -- heritage scope: is `heritage_status` plus condition-level relaxations enough (proposal),
or do v1 studies need dedicated heritage programs (e.g. section 7i EStG monument depreciation) as
their own benefit kind? The tax-credit payout profile already exists, so this is likely catalog
data, not engine work.

title: Replace the placeholder Irish factors in the legacy emission and price table
description:
Source: roadmap/renovisor/challenges.md section 11 F2 and its revision of 2026-09-19;
/home/renovisor-api-contract/specs/todos.md H1 (decided `[-]`: keep the placeholders)

The legacy KPI path has emission and price factors for DE and AT only
(`hisim/components/configuration.py`, `EmissionFactorsAndCostsForFuelsConfig`). Rather than
leaving `SimulationParameters.country` at DE -- a shim that would be rediscovered in three months
as "the country setting does nothing" -- Ireland is registered as a placeholder with every number
set to -1 000 000 000 (`PlaceholderCountryFactors`). A run with `country = "IE"` completes, and
every legacy cost or CO2 KPI of an Irish run is visibly absurd until sourced Irish rows replace
the block. Verified: the KPI path ran, "Costs of grid electricity" = -1.2e10 EUR for one January
day.

The owner's H1 decision of 2026-09-19 was (a) -- keep the placeholders, correct the spec text --
with the closing line: "Sourced Irish rows in `hisim/components/configuration.py` replace the
placeholder block when they exist." The payload reads none of those KPIs: emissions come from the
lifecycle engine's Irish factors, and energy demand and self-sufficiency do not depend on the
tables.

Done when: sourced Irish emission and price factors (SEAI / CRU) replace `PlaceholderCountryFactors`
and `mapping_report.translator.legacy_factors` stops saying "placeholder".

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-19 (shared todos H1): keep the -1e9 sentinel placeholders on purpose; money for RenoVisor comes from the lifecycle engine, so the legacy table is only what all_kpis.json shows. Priority lowered to P3; the item is data sourcing, not a blocker.

title: Review the ENERGY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM investment migrated as an absolute euro amount
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 2

The legacy `ENERGY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM` investment comment says "EUR/kW" but the key is absolute
EUR (`investment_costs_in_euro: 3500`). It was migrated as absolute (`per_unit = null`).

Done when: someone decides which the 3500 is and the row says so, with a source.

title: Correct the DE/2018 diesel price of 128.90 EUR per litre in the migrated data
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 3

`opex_techno_economic_parameters` mixes carriers and units (oil in EUR/l, pellets in EUR/t) and
prices diesel at `128.90` EUR/l for DE/2018 -- an obvious typo for 1.2890. It was migrated 1:1
for parity; the DE/2018 diesel price should be corrected in a data PR.

Done when: the row reads 1.2890 EUR/l with its source, and whatever KPI it moves is blessed.

title: Reclassify every migrated price as net and set its true VAT handling
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md "Spec open questions (section 11)" Q5 and "New issues" 4;
cost_spec.md section 11 Q5 (Phase 3)

Device entries migrated from `configuration.py` carry `vat_rate: 0.19` (DE) / `0.20` (AT) and are
stored as-is from the legacy dicts. The legacy numbers' VAT status is undocumented -- parity
requires using them unchanged -- so the migrated entries are flagged `"price_basis": "AS_LEGACY"`
and the gross-up for FINANCIAL accounting is a no-op for them.

Consequence recorded in item 4: all migrated energy prices and device costs are treated as
household-final prices; `tax_and_levy_share` is filled only where a source exists, otherwise 0
with an EXPERT_ESTIMATE source, so macroeconomic results for migrated data are approximate.

cost_spec section 11 Q5's proposal: store net + `vat_rate` per entry; household perspectives
gross up, macroeconomic uses net directly, VAT-reduction subsidies override the rate. Requires
touching every price entry once during data migration.

Done when: each entry is classified as net or gross with a source, `price_basis: AS_LEGACY` is
gone, and `tax_and_levy_share` is sourced.

title: Fix the pellet and wood-chip emission factors quoted per kWh against per-ton prices
description:
Source: cost_module_issues.md, "New issues found during implementation" 24

The legacy dicts price pellets and wood chips per ton but state their emission factors per kWh.
The migration kept both as-is, so for these two carriers the engine multiplies tons by a per-kWh
factor -- understating CO2 by a factor of a few thousand.

The new AI-estimate entries (2026/2035) carry per-ton factors (pellets ~175 kg/t, wood chips

title: Part-load run fraction above a step-length threshold: the threshold, the memoryless part-load rule and the boiler
description:
Source: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §2, §4, §5 (owner, 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-10).

Above a step-length threshold (SimulationParameters.part_load_above_seconds, default 600 s), a device its controller has switched on runs only the fraction of the step (PLR) that ends its store at the controller's target. The averaged flow enters the store's node as a constant inflow; the controllers' on/off and mode decisions and MixedNode.step are unchanged; at and below the threshold the ratio is exactly 1 while running and 0 while off, so 60 s results and goldens stay bit-identical.

Design (owner, 2026-10-10, replacing the pass-counting search): hisim/part_load.py holds a pure memoryless rule, PartLoadRule.next_part_load_ratio: r_next = r_run (T_aim - T_start) / (T_end - T_start), clamped to [0, 1], T_aim the middle of the 0.05 K band above the target; inside the band r_run is kept; a store at or above its target gives 0, an end at or below the start (draw dominates) gives 1, a device that ran nothing below the target gives 1. Each device publishes the ratio it ran with (Units.FRACTION) and its controller reads it; the simulator's plain iteration solves the rule, with no acceleration and no controller state; under force_convergence the controller publishes the ratio run. PartLoadControl (controller part) and PartLoadCommand (device part) are stateless. GenericBoilerController commands the boiler's hot-water fraction (every fuel) and publishes its target; GenericBoiler books the fraction and reports it. SimpleDHWStorage publishes nothing new.

Done when: 60 s golden checks pass unchanged; the gas twin's hot-water heat and gas agree within 1 % at 900 s and 3600 s against 60 s over a full year; forced steps and run time reported.

Open: in the boiler twins the boiler is evaluated between its controller and the tank, so the rule pairs a ratio with the tank's answer to the one before and does not settle (hisim-fxix.16, owner decision).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10, memoryless rule (branches hydronic-part-load to part-load-hds), full year 2021 against 60 s of the same head: gas twin hot-water gas +0.27 % at 900 s and +0.18 % at 3600 s with 1013 and 679 forced steps in the twin's order (the controller pairs a ratio with the tank's answer to the one before, hisim-fxix.16); with the controller moved before the boiler -0.00 % and -0.01 % with 46 and 50 forced steps and 3.42 / 3.89 passes per step. 60 s bit-identical to #914 (gas and gas + solar). Details: roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md §11.

title: Staged document: kept-asset replacement years count from the price basis year, calendar_year from the simulation year
description:
Source: renovisorissues #58 work (worktree agent-e58), 2026-09-26.

The staged document labels year index y as calendar_year = simulation_year + y (2019 + y for the
mockup), but the engine ages every kept register asset at the price basis year
(calculators/context_resolution.py: first_replacement_year = max(1, round(life - (price_basis_year -
installation_year)))). The relative replacement year therefore counts from price_basis_year while
the document says it counts from simulation_year.

Mockup (IE, simulation_year 2019, price_basis_year 2026): the hot-water cylinder is installed 2008
(request) with a 20-year life from the cost database. It is due in 2028, the engine books it at
year index 2 = 2008 + 20 - 2026, and annual[2].calendar_year says 2021. Every kept asset of the
mockup is shifted the same 7 years (boiler 2008+18 -> year 1 = "2020", meters 2018+16 -> year 8 =
"2027").

The same mismatch reaches the staged ageing: StagedEvaluator._staged_inputs registers a subject an
earlier stage bought as installed in simulation_year + from_year_j, and the next stage ages it at
price_basis_year, so it is (price_basis_year - simulation_year) years older than the plan says.

Related: hisim-cyc.16 (whether a weather/price-basis mismatch gets a report note) - this one is a
figure, not a note. Decide which year is the plan's year 0 (price_basis_year, or simulation_year
with ages anchored there) and make calendar_year, the register ages and the staged ageing agree.
Done when the mockup cylinder's replacement year satisfies installation_year + service_life_years -
(year-0 calendar year) on the published document.
close_reason: kept assets age against plan year 0, so calendar_year and replacement years agree (feat/year-zero)

title: Add a CI rule that no module under hisim/ outside hisim/renovisor imports hisim.renovisor
description:
Source: review of hisim/economics for size and maintainability, 2026-09-27 (Claude session with Noah; no document).

Add a quality gate so the rest of HiSim can never import hisim.renovisor again. RenoVisor is the
top layer (a request translator on top of the energy-system format and the economics engine);
nothing below it may depend on it. Today the rule is broken only by hisim/economics (see the
inversion bead this one depends on), and nothing stops it happening again.

Implement it as a base-marked test in the style of tests/test_economics_import_lint.py (parse
every .py file under hisim/ with ast, so function-local imports count like top-level ones), not
a grep:
- walk hisim/**/*.py excluding hisim/renovisor/;
- flag every Import/ImportFrom whose module is hisim.renovisor or starts with hisim.renovisor.,
  and relative imports that resolve into it;
- the failure names file, line and imported module, and says the rule: renovisor sits on top.
Optionally add a fresh-interpreter check like tests/test_energy_system_layering.py (import
hisim.economics.__main__, hisim.hisim_main, hisim.simulator and assert no hisim.renovisor module
was loaded), which also catches imports through importlib.
Tests, system_setups and scripts are out of scope (tests may use renovisor freely). Mention the
rule in the CLAUDE.md RenoVisor paragraph.

Done when: the test runs in the base CI job, passes after the inversion is fixed, and fails on a
deliberately added import.

title: Make self.config precisely typed per component so mypy sees the 300 masked findings
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/json_cleanup.md section 6, "Mypy visibility for config classes
(follow-up to sweep 1)"

Removing the dataclass-wizard's `Any` base revealed about 300 latent typing findings that sweep 1
deliberately re-masked to stay reviewable: LSP-violating `get_cost_capex(config: SpecificConfig)`
overrides (about 75), subclass-field reads and writes on `ConfigBase`-typed slots (about 280),
and a handful of genuine type lies (`my_module_config` holding a dict, the `List[int]` annotation
on `post_processing_options` that actually holds enum members).

The real fix is a generic `Component[TConfig]` so `self.config` is precisely typed per component,
then: delete the checking-only escape hatches on `ConfigBase` (the `__getattr__`/`__setattr__`
and serialization-API stubs), re-enable the `override` error code, and drop
`follow_imports = skip` for `dataclasses_json` -- which restores the injected-API stubs problem,
to be solved via a small typing shim or upstream stubs.

Related, and unblocked by the same change: the config-presets findings note that
`Catalog` attribute access is inherently `Any` because a `ClassVar` may not contain a type
variable, so `Catalog` cannot be generic over the config class it serves; a
`__class_getitem__`-based `Catalog[SomeConfig]` declared as a plain class attribute might work
once the `Component[TConfig]` generics sweep lands.

Also named there: `my_sim.my_module_config` holding a dict is one of the type lies -- see the
issue that settles what that attribute may hold.

title: Re-enable pylint's cyclic-import check by moving for_building into the building package
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] pylint's
`cyclic-import` cannot see the difference between a lazy import and a real one"

`SizingContext.for_building` imports the building package inside the method body, which is
invisible to Python's import system but fully visible to pylint's import graph, so prospector
reports the cycle anyway. Worse, it attributes the message to an arbitrary module outside the
cycle (a file under `hisim/inputs/`), so a `# pylint: disable=cyclic-import` at the actual site
does nothing. It is disabled in `.prospector.yml`, matching `pylintrc-critical-only`, which
already disables it.

If the check is ever wanted back, the honest fix is to move `for_building` into the building
package and leave `SizingContext` fact-agnostic.

Done when: either the check is back with the move done, or the disable carries a note saying this
is the reason and the fix.

title: Settle the five open questions of the HPC harness spec
description:
Source: hpc_harnes_spec.md section 17, "Open questions / future"

* Autoscaler: whole-node autoscaling and proactively cancelling running (not just Slurm-PENDING)
  surplus workers are the natural follow-ups.
* Priorities and fairness across multiple submitted batches -- the schema supports `priority` and
  `batch_id`; the policy is TBD.
* Richer output validation -- section 4.8 requires a single success file for `done`; a future
  extension could let a runner check multiple files, sizes or content hashes before the rename.
* Multiple runners per server -- the database is already runner-tagged; confirm whether one
  server should host mixed-runner queues or one runner per server instance.
* Database growth at very large scale -- a `worker_metrics` downsampling policy, and possibly
  moving long-term metrics to a separate rollup database.

Also relevant to the harness, from the declarative plan's P5: the payload becomes an
energy-system string plus simulation parameters and the worker loads from the string, which
changes what a job record has to carry.

title: Check autodoc member visibility for the building package when the Sphinx docs are next built
description:
Source: roadmap/json_development/building_cleanup_findings.md, item 15

`docs/api/hisim.components.building.rst` uses `automodule` on the package, and the classes are
now imported names in `__init__` (listed in `__all__`). The docs build is not a CI gate, so this
was left unchanged -- worth a look whenever the Sphinx docs are next built, because `automodule`
on a package whose classes are re-exports can silently document nothing.

Done when: the docs build is checked and either the members appear or the `.rst` names them.

title: Explain the sporadic errors of test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`test_building_information_for_every_tabula_code` errors sporadically when anything else runs in
the repo concurrently"

Three `pytest -m base` runs that overlapped with other work in the same checkout (a scenario-JSON
regeneration, a parallel pytest invocation, live source edits) each produced one or two
collection/setup ERRORs on random TABULA parametrizations of this test; the identical suite run
sequentially passes twice with zero errors, and every errored parametrization passes in
isolation. Plausibly contention around a shared file (`logs/`, `results/`, or the class-scope
TABULA CSV cache being rebuilt while another process imports).

Harmless for CI, which runs one suite per checkout, but worth knowing before blaming a branch for
a red local run -- and worth a look if it ever appears in CI.

needs-triage: no owner and a named reason not to chase it. It is the same class of hazard as the
stale-cache one and the `--scan-all` non-determinism; whoever does the cache-injection work
(Rust Tier 3) should check whether it disappears.

title: Add a syntax gate to any future mechanical call-site rewriting sweep
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction] Mechanical call-site
rewriting needs a syntax gate, not a diff review" and "[bug] Import-insertion tooling corrupted
one setup"

Converting the 72 `get_default_german_single_family_home` call sites with a
keyword-args-to-field-assignments script silently produced one wrecked file: the setup whose last
keyword argument ended `...,)` on the same line ran the "read until the closing paren" loop past
the end of the call and rewrote nine following statements into attribute assignments.
`compileall` over the touched trees caught it instantly.

The same shape bit once before: inserting a `SizingContext` import after
"from hisim.simulator import SimulationParameters" broke
`household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer.py`, whose import line continued with
", Simulator". Textual import insertion needs full-line anchors.

Any future sweep of this shape should run a parse gate per file, not per tree.

Done when: the rule is written where a sweep author will read it (a script helper that does the
per-file `compileall`, or a line in the repository's own conventions).

title: Keep ConfigBase annotations importable at runtime from hisim/config/base.py
description:
Source: roadmap/declarative_energy_systems/random_findings.md, "[friction]
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` needed a home on `ConfigBase`" ("third occurrence of the pattern; worth a
rule"), with the two earlier occurrences in the same document

The pattern, hit three times from three directions: a name that is not importable at runtime from
`hisim/config/base.py` must not appear in a `ConfigBase` annotation, because `dataclasses_json`
evaluates those annotations from every subclass's module.

The three occurrences: `Sizable = Union[T, _AutoSize, "SizingLaw"]` as a string forward reference
above the class made `get_type_hints` fail with `NameError` in every config module that did not
itself import `SizingLaw`, fixed by defining the alias below the class with a real reference;
`SIZING_CONTRIBUTIONS` had to be declared on `ConfigBase` for mypy, with its element type kept as
`Any`, because naming `FactContribution` would either invert the package layering or leave a
`TYPE_CHECKING`-only forward reference; and the general lesson for shared aliases.

Done when: the rule is stated where a config author will read it -- the `hisim/config/` package
docstring is the natural place, since it is where the layering rule already lives.

title: Clean up and unify the output files of a run: result.json, all_kpis.json and the rest
description:
Source: owner request 2026-09-25 ('result.json vs all_kpis.json is a mess').

A RenoVisor job writes several overlapping files, each with its own naming, units and provenance rules:
- all_kpis.json (postprocessing): flat KPI names with values baked into the names (setpoints, '1.0 K', '26.0 Celsius'), units such as °C*h, and legacy cost leaves that must not be read (renovisorissues #16).
- result.json (hisim/renovisor/result.py, kpis.py): the payload, with its own field names (energy_demand_in_kilowatt_hour_per_year, comfort ratings), each value wrapped with provenance/source strings that quote all_kpis.json names.
- economics_result.json (staged document) and economic_inputs.json (bridge), plus the lifecycle exports.
- mapping_report.json, problems.json, translator_error.json, and the capability document's results rows (KpiSchema, CostSchema) that describe the payload.
The same figure can appear in two files under two names and units (e.g. degree-hours K*h vs °C*h; energy in kWh vs Wh), and a reader cannot tell which file owns it.

Goal: one documented output layout. Decide which file owns each figure (simulation KPIs vs the RenoVisor payload vs economics), give every figure one name and one unit convention (_in_<unit>, as the contract now uses), stop duplicating values across files (reference instead), drop or quarantine the legacy cost leaves of all_kpis.json, and keep the capability document's result rows generated from that single description. Include a migration note for the backend and frontend (renovisorissues heads-up) and the golden references (all_kpis.json keys are what the golden check compares).

Start with an inventory: every file a RenoVisor run writes, its writer, its readers (backend, frontend, goldens, tests), and every figure it carries.

title: Remove the retired legacy_flat_subsidy_share field from the device tables, loader, validation and reports
description: Follow-up of the PR #799 review (owner decision 2026-09-24): the §10.1 flat subsidy shim is retired in behaviour -- with no catalogue nothing is booked on any path -- but the legacy_flat_subsidy_share field was kept in hisim/cost_database/devices_{DE,IE,AT}.json (about 150 lines) and in the loader, validation and catalog_entries, documented as retired. Remove it everywhere in its own PR (not in the bottom of the stack), with the data files, the dataclass field, validation, and any report text.

title: An omitted applicant.role defaults to owner_occupier without a defaulted line in the mapping report
description: Found by the tier-1 path verifier after hisim-qzyv (probe field:applicant.role=owner_occupier: no_effect against the anchor, 'applicant.role: no line there'). The request schema says an omitted role defaults to owner_occupier, and EconomicContextBuilder._subsidy_context leaves the profile's owner-occupier default standing, but EconomicContextBuilder.stated_leaves only reports applicant keys the request states, so the anchor's mapping report carries no line for applicant.role at all. The contract's rule is that the backend reports every default: a request without a role should get a 'defaulted' line for applicant.role (owner_occupier). The other applicant keys stay undetermined when omitted (a question, not a default), so no line is right for them.
close_reason: An omitted applicant.role now yields a defaulted line (owner_occupier, the profile's own actor, with a note citing the schema default) from EconomicContextBuilder._subsidy_context. No other applicant key has an engine default (main_residence is schema-required; the rest stay None = undetermined), so none gets a line. Tested in test_economics_context and test_translate.

title: Review the wood-fuel emission factors against one stated accounting
description: From the PR #794 review (owner decision 2026-09-24: a bead, not in #794). title: Stop the heat pump's space-heating controller from staying off below a low flow setpoint
description:
Found 2026-09-23 while computing comfort grades (hisim-sska) on the RenoVisor mockup package, full year 2019, IE: air/water hplib + floor heating + insulation.

MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerSpaceHeating (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2658-2686) switches on only when the buffer water is below set_heating_flow_temperature - lower_temperature_offset_for_state_conditions_in_celsius (5.0) and off above flow + upper offset (5.0). With floor heating in mild weather the HeatDistributionController asks for a flow of ~23.4 C, so the switch-on point is ~18.4 C; the buffer sits at room temperature (~18.6 C) and never gets there. The pump stays off while the distribution is on and the room sits at 18.6-19.5 C against a 21 C setpoint.

Evidence: June-August 4516 quarter-hours with room < 20.5 C, of which 4223 with SH controller off, HDS state on, window closed. 1944 of the year's 2503 K*h below setpoint fall in June-September at outdoor > 10 C. Heat delivered 26 233 kWh vs 29 425 kWh theoretical demand (-11%). The gas-boiler baseline of the same house: 331 K*h.

Consequence: every heat-pump plan with a low flow setpoint under-delivers heat, so its electricity, bills, CO2 and LCOH are too low -- the economics comparison favours the heat pump by roughly that much. Owner interview on the fix pending.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/heat-pump-switch-on-floor (decided with Noah 2026-09-23: never switch on below the room setpoint, component-wide). RenoVisor mockup package, full year IE: heat delivered 26 233 -> 26 877 kWh against 29 425 -> 27 530 kWh demand (-11% -> -2.4%), K*h below 21 C 2503 -> 729 (the rest is on/off ripple: 57 K*h beyond 1 K), grid electricity 8 490 -> 8 619 kWh. HiSim's heat-pump twin (Aachen, 2021, predefined profile): 230.5 -> 228.3 K*h, 2 253 -> 2 255 kWh.

title: Staged splice: a later stage's anyway-cost credit is neither shifted to its stage nor kept when another stage is active in its year
description: Found while fixing hisim-4uv9 (PR #841 review fixes, 2026-09-27). resolve_replaced_asset books the ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT at credit_year = round(remaining life), a year of the stage's own evaluation. StagedCategories.STAGE_START lists ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT but the splice takes STAGE_START entries only when entry.year == 0 (_spliced_entry), so a credit at year r > 0 falls to the operating branch: kept only if the replacing stage is active in plan year r, unshifted by from_year_k. Probe: stage 1 (f=3) buys a heat pump, stage 3 (f=8) replaces it with a same-class subject, anyway_threshold_years 5 -> stage 3's own evaluation books the credit at year 5 (age 5, remaining 5; hisim-4uv9), and the plan timeline drops it (stage 1 is active in year 5). economics-hisim-spec §1 item 2 says the credit is booked in from_year_k. The same applies to a register asset a later stage replaces (its age is measured at plan year 0, so its credit year is in plan years and survives only when that stage is active then). Decide: book the credit at from_year_k + r (the year the avoided replacement would have fallen) or at from_year_k, and pin with a hand-computed test.
close_reason: Obsolete since #855: the staged engine books no anyway-cost credit (book_anyway_credit=False), and the levy basis takes the credit amount, not its timeline year; tests/economics/test_staged.py pins no ANYWAY_COST_CREDIT flow

title: Check the SCOP calibration's mean-outlet anchors against measured heat pump data
description:
Source: decision with Noah, 2026-09-23, while implementing hisim-4g9.15 ("go with the mean outlet
anchors, but make a bead that we need to check this against real data").

What was decided without data: when a heat pump's datasheet states both EN 14825 SCOPs (W35 and
W55), ScopCalibration scales hplib's COP by a factor that is linear in the outlet temperature
between two anchors and constant outside them. The anchors are the heat-weighted mean outlets of
the two EN 14825 rating lines (28.9 C for W35, 40.7 C for W55), and both factors are solved so the
calibrated fit rates exactly at the stated SCOPs. The alternative, anchors at the nominal 35 / 55 C,
was rejected because it is ill-conditioned: wide pairs (e.g. 5.5 / 3.0) drove the 55 C factor to
0.46 (air) and 0.19 (brine), which domestic hot water at 55 C would inherit. The comparison table
over nine realistic pairs is in the 2026-09-23 session and summarised in the commit that adds
ScopCalibration.

Nothing checks that the calibrated machine behaves like the real one away from the two ratings.
In particular: (1) the factor at 45-55 C outlets (radiator houses, DHW) is an extrapolation;
(2) hplib's Generic air/water fit gives COP 1.41 at A-7/W52 where real units reach about 2.5, a
curve-shape error a factor per outlet temperature cannot fix; (3) the Generic brine/water fit's
W35/W55 spread (4.85 vs 4.02) is narrower than real datasheets, so every realistic brine pair
lands in the regime where the anchor choice matters.

Wanted: take several real units with published EN 14825 data (both SCOPs plus COPs at the
standard rating points A7/W35, A2/W35, A-7/W35, A7/W55, A-7/W55, A-7/W52, ideally from the
hplib database's own rows or a Keymark / HP Keymark certificate), calibrate the Generic fit to
their two SCOPs, and compare the calibrated COP with the stated one at each rating point. Report
the error per point for both anchor schemes, and for "calibrate a matched hplib database row
instead of Generic".

Done when: the error table exists, and the anchor choice is either confirmed or changed with the
data behind it; if the A-7 shape error dominates, a follow-up for the fit shape is filed.

title: CI rule: no Python file over 500 lines of source code (comments excluded); split larger files
description:
Owner request (cmf, 2026-09-27): a CI rule that no Python file may hold more than 500 lines of actual source code; anything larger is split into several files (modules / a package).

**Counting.** A line counts when it carries a code token. Comment-only lines and blank lines don't count. Count with `tokenize`, not a regex, so a `#` inside a string still counts as code. Open question for the owner: do docstrings count as code? (Tokenize treats them as strings, so today they count.)

**Today (2026-09-27, main e51dfca3, docstrings counted):** 145 of 662 files are over the limit (hisim 80, tests 52, scripts 8, obsolete 5). The worst:
- `hisim/economics/views.py`: 5051
- `hisim/components/more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py`: 2798
- `hisim/economics/staged.py`: 2371
- `report_prose.py`: 2125
- `renovisor/capabilities.py`: 2074
- `renovisor/translate.py`: 2046

**Rollout (proposal):** a ratchet, so CI stays green from day one.
- `scripts/check_file_size.py` (or a flake8 plugin) plus an allowlist file, e.g. `.github/file_size_allowlist.txt`, holding each current offender and its count.
- CI fails on:
  - a new file over 500;
  - an allowlisted file that grows;
  - a stale allowlist entry (the file is now ≤500 or was deleted, so it must leave the list).
- Wire it into `quality.yml` as a new job (it's cheap).
- Decide the scope: `hisim/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `system_setups/`. Exclude `obsolete/`? Generated files?
- Then split the offenders, one bead per file or per package, starting with the economics and renovisor giants. Each split keeps imports stable: re-export from the old module, or update the call sites.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decisions (cmf, 2026-09-27): docstrings do NOT count as code (module/class/function docstrings excluded, like comments and blank lines); obsolete/ is out of scope. Recount on main with that rule: 74 of 628 files over 500 (hisim 44, tests 27, scripts 3). Largest: economics/views.py 2727, more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py 2381, economics/report_prose.py 1920, loadprofilegenerator_utsp_connector.py 1671, kpi_preparation.py 1629, building/building.py 1569.

title: Weather year separate from the calendar year (renovisorissues #57 step 2)
description:
# Weather year separate from the calendar year (renovisorissues #57, step 2)

Status: **decided by cmf on 2026-09-27**. Base: origin/main @ faa88f3b.

## Today
`SimulationParameters.__init__` (hisim/simulationparameters.py) sets `self.year = start_date.year`, which serves as both the calendar and the weather year.

`Weather.build_calculation_inputs` hands `year=C` to `WeatherSeriesInputs`. Every reader in `hisim/components/weather/calculation.py` stamps the file's rows onto C **by position** (`pd.date_range(f"{year}-01-01 …", periods=N)`):

| source | reader | anchor | data year in file | shipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DWD_TRY | read_dwd_try_data | Berlin 00:30, 8760 h | none (MM/DD/HH, MEZ) | Aachen TRY, 15 regions |
| NSRDB | read_nsrdb_data | Berlin 00:30, 8760 h | Year 2019 | 9 cities |
| NSRDB_15MIN | read_nsrdb_15min_data | UTC 00:00, 35040 | Year 2019 | 20 countries (RenoVisor) |
| DWD_10MIN | read_dwd_10min_data | UTC 00:00, 52560 | year 2021 | Aachen |
| DWD_15MIN | read_dwd_15min_data | UTC 00:00, run duration | year 2024 (leap) | Düsseldorf |
| ERA5 | read_era5_data | UTC 00:00, 8760 | year column | none shipped |

Nothing reads the data year. Sun position (`produce_weather_series`: pvlib `get_solarposition`, `get_extra_radiation`) is computed on the C-stamped index, i.e. on the calendar, and PV, the building and solar thermal read it. When C is a leap year, dates after 28 Feb drift by position and `interpolate` pads 31 Dec flat.

## Decisions (cmf, 2026-09-27)
1. **The parameter is `SimulationParameters.weather_year: Optional[int] = None`.** It covers the whole run and is also a `*.simulation.json/.yaml` key, which the loaders already accept through `SimulationParameters(**data)`. `self.year` stays C. Valid range: int, 1900–2100.
2. **Unset = today, byte-identical:** positional stamping, no check, no remap. A mismatch between the file's declared year and C is logged at INFO and noted in the realized record (not a WARNING). This closes hisim-9g2.1.
3. **When set:**
   - The file's rows of year W are selected. The run is refused if W is not in the file (the message names the years that are), and refused on a source with no data year (TRY: pick the file instead).
   - The direct normal irradiance is derived on the W-stamped frame.
   - The rows are then remapped W→C **by same date**, in the source's own fixed-offset clock (UTC, or MEZ = UTC+1 for the Berlin-anchored readers), never Berlin wall time.
   - A 365-day W onto a leap C: 29 Feb is a copy of 28 Feb. A leap W onto a 365-day C: 29 Feb is dropped. W = C is the identity.
   - `interpolate(…, C)` and the resampling are unchanged. The sun stays on C.
4. **Future climates are weather files** (a LocationEnum entry or `WeatherConfig.for_data_file`), never a weather_year value. Revisit a `climate_scenario` parameter when scenario files ship.
5. **Cache keys and records:**
   - `get_unique_key` gets `###weather=W` and `get_unique_key_as_list` a line, **only when set**.
   - `ParameterNormalisation.normalise` and `ParameterFileWriter` write `weather_year` only when set, and `ParameterFileName` gets a `_weatherW` suffix only when set.
   - `WeatherSeriesInputs` gets `weather_year: Optional[int]`.
   - The LPG, car and solar-thermal caches key on W when set.
   - Unset keys and records stay byte-identical.
6. **Economics (PR D):**
   - `EvaluationInputs.weather_year: Optional[int]` is serialized in economic_inputs.json (read with `.get`), filled from the repository value `weather_year_effective` that the weather component publishes: W if set; otherwise the file's single declared year; otherwise None.
   - The staged document echoes it when the stages carry it, else `simulation_year` as today (no change while unset).
   - The staged "same year across stages" check also covers weather_year.
7. **RenoVisor (PR E):** `renovisor/simulation.py` `SimulationSetup.YEAR` splits into `CALENDAR_YEAR = 2019` and `WEATHER_YEAR = 2019`. The numbers are identical; the records gain a `weather_year` line. There is no request key. Later we ask RenoVisor whether they want a calendar year (e.g. = plan_start_year) and a weather choice (typical / extreme / 2045).
8. **Order:** A and B now; C after hisim-9g2.4 (reuse its "resolve a date against the delivered frame" helper and its reader anchor tests; 9g2.4's leap refusal stays for the unset case only); then D and E.

## PRs
- **A, the parameter:**
  - `weather_year` in SimulationParameters, with validation, keys and records only when set.
  - If set, the weather component refuses by name until PR C lands.
  - Tests: .simulation.yaml round trip with and without the key; `get_unique_key()` pinned identical when unset; the realized record is identical when unset.
- **B, declared data years:**
  - `WeatherSourceFiles.data_years(source, path) -> Optional[FrozenSet[int]]`, reading the year column, None for TRY, cached per content hash.
  - `Weather.i_prepare_simulation` publishes `weather_year_effective` and logs the INFO mismatch note, plus a note in the record.
  - Tests: the data_years of every shipped file (NSRDB_15MIN {2019}, DWD_10MIN {2021}, DWD_15MIN {2024}, TRY None); the note is emitted; the series are unchanged. Closes hisim-9g2.1.
- **C, select and remap:**
  - Readers filter by year when W is set; `remap_to_calendar(raw, W, C, clock)`; the refusals.
  - Tests: W = C frame-equal to unset; 365→leap (29 Feb = 28 Feb, 31 Dec real); leap→365; no duplicate or missing hour around the DST dates of W and C; sun series equal for W ≠ C; cold and warm cache equal.
- **D, the economics echo:** as in decision 6.
- **E, RenoVisor internal 2019/2019:** as in decision 7.
- No golden moves while weather_year is unset.

## Side findings (to be filed as beads)
- `read_nsrdb_data` labels UTC NSRDB data as Europe/Berlin, probably a 1 h shift.
- `calculation.interpolate` pads 31 Dec 23:00 of the previous year with 0.0 in every column, a temperature of 0 °C included.
- `read_dwd_10min_data`: the file is named 2021-2022 but holds 365 days.
- `Weather.calc_sun_position` (weather.py ~458) looks unused.

title: Make the water storages conserve the energy their heat generators book
description:
Found while root-causing hisim-4g9.11 (2026-09-27).

`SimpleWaterStorage.calculate_mean_water_temperature_in_water_storage`
(hisim/components/simple_water_storage.py ~375) updates both storages (SimpleDHWStorage and
SimpleHotWaterStorage) as `T_new = (M*T0 + sum m_i*T_i)/(M + sum m_i)`, where `m_i = mdot_i * dt`. This
mixes temperatures by mass, but it does not conserve energy. The heat generator books
`m*c*(T_sup - T0)`: GenericBoiler thermal output, gas demand, and the storage's own
ThermalEnergyFromHeatGenerator output. The vessel, however, gains only `M*c*(T_new - T0) = M/(M+m)` of
that. The rest vanishes, and the vanished share grows with dt and with small lifts, because the boiler
sets `m = P/(c*dT)`.

Measured on the RenoVisor translation of an IE detached house built 1960 (TABULA
IE.N.SFH.04.Gen.ReEx.001.001, mockup-1 envelope, gas, no measures), full year 2019:

| dt | DHW boiler heat | vessel gain | lost | DHW drawn + standby | SH boiler heat | HDS draw |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 900 s | 7680 kWh | 3982 | 48 % | 2854 + 281 | 44778 | 39258 |
| 1800 s | 10015 | | | 2854 + 278 | 48988 | 39271 |
| 3600 s | 14120 | 3630 | 74 % | 2854 + 280 | 57500 | 39290 |

The gas bill therefore depends on the resolution: DHW gas 8.5 / 11.1 / 15.7 MWh and SH gas 61 / 66 / 75
MWh at 900 / 1800 / 3600 s. Even at 900 s the DHW gas is roughly 2.4 times the physical demand. The
median charging step at 3600 s has m/M = 2.9 (the tank volume passes through the boiler about three times
per step).

Every generator that feeds these storages shares this: GenericBoiler, MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLib,
DistrictHeating, ElectricHeating and SolarThermalSystem.

The fix is the physically correct form of the bead's option (1). Make the update energy-conserving, with
`T_new = T0 + sum m_i*(T_i - T0)/M` (or the exact well-mixed solution `1 - exp(-m/M)`, with the generator
booking what the vessel actually took). Cap the per-step delivery so the vessel cannot pass the supply
temperature: `Q_max = M*c*(T_sup - T0)`, i.e. `P_max = M*c*dT/dt`. The generator must be told what was
accepted, or it must compute it itself.

This moves every golden and KPI that includes a SimpleWaterStorage, including at 900 s, so the owner has
to decide on it.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text:
Measured 2026-09-27 (origin/main faa88f3b, full years, per-step balance from hooks on the converged call; scripts and pickles in scratchpad egap/). Balance per storage: R = generator's own booked heat (GenericBoiler ThermalOutputEnergyDhw/Sh; HPLib ThermalEnergyDHW/SH) - booked draw (DHW: m_d*c*(T_warm-T_drain) = -ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW; SH: HeatDistribution ThermalPowerDelivered*dt) - standby (loss_W*dt) - M*c*(T_end-T0). Identity R = sum m_g*c*(T_new-T0) [R_gen] + secondary term [DHW m_d*c*(T_new-T_warm); SH m_h*c*(T_new-T_to_hds)] + booking-vs-flow (HDS inlet, HP c): holds to 1e-14 kWh per step in every run. Return temperature told to the generator = T0 exactly (heat exchanger present in all cases).

Residual R (R_gen) as % of booked heat:
| case | dt | DHW R kWh (%) | DHW R_gen (%) | SH R kWh (%) | SH R_gen (%) |
| RenoVisor mockup baseline (IE.N.SFH.05 gas) | 900 | 4747 (60) | 3566 (45) | 4459 (9.5) | 3612 (7.7) |
| RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib) | 900 | 5667 (66) | 5104 (59) | 5541 (17) | 5050 (15) |
| household_gas_building_sizer (DE) | 300 | 1565 (33) | 451 (9.6) | 361 (2.8) | 273 (2.1) |
| same | 900 | 2419 (44) | 1361 (25) | 855 (6.5) | 633 (4.8) |
| same | 3600 | 5537 (64) | 4545 (52) | 2572 (17) | 1771 (12) |
R_gen -> 0 roughly linearly in dt. The DHW secondary term (~1.0-1.2 MWh/yr, dt-independent) is a second defect: the draw takes m_d at tank temperature T_new but books it at 40 C (no mixing valve), so it survives dt -> 0.

KPI first order (residual / per-step efficiency or COP): gas baseline -8.7 MWh gas (R_gen only) to -11.4 MWh (full R) of 73.4 MWh = -11.8..-15.5 %; at 0.11 EUR/kWh -950..-1250 EUR/a; CO2 -1.7..-2.3 t of 15.5 t/a. HP package: -2.2..-2.5 MWh of 8.2 MWh HP electricity (-27..-30 %), upper bound -780..-870 EUR/a at 0.35, -0.62..-0.69 t CO2 of 2.41 (grid share <1 because of PV).

Side findings: the mockup baseline crashes at 1800 and 3600 s (DHW > 90 C raised on a non-converged iterate; hisim-4g9.11) and cannot run at 300/600 s (weather array one/two short; new hisim-j2mh).

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Owner decision (cmf, 2026-09-27): fix with option B (vessel updates on booked energy: T_new = T0 + (Q_gen - Q_draw - loss)/(M c), delivery capped at M c (T_supply - T0), accepted heat fed back to every generator) plus the DHW mixing valve (m_hot = m_d (T_warm - T_cold)/(T_tank - T_cold)). Option A evaluated separately. Announce on renovisorissues when the fix lands.
