title: Enforce the boiler controller's minimum runtime and resting time, and stop them rounding to zero at coarse timesteps
description:
Found while root-causing hisim-4g9.11 (2026-09-27). hisim/components/generic_boiler.py:

1. `GenericBoilerControllerState.activate()` / `deactivate()` are never called, so `activation_time_step`
   and `deactivation_time_step` stay 0 forever. `enforce_minimum_run_and_idle_times` therefore never
   enforces a minimum runtime or resting time after the start of the simulation. The only effect is a
   start-up lockout: the controller is forced OFF for timesteps < minimum_resting_time_in_timesteps.
2. `minimum_*_in_timesteps = int(seconds / seconds_per_timestep)` rounds down. The default 1800 s
   becomes 2 steps at 900 s, 1 at 1800 s and 0 at 3600 s. The start-up lockout therefore vanishes at
   hourly resolution. This is exactly what let the controller act on the zero-initialised storage
   temperature at timestep 0 in hisim-4g9.11 (the 3600 s crash; 900/1800 s were protected by the
   lockout). The same `seconds / dt` conversion exists in generic_chp/controller.py:346 and
   generic_heat_pump.py:455.
3. Related: in DHW or SH mode the boiler's supply temperature is `temperature_delta + T_in`, where
   `temperature_delta` is the controller's output from the previous iteration and `T_in` is the storage's
   current output. At timestep 0, `stsv` starts at zero, so the first iterate gets a 70 K lift on top of
   60 degC, i.e. a 130 degC supply. The loop corrects it; an output of target supply temperature instead
   of a delta would not have the mismatch.

Fixing (1) or rounding (2) up changes results at 900 s, so the owner has to decide on it.

title: Coal and peat as a fuel carrier, so a solid-fuel house can be simulated and its replacement priced (renovisorissues #76)
description:
Since PR #865 a request whose house.heating.type_of_system is solid_fuel_heating is refused by name (heating.type_of_system.unsupported), also when a heating_system measure replaces the boiler (owner decision 2026-09-29). Before, it ran on the pellet twin and was priced as wood chips, so fuel, cost and CO2 were a wood boiler's; coal/peat CO2 per kWh is many times wood's, which understated exactly the saving these houses are interesting for.

Needed: a coal/peat carrier (fuel price, CO2 factor, sources) in the economics data, a boiler twin that burns it (or the pellet/wood-chip boiler parametrised with the carrier), a solid-fuel boiler asset class (price, lifetime) for the existing-asset register, then remove SOLID_FUEL_HEATING from SemanticChecks.UNSUPPORTED_GENERATORS and put it back into BaseFiles.BY_GENERATOR and GeneratorAssets.BY_GENERATOR.

title: Stop publishing hand-copied measure-option bounds that contradict the request schema
description: Source: PR #807 review follow-up (the fix agent's finding, 2026-09-24). ProbeSet.OPTION_BOUNDS is published as each measure option's minimum/maximum (capabilities.Aggregation._options) and is hand-copied from the house fields each option writes into; the request schema declares no bounds on options ($defs.measure.options is a free anyOf), so nothing can be derived. Three entries contradict the fields they copy: u_value_in_watt_per_m2_per_kelvin publishes minimum 0.1 where the target is exclusiveMinimum 0; number publishes (1, 2) where the target is the enum [1, 2]; installation_year borrows construction_year's range. Decide: an explicit option -> target-field map so option bounds are read from the target field's schema bounds (and enums as values[]), or bounds declared in measures.yaml by the contract owner (GitLab ask), or stop publishing option bounds.

title: Feed-in escalation counts from year 1, so the rate jumps at year 21
description: Source: #52 spec review, 2026-09-26. The feed-in rate is held nominal for its 20 guaranteed years, then should rise with escalation.feed_in; the engine applies (1 + feed_in)^(y - 1) counted from year 1, so at year 21 the rate jumps by 20 years of escalation at once when feed_in != 0. Count from the end of the guarantee (hisim/economics/calculators/energy.py ~317-324) and fix the spec's §6.1 sentence.

title: Evaluate and test option A for the water storages: generator books against the end-of-step (implicit) return temperature
description: Owner (cmf, 2026-09-27): hisim-4g9.16 is fixed with option B (the vessel updates on booked energy, delivery capped, accepted heat fed back). Option A must still be evaluated and tested properly, because the mixing in the storage tank is crucial for heat pumps in particular: the return temperature a heat pump sees sets its COP. Option A: the storage reports its end-of-step temperature as the return to the generator (and the supply to the heat distribution); the generator books m*c*dT from there; conserves energy at convergence. Evaluate against B on the RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib) and a plain HP setup at 300/900/3600 s: COP, electricity, iteration counts, oscillation at coarse dt, stratification (the mixing-factor path of a storage without heat exchanger). Measurements of the gap: hisim-4g9.16 comments, scratchpad egap/.

title: At 3600 s a whole hour goes to hot water and empties the space-heating buffer: split a timestep between space heating and hot water
description: Owner (cmf, 2026-09-27): accepted for now after hisim-4g9.16/hisim-6ehm (option B + draw feed-forward). DE gas house full year: 222 degree-hours below set at 3600 s (1.8 at 900 s), all within 2 steps of a hot-water hour when the DHW tank is below 45 C (the hot-water charge is never interrupted there) and the 170 l buffer empties; the distribution system's request lags one step. Fix: time-share a step between SH and DHW (fractional operation) for coarse timesteps, or size the buffer. Traces: scratchpad stor/.

title: Weather file readers: time zones, lengths and padding
description: Source: beads schema migration of 2026-09-28 (owner-approved proposal). Side findings of the renovisorissues #57 step-2 design (hisim-wps1) in hisim/components/weather/calculation.py and weather.py: readers that stamp a file's rows onto the wrong time zone, files shorter than their name says, padding with zeros, upsampling that comes up short, and dead sun-position code. Each child is unverified until confirmed.

title: Survey HiSim's hot-water components for the LCOH's useful-heat table
description:
Follow-up of PR #812 (hisim-4p86, the LCOH denominator is the useful heat the run measured).

`adapter.UsefulHeatSources` lists two sources of useful heat: the Building's
TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand (rooms) and SimpleDHWStorage's ThermalEnergyConsumptionDHW (hot water).
A run with a Building and no listed hot-water source divides the system cost per unit of heat by the
rooms' heat alone; the bridge logs a warning and the plausibility panel carries a WARN row
(`useful_heat_without_hot_water`) saying so.

Survey HiSim's components that deliver domestic hot water without a SimpleDHWStorage — combi boilers,
electric (instantaneous or stored) water heaters, heat-pump DHW paths, solar-thermal DHW, generic DHW
storages, the UTSP/LPG hot-water profiles — and for each name the output that states the heat drawn
(column, unit, sign convention). Then add the rows to `adapter.UsefulHeatSources` (kind HOT_WATER, sign
INTO_THE_HOUSE or LEAVING_THE_SOURCE), with the binding test in tests/test_economics_bridge.py.
Watch for double counting where a setup contains both a tank and a device that also states the drawn heat.

title: SH buffer control oscillates and underheats at coarse timesteps once the storage conserves energy
description:
Found while implementing hisim-4g9.16 (2026-09-27, worktree agent-stor, branch fix/storage-energy).

Once the water storages conserve energy (4g9.16, option B), the space-heating buffer shows the dynamics the old mass-mixing update damped away. The generator controllers (GenericBoilerController.modulate_power: full power 5 K below the set flow temperature, linear to minimum at the set temperature; the HPLib SH controller's on/off hysteresis) act on the buffer temperature only, with no feed-forward of the distribution system's draw, and the distribution system's request is one step old. With a small buffer (20 l/kW gas: 170 kg, M c = 0.2 kWh/K) the buffer swings:

- DE household_gas_building_sizer, full year: 900 s period-2 oscillation of +-2 K around the set flow temperature; 3600 s a period-3 limit cycle of 14..32 degC, and during DHW-priority hours the buffer empties to the indoor-air floor. Heat delivered to the building 12236 -> 12193 kWh (900 s), 12243 -> 10579 kWh (3600 s, -13.6 %); degree-hours more than 1 K below the heating set temperature 2.2 -> 96.7 (900 s), 3.2 -> 4681 (3600 s).
- RenoVisor mockup package (HPLib), 900 s: degree-hours 57 -> 291 (comfort rating 4 -> 2): during long DHW runs the buffer now drains to the indoor temperature at the real rate.

Options: feed-forward of the distribution system's request into the boiler modulation (P = request + M c (T_set - T0) / dt); a larger buffer or sizing rule; or sub-stepping. Owner decision needed; numbers and traces in the 4g9.16 report.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: Fixed in fix/storage-energy (agent-stor, uncommitted) per owner decision 2026-09-27: storages publish ThermalPowerDrawForecast + WaterMassInStorage; GenericBoilerController modulating path asks the boiler for draw + M c (T_set - T0)/dt (new ThermalPowerSetpoint, boiler inverts its efficiency curve, min lift 5 K) and lets a DHW charge yield a step when the SH buffer would drop > 5 K below the flow temperature (tank >= 45 degC); HPLib SH/DHW controllers switch on the forecast after the step's draw and the DHW controller yields steps likewise. DE gas 900 s degree-hours 1.8 (pre-B 2.2), 3600 s no limit cycle (222 degree-hours remain: one 1 h DHW slot empties the 170 l buffer, then the HDS's one-step-late request is zero); RV baseline 5.8 (rating 5), package 25.0 (rating 4 -> 5). Balance <= 6e-15 kWh/step at 300/900/3600 s.

title: The audit export shows the battery's energy-management controller with its own database lifetime, not the battery's
description: Left open by PR #867 (renovisorissues #77.2): the controller is costless and dated/renewed with the battery via lifetime_of_asset_class, but hisim/economics/audit.py still displays its own ENERGY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM lifetime. Display only, no money.

title: Decide whether the air conditioner's building-load sizing is inverted (effective capacity falls as the load rises)
description:
Source: the #816 bless (#821, 2026-09-24) and the history of hisim/components/air_conditioner.py.

AirConditionerConfig.for_building_load picks the catalogue unit whose heating capacity (at the reference temperature) is nearest the building's heating load and sets scale_factor = capacity * CAPACITY_SHARE_FOR_BUILDING_LOAD (0.6) / heating_load. The component multiplies every heating/cooling capacity and power by scale_factor, so the capacity it runs with is capacity^2 * 0.6 / load: the larger the building's load, the SMALLER the effective unit. The docstring's intent ('sizes it down to' the load, 'run below its rating') suggests scale_factor = 0.6 * load / capacity (running at 60 % of the load) or 0.6 alone.

Evidence (#821, air_conditioned_house, one week): a door on the doorless TABULA row raised the heating load 9619 -> 9780 W (+1.7 %); scale_factor fell 0.5364 -> 0.5276; heat delivered fell 768.5 -> 758.1 kWh while the theoretical demand rose 600 -> 661 kWh; K*h below setpoint 45 -> 63 (+40 %), minimum room temperature 17.27 -> 16.93 degC.

History: introduced 2025-06-05 by efca6bcf (#392, 'Update air conditioner'; before it there was no scaling); unchanged through e2033174 (#547, 2026-08-07) and c7ce8f65 (#757, 2026-09-16, factory -> for_building_load). The 0.6 is 'determined heuristically based on manually experimenting', possibly against this formula. The effect is small while the nearest unit's capacity is close to the load (factor ~0.6 either way); it grows when it is not. Scope: hisim/components/air_conditioner.py and the air_conditioned_house setup (RenoVisor does not use air conditioners, not_implemented_yet).

Decide with the component's owner: the intended law (0.6 * load / capacity, or fixed 0.6, or other), then re-check the 0.6, re-record the air_conditioned_house twin and re-bless its golden (without force_rewrite).

title: Estimate an energy label per house from its simulated energy demand per m2 and year, on the country's scale
description:
Source: owner request 2026-09-25. result.json's kpis.energy_label is always null today (decision in hisim/renovisor/kpis.py: 'no BER/DEAP procedure in HiSim; no letter is invented'). The owner now wants an ESTIMATED label: the simulated annual energy demand per square metre of reference area, placed on the dwelling country's label scale.

Scope:
- One scale table per country the request schema admits (at least IE and DE, then ES and NL), each with its source, its basis and its bands. The bases differ and must be matched, not mixed: IE BER grades primary energy in kWh/m2a (A1..G), DE's Energieausweis grades final (or primary) energy in kWh/m2a (A+..H), ES's CEE grades non-renewable primary energy and CO2 by climate zone (A..G), NL's label grades primary fossil energy per NTA 8800 (A++++..G). Every threshold must be taken from the official source and cited, not from memory.
- The quantity: which simulated figure feeds each scale (final energy from all_kpis.json, or primary energy via the country's primary-energy factors), per m2 of which area (the scale's reference area vs HiSim's conditioned floor area / the request's living_area_in_m2), and annualised only from a full-year run (like the comfort grades: absent with a reason otherwise).
- Provenance: the label is an estimate from HiSim's simulation under its own weather, occupancy and control assumptions, not the certified procedure (DEAP, GEG, CE3X, NTA 8800). Publish it as approximated/estimated with that note and the figure it was derived from in the source string; never present it as an official rating.
- Reference and plan both get one, so the label change of a package is visible.
- Update the capability document's result row (KpiSchema), the translation map, and tell the frontend (renovisorissues heads-up) that energy_label stops being null; check the contract's Kpis.energy_label type (string) still fits.
Relates to hisim-kuna (the other placeholder KPIs) and hisim-ofqy (output unification: the label's source figure should come from the one place that owns it).

title: Upsampled NSRDB 15-min weather is two or one values short at 300 s and 600 s timesteps
description: Found while measuring hisim-4g9.16 (2026-09-27). The RenoVisor energy system of the vendored mockup request (IE, Dublin NSRDB_15MIN 2019, baseline) fails before the first timestep at sub-15-min resolutions: at 300 s 'The yearly weather arrays in this simulation's sim repository hold 105118 values but the simulation needs 105120'; at 600 s 52559 vs 52560. 105118 = (35040 - 1) * 3 + 1, i.e. the 15-min series is interpolated between its first and last sample without extending the last interval to the year end. So no IE (NSRDB 15-min) RenoVisor case can run below 900 s. Repro: translate calculation-request.mockup-1.yaml with measures: [], then hisim_main <file> with a full-year 2019 IE simulation file at seconds_per_timestep 300.

title: Make the golden-update workflow's force_rewrite checkbox say what it does and when not to tick it
description:
Source: owner, 2026-09-24, after bless PR #819 (for #816) was run with force_rewrite ticked by mistake.

The workflow_dispatch input of .github/workflows/golden-update.yml reads: "Overwrite every stored value with the fresh one, dropping KPIs the runs no longer produce." The owner read it as "write the new values for what changed" -- i.e. what a normal bless already does -- and ticked it. The forced run rewrote every golden verbatim, so 16 goldens that did not change got last-digit float noise (1e-16 .. 5e-10 relative) next to the one real change (air_conditioned_house), burying it and inviting conflicts; stale bless #817 looks the same.

Wanted: the input's description (the one line GitHub shows next to the checkbox) makes the default clear and the checkbox the exception, e.g.: "Leave UNTICKED for a normal bless: values within the gate's tolerance keep their stored value, so the PR shows only KPIs that really moved. Tick only to clear accumulated noise, retire a KPI or repair an unreadable golden: it rewrites EVERY value (float noise in every golden) and drops KPIs the runs no longer produce." Also consider renaming the input to something that reads as dangerous (e.g. force_rewrite_all_values), and make the bless PR body of a normal run say "only KPIs beyond tolerance were rewritten" and of a forced run warn at the top that every golden carries noise and that the reviewer should check the non-intended files. GitHub limits input descriptions in length -- keep the key sentence first. The file header comment (lines 6-12) already explains it; the checkbox text is what people actually read.

comments.author: cmf
comments.text: 2026-09-24, second pitfall: bless #820 ran on main although the reason said building-door-estimate -- the 'Use workflow from' branch selector of the Run workflow dialog defaults to main, and the reason text does not choose the branch. The input description (or the reason's default text) should say to pick the PR's branch in 'Use workflow from'; the workflow could also refuse to run on main unless the reason says so, or print the branch it ran on at the top of the bless PR body.

title: Every time step's convergence iteration starts from an all-zero vector instead of the previous step's converged values
description:
hisim/simulator.py:628 creates stsv once and the loop at :631-638 never reassigns it (the reset line is commented out, and its comment claims the opposite of what the code does); process_one_timestep clones the incoming vector (:388-389). So in pass 1 every component reads 0 from every output that sits later in file order: the iteration's starting point depends on component order, the heat pump carries a 'storage sends zero' workaround (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:3357-3362), and no step converges in fewer than 3 passes. Expected fix if confirmed: stsv = resulting_stsv after each step (warm start), remove the workaround; results change slightly; hydronic spec D7 (no simulator change) to be amended.

VERIFY FIRST (owner, 2026-10-03): confirm with a minimal reproduction that this is a defect and what it changes before fixing anything. Found by a read-only analysis of the convergence loop after measuring that component order changes one week's KPIs by 0.1-7 % (analysis: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-cmf-HiSim/8a0b0959-06ba-4050-82c1-5ca9a7a47108/scratchpad/order/convergence_analysis.md; measurement artefacts in the same directory). Citations against origin/main 0921f9bd.
close_reason: Done in the simulator warm-start PR: Simulator.run_all_timesteps now hands each step's converged values to the next step (stsv = resulting_stsv), so only step 0 starts from zeros; the misleading comment is corrected, tests/test_simulator_warm_start.py pins the warm start, and the heat pump's DHW zero guard stays as a documented step-0 guard until the controller restore fix (hisim-4g9.28).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: Relinked from the #909 review (finding M4, 2026-10-10), against hydronic-stage-c 0cce1839: the zeroing now sits in hot_water() (more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:1408, self.minimum_thermal_output_power = 0.0), and it has a second consequence. The hplib cache key (CalculationRequest in cached_hplib_result, around :2045) holds t_in_primary, t_in_secondary, t_amb, mode and operation_mode but not p_th_min, while heatpump.simulate is called with p_th_min=minimal_thermal_power_in_watt (:2063). A grid point first computed before the first hot-water step is cached with p_th_min = 1800 W, one first computed after it with 0 W, and both are reused for the rest of the run. Results therefore depend on whether a grid point was cached before or after the first hot-water step, not only on the restore defect described above. Fix both together: restore the minimum (or keep it in the saved state) and put p_th_min into the cache key.

title: force_convergence accepts steps where controller and plant carry different states: 4.5-4.8 % of all 900 s steps
description:
After 10 tries (simulator.py:415-416) controllers skip their computation (e.g. more_advanced_heat_pump_hplib.py:2835, :3351; heat_distribution_system.py:1194) but restore_state has already reset their internal state, so stsv keeps pass 12's output while the controller's memory is the start-of-step state; the plant (heat pump :1496, storages, EMS :823, battery) keeps computing on the frozen outputs and advances its own timers (:1953). Measured on the heat-pump twin, one week at 900 s: 32 forced steps (original order) / 30 (reordered) = ~8 h per week; every step with more than 7 passes is a limit cycle the freeze ends (histogram 14-15 passes). At step 44 the frozen state heats at 10.3 kW with the buffer above its switch-on point and an HDS flow temperature not derivable from its own inputs. Root cause of the cycles: the EMS surplus sign test (:765, :782) includes the heat pump's own draw, so 'on' is never a consistent state. Expected fix if confirmed: controllers decide on start-of-step values (hydronic D4 extended to the EMS, surplus from exogenous + start-of-step quantities with hysteresis), skip restore for frozen components, and a forced-step counter with target 0.

VERIFY FIRST (owner, 2026-10-03): confirm with a minimal reproduction that this is a defect and what it changes before fixing anything. Found by a read-only analysis of the convergence loop after measuring that component order changes one week's KPIs by 0.1-7 % (analysis: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-cmf-HiSim/8a0b0959-06ba-4050-82c1-5ca9a7a47108/scratchpad/order/convergence_analysis.md; measurement artefacts in the same directory). title: GenericBoiler's maximal_thermal_power_in_watt is the maximal fuel input, so a boiler sized to the heating load delivers only about efficiency x load
description: Where: hisim/components/generic_boiler.py. GenericBoiler.i_simulate (lines ~688-708) burns control_signal * maximal_thermal_power_in_watt (maximum_power_used_in_watt, also the fuel energy) and delivers that times real_combustion_efficiency, which runs between eff_th_min = 0.60 and eff_th_max = 0.90 (GenericBoilerConfig, lines ~207-208). The sizing law MAXIMAL_POWER_LAW (lines ~189-195, scale_thermal_power ~104-122) sets that field to the building's heating load, or 2.5 kW per apartment for DHW, whichever is larger, plus 10 % when the boiler serves SH and DHW. So the field named thermal is the fuel input, and a boiler sized by the law delivers at most about 0.9 x the heating load (plus the 10 % margin): it is undersized by the efficiency. Found in the review of PR #900; the assemblies' power_in_watt descriptions now say fuel input (wording only). Open questions: rename the field (to a fuel-input name) and/or divide the law by the maximal efficiency so the delivered heat covers the load. Either changes every boiler twin's goldens (gas, oil, pellets, wood chips, hydrogen, and the setups that use GenericBoiler), so the fix gets its own PR with a golden re-bless.

title: ElectricHeating delivers the building's full demand in space-heating-only steps, ignoring maximum_electric_power_w
description:
Evidence: hisim/components/generic_electric_heating.py, ElectricHeating.i_simulate. The HeatingMode.SPACE_HEATING branch (lines 427-444) sets thermal_power_sh_delivered_in_watt to the Building's TheoreticalHeatingDemand and the energy to TheoreticalHeatingEnergyDemand whenever the demand is positive, with no reference to config.maximum_electric_power_w. The parallel branch, HeatingMode.SPACE_HEATING_AND_DOMESTIC_HOT_WATER_IN_PARALLEL (lines 467-513), caps space heating at maximum_electric_power_w minus the DHW power (available_electric_load_in_watt, line 497, min() at 504-511). The electric outputs equal the thermal ones (direct resistive heating), so the same holds for the electricity drawn.

Consequence: with parallel_space_heating_and_dhw_option true (household_electric_heating_building_sizer and energy_systems/assemblies/heating/electric_resistive.assembly.yaml), every step without hot-water demand runs SPACE_HEATING and is uncapped. A stated maximum_electric_power_w below the building's demand has no effect in those steps, so the delivered heat and the electricity drawn are overstated. AUTO sizing hides it: the law sets the power to the building's heating load, which the demand rarely exceeds.

Fix: cap the SPACE_HEATING branch as the parallel branch does (power at min(demand, maximum_electric_power_w), energy at min(energy demand, maximum_electric_power_w * seconds_per_timestep / 3600)), then re-bless the electric-heating goldens (household_electric_heating_building_sizer week and year) and re-check the heating/electric_resistive monotone and expect figures. Found in the review of PR #904; owner decision 2026-10-08: its own PR, not #904.

title: The energy manager switches its temperature raise on a +-5e-12 W surplus, so a 1e-13 K flip in a storage loops forever; fix it at the source (hysteresis or a threshold) and remove the tank's 1e-9 K deadband
description:
Source: hydronic stage C (branch hydronic-stage-c), commit 858f5012; roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §6 (owner, 2026-10-09).

L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.modify_set_temperatures_for_components_in_case_of_surplus_electricity (hisim/components/controller_l2_energy_management_system.py) raises the building, buffer and hot-water set temperatures when available_surplus_electricity_in_watt > 0, the surplus left after the battery is dispatched. When the battery balances the house exactly, that surplus is float noise: measured +-5e-12 W at step 758 of household_heatpump_building_sizer (full year 2021 at 900 s, predefined occupancy profile) and at step 10674 of household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer. A converged DHW tank whose step mean flips between two neighbouring floats (about 1e-13 K apart at 70 °C) moves the heat pump's hot-water electricity by 5e-12 W, the sign flips, the raises toggle 0 <-> 10 K (building 0 <-> 2 K), the building's demand toggles with them, and the simulator aborts after 100 tries.

Stopgap in stage C (owner, 2026-10-09): SimpleDHWStorage publishes the same float once its step mean moves by at most PUBLISHED_MEAN_DEADBAND_IN_KELVIN = 1e-9 K. Fix at the source: a threshold or a hysteresis on the surplus the energy manager switches on (or deciding on start-of-step values, hisim-4g9.28), then remove the deadband and its spec sentence and show the heat-pump twins' years at 900 s complete without it. Related to hisim-4g9.28 (the energy manager's on/off loops at force_convergence): the same switching rule, here at zero surplus rather than at the heat pump's own draw.
close_reason: The energy manager decides with a 0.01 W hysteresis around zero surplus; the heat-pump twins' years complete without the simulator's 1e-9 deadband, which is removed (branch ems-surplus-hysteresis).

comments.author: noah
comments.text: 2026-10-10 (hydronic-stage-c, guideline review F2, owner decision): the 1e-9 K deadband left the tank. The simulator now holds any output a component declares accelerated within 1e-9 of the value it stood at (hisim/fixed_point_acceleration.py, SecantAcceleration.DEADBAND); the tank declares its two step-mean outputs. Removing the deadband after the energy-manager fix now means deleting held_value's use there; the full-year measurements (spec §6) show the heat-pump twins abort without it.

comments.author: noah
comments.text:
Fixed on branch ems-surplus-hysteresis (between #912 and #914), owner decision 2026-10-10: a hysteresis. L2GenericEnergyManagementSystem.raises_set_temperatures (pure, transition-table test) raises above +0.01 W surplus after the battery, not below -0.01 W, and keeps the previous step's decision within the band (edges included). The previous decision is the manager's frozen EMSState, read from the saved state and advanced only in i_save_state. Band: 1e9 x the +-5e-12 W float noise and 10 x the ~1e-3 W a converged surplus can move under the simulator's 1e-4 tolerance; inside it at most 0.01 W goes to or from the grid whichever decision is kept (at most 88 Wh a year at any step length).

The simulator's 1e-9 deadband (SecantAcceleration.DEADBAND, held_value, StepAcceleration.hold) and its spec sentence are removed; under forced convergence the simulator no longer touches the accelerated outputs. The secant acceleration stays (without it the gas twin at 900 s has 52 forced steps instead of 0, the heat-pump-and-solar twin 5.08 instead of 4.77 passes at 900 s and 6.33 instead of 5.20 at 3600 s).

Full year 2021, predefined occupancy, on #912's head (no warm start), mean passes / forced steps:
(a) no deadband, no hysteresis: heat pump aborts at step 22058 (60 s), 1414 (900 s), 158 (3600 s); heat pump + solar at 22101, 1232, 979.
(b) no deadband, hysteresis: all six complete. Heat pump 6.21 / 89091 (60 s), 7.39 / 8550 (900 s), 8.79 / 3038 (3600 s); heat pump + solar 4.38 / 3467, 4.77 / 1540, 5.20 / 554.
With the deadband and no hysteresis (#912 as is): heat pump 7.37 / 8396 (900 s), 8.79 / 2980 (3600 s); heat pump + solar 4.80 / 1725, 5.19 / 553.

title: Refuse thermalpower_dhw_is_constant=true when the hot-water controller is built, for every storage position, or remove the field
description: MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHWConfig.thermalpower_dhw_is_constant (with p_th_max_dhw_in_watt) asks the hplib heat pump for a constant hot-water power. Since hydronic stage B (PR #908) the heat pump books the heat its flow carries, so with a parallel storage it refuses the flag at runtime, at the first hot-water step (ValueError naming thermalpower_dhw_is_constant), and in the fixed-flow mode (a series storage or none) it silently ignores it. No file in the repository sets it. Wanted: refuse true when the controller is built, for every storage position, so the configuration fails before the simulation starts and the fixed-flow mode no longer ignores it. Option: remove the field and p_th_max_dhw_in_watt altogether (config schema, the energy-system recorder, the controller's ThermalPowerHPForDHWConst outputs and the heat pump's matching inputs).
close_reason: Removed on hydronic-stage-c (#909, guideline review finding F9, owner 2026-10-10): thermalpower_dhw_is_constant and p_th_max_dhw_in_watt, the controller's two outputs, the heat pump's two inputs, their default connections, the refusal and the controller's print are gone; schema regenerated. No setup or energy-system file set the option.

title: The boiler's total fuel KPI sums two separately rounded parts and differs from its meter's by up to 0.1 kWh
description:
`GenericBoiler.get_cost_opex` (hisim/components/generic_boiler.py, around :890-912) rounds the space-heating and the hot-water fuel to 0.1 kWh each and books their sum as "Total <carrier> consumption (energy)"; the meters round the one total once (GasMeter to 0.1 kWh, FuelMeter to 0.01 kWh). Every step agrees, but the two totals can differ by up to 0.1 kWh, and the boiler's volume, mass, cost and CO2 KPIs follow from the doubly rounded total.

Measured on hydronic-stage-c (one day, 900 s): the gas, oil and hydrogen composed files burn 76.531 + 10.635 = 87.166 kWh; the boiler reports 76.5 + 10.6 = 87.1, the GasMeter 87.2 and the FuelMeter 87.17. Pellets: boiler 201.0, FuelMeter 201.07 on 201.069 burned. GenericDistrictHeating and GenericElectricHeating round their two parts the same way (district heating on the test day: 56.3 + 5.5 = 61.8, the FuelMeter 61.77).

Fix: sum the unrounded series, round the total once (and each part for its own KPI). This moves KPI values in the goldens by up to 0.1 kWh, so it needs a golden re-bless; the assembly test of the gas house (tests/assemblies/test_assembly_crossing.py) already compares the meter per step on the unrounded results.

title: The golden history stitching does not know the fleet-wide KPI key suffix rename of the stable KPI addresses
description: scripts/golden_kpi_renames.py is the table scripts/golden_history.py stitches renamed golden keys with. The stable KPI addresses (hisim-b3b.1, branch feat/kpi-addresses, roadmap/kpi_address_spec.md) key every component KPI as '<name> (<source.name>)' whether or not a collision exists, so the re-bless after that PR renames almost every component KPI key of every golden (e.g. BUI1.Building.Conditioned floor area -> BUI1.Building.Conditioned floor area (Building)), while keys already suffixed since #653 stay unchanged. Until the table carries this rename, every component KPI's history splits into two half-length series at the re-bless commit. The rename is fleet-wide in shape but not one literal pair per name (the suffix is the source component's runtime name, which differs per setup, and the flat goldens store no source), so the table needs either one entry per (pair, key) derived from the re-bless diff, as the module docstring prescribes, or a declared fleet-wide rule '<key>' -> '<key> (<suffix>)' restricted to the re-bless commit and to keys whose value is unchanged. title: Circuit laws for the hydronic ports: an owner publishes its outlet-vs-inlet curve so a node solves the step exactly in 2-3 iterations (if pure (m, T) ports get slow or biased)
description:
Owner decision 2026-10-01: the generator-storage coupling is redesigned in the temperature domain with PURE (m, T) ports — mass flow, supply and return temperature only; energy only derived as m c dT; no accepted-heat back-channel (PR #864's design rejected as an interim fix). This bead keeps the alternative analysed the same day, for when iteration counts or accuracy become a problem.

ALTERNATIVE: circuit laws. Each circuit owner publishes, besides m, its outlet-vs-inlet curve in temperatures only: T_out(T_in) = T_in + clamp(T_target - T_in, -max_drop(T_in), +max_lift(T_in)), max_lift = a + b*T_in (K, K/K; boiler: P_max/(m c), b = 0; heat pump: tangent of hplib's P_th(T_in)/(m c) at the current return estimate, b < 0). The water-holding node (mixed vessel, or HDS pipe water without a buffer) integrates C dT/dt = sum_i m_i c (T_out,i(T) - T) - UA (T - T_amb) exactly, piecewise-exponential across the kinks (<= 2 per circuit, each crossed once), and publishes per circuit the realized step means T_sup and T_ret; owners book Q = m c dt (T_sup - T_ret). The balance closes by construction; a heating-only source can never push the vessel above its T_target; cooling falls out (colder target). For a non-linear curve (hplib) the tangent is re-drawn at each iterate: Newton-like, quadratic convergence.

WHY PURE PORTS CONVERGE TO A BIASED ANSWER: the generator sends one supply temperature computed at the guessed return; the node must treat it as constant over the step. A heat pump holds its lift, not its supply temperature, so the node models the wrong reaction (with a fixed supply, every K the tank warms cuts the delivered heat by m c = 670 W/K instead of the heat pump's ~135 W/K). The iteration converges to the answer consistent with that assumption — converged = self-consistent, not correct.

TOY NUMBERS (300 kg tank at 35 degC, 6 kW draw, HP 0.16 kg/s, P_th = 9000*(1 - 0.015 x - 0.0004 x^2), x = T_in - 35; reference = 200k Euler sub-steps):
- 3600 s: reference mean 38.749, end 41.962, heat 8429 W (HP 9.0 -> 7.9 kW). Pure ports: 17 iterations, supply frozen at 51.82, mean 39.369 (+0.62 K), end 41.712, heat 8341 W (11.3 -> 6.8 kW). Law (single tangent): 3 iterations, mean 38.768 (+0.019 K, curvature over a 7 K swing).
- 900 s (the RenoVisor resolution, hisim/renovisor/simulation.py:74): reference mean 36.040, end 37.046, heat 8854 W. Pure ports: 8 iterations, mean 36.101 (+0.06 K), end 37.040, heat 8847 W (< 0.1 %).
- Design-draft measurements (agent, 300 kg buffer, 10 kW boiler, HDS 6 kW): plain fixed point boiler holding 55 degC 3/8/15 iterations at 60/900/3600 s; power-limited boiler 4/11/41; district heating -> HDS without buffer (30 kg pipe water, 900 s) 24 iterations and end 43.66 degC vs exact 44.18; law + exact node 2 iterations in all cases. Plain fixed-point contraction theta = 1 - (1 - e^-a)/a, a = sum(m) dt / M: tends to 1 for long steps or small vessels.
- Simulator limits (hisim/simulator.py:322-324): controllers frozen (force_convergence) after 10 tries, run aborted after 100; tolerance 1e-4 absolute on every output (hisim/component.py:189-195).

WHEN TO PICK THIS UP: iteration counts near 10 (frozen controllers) at 900 s or 3600 s, runtime problems from iterations, setups without a buffer (generator -> HDS) converging slowly, or visible bias at large steps / at regime switches inside a step (thermostat taking over, tap mixing valve below 40 degC, heat pump at max outlet temperature). The law is a pure temperature-domain extension of the pure ports (adds T_target and K, K/K parameters per circuit), so it can be added later without redesigning the ports.

title: Pin a meter's carrier and fuel constants from its provider so a file with two energy_carrier providers can be sized
description:
Decided (owner, 2026-10-08, review of PR #899; spec §5.1, the §13.1 cut table and D30 amended): in v1 a meter's carrier, and a fuel meter's heating value and density, follow its class's law from the file's one `energy_carrier` provider, as in the twins, which write no line for it (D28). Pinning them from the provider, which the earlier §5.1 wording asked for, is cut from v1 and tracked here.

Evidence:
- hisim/components/gas_meter.py: `CARRIER_LAW = Size.ENERGY_CARRIER`, the law of `gas_loadtype` (around :68 and :84 on main as of 2026-10-08).
- hisim/components/fuel_meter.py: the same `CARRIER_LAW` on `fuel_loadtype` (around :59 and :74), plus the heating-value and density laws.
- The providers of the `energy_carrier` fact: `GenericBoiler` (generic_boiler.py, around :242 and :257) and `generic_district_heating` (`DistrictHeatingConfig.ENERGY_CARRIER`, around :135 and :148).
- hisim/config/engine.py (around :360): a scalar read binds by the bare-fact rule only when `len(candidates) == 1`, else `_unbindable_error`. So a second `energy_carrier` provider of ANY value is refused at sizing: a second burner of the same fuel, or a boiler beside a district heating connection.
- Step 3 already checks the fuel constants of a provider's consumers in the expansion (EF-7Z). Two burners with equal constants therefore pass that check and then fail at sizing (EF-4B).

Gate implication: the twins write no carrier line on the meter, so a carrier pinned from the provider and written as a config line differs from every twin. Pinning needs either an intended difference in the twin gates or an omit-when-equal rule (write the line only where the law would not give the same value, as D28's G9 does for parameters).

Due: before the first file with two `energy_carrier` providers: a gas boiler beside a gas cooker (step 6), a boiler beside district heating, or a hybrid.

title: Test the solar thermal assembly's collection when its composed file and gate arrive with hydronic stage C
description:
Evidence (owner review of PR #905, 2026-10-08): the test contract of energy_systems/assemblies/heating/solar_thermal.assembly.yaml cannot fail on the collector's physics. The isolation run is the fixed test day, 1 January in Aachen at 900 s; at most 53 W/m² reach the collector plane, the collector never gets 10 K above the cylinder, so the solar pump never starts. The contract's only monotone sweep is the investment cost over area_in_m2 (797 EUR per m², 1594 to 15940 EUR over 2 to 20 m²), and its expect entry is 0.0 kWh of heat delivered at the defaults. The bounds hold trivially for every output that only moves while the pump runs. What the contract tests is the assembly's build, its bounds and its pricing, not collection.

What an effective test needs: a run in which the pump starts, either an isolation day with sun (the harness has one fixed test day for every assembly, and the owner does not want the harness changed for this) or the full-year golden of the assembly's composed file, whose summer covers collection. Until then the collector's physics is covered by the goldens of the two solar twins (household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer).

Due: with hydronic stage C (hisim-fxix.4), which brings the solar composed files and their gates (spec §13 step 5). Then add a monotone sweep or an expect entry on the heat the collector delivers, measured on a run with sun, and check that it can fail.

title: One ground albedo for every plane-of-array computation: the solar thermal collector uses pvlib's default 0.25 while Window.ALBEDO and the PV system's ALBEDO are 0.2
description: Found reviewing PR #876 (2026-10-04). Three components compute irradiance on a tilted plane with pvlib.irradiance.get_total_irradiance: generic_pv_system/calculation.py passes ALBEDO = 0.2 (line ~113); building/window.py passes Window.ALBEDO = 0.2 (a class attribute since #876, with tests/test_building_window.py pinning it equal to the PV constant); solar_thermal_system.py (plane_of_array_irradiance_w_m2, around line 42) passes no albedo and therefore gets pvlib's default 0.25. One ground in front of the house, two values. Resolution: one shared constant in a core module below the components (as hisim/hydronics.py holds the water constants, cf. PR #890), passed explicitly by all three callers; the EN ISO 52010-1:2017 default 0.2 is the documented choice. Result change: solar thermal collector irradiance moves slightly (ground-reflected share 0.2 vs 0.25 of GHI times (1-cos tilt)/2), so one golden re-bless for the solar-thermal twins, announced. Done when: grep for get_total_irradiance shows every call passing the shared albedo, and the equality test becomes an identity.

title: Refuse NaN and negative irradiance at the weather boundary once, for every consumer, instead of each consumer guarding (window returns 0 on NaN, nothing clamps negatives)
description: Found reviewing PR #876 (2026-10-04). building/window.py returns 0.0 when the plane-of-array irradiance is NaN (a silent zero gain; #876 is asked to raise instead), and no consumer clamps slightly negative GHI/DHI (night zero-offsets in some weather sources), which would give negative window gains, PV output or collector irradiance. hisim/components/weather/calculation.py handles only the horizon divisor (around lines 836-862), it does not validate the irradiance columns. Resolution per the fail-hard rule: the Weather component validates its irradiance series once after loading (DNI, DHI, GHI, extraterrestrial: finite and >= 0; small negative night offsets are a data defect to refuse by name with the source file and timestep, not to clamp silently — if a known source needs a tolerance, state it as a documented threshold), so every consumer (window, PV, solar thermal, air conditioner) can drop its own guard. Check every bundled weather source (DWD TRY, EPW readers, the IE data) for negatives/NaNs before enabling, and the UTSP/renovisor paths. Done when: the weather component refuses bad irradiance by name, the consumers' NaN guards are gone, and a test feeds a NaN and a negative value through the loader.

title: A stated boiler seasonal efficiency below 30 % maps to eff_th_min above eff_th_max, and the boiler config cannot refuse the inversion without breaking the translator
description: Found in the review of PR #909 (R33, 2026-10-10). The translator maps heating.seasonal_efficiency_in_percent (request schema 1-400) to eff_th_max = value/100 and eff_th_min = max(eff_th_max - 0.3, 0.3) (hisim/renovisor/constants.py BoilerEfficiency, from calculation-request.md section 3.6). Below 30 % that rule contradicts itself: 1 % gives eff_th_min 0.3 > eff_th_max 0.01. GenericBoilerConfig therefore only refuses non-finite or non-positive efficiencies (PR #909); a check eff_th_min <= eff_th_max (and any upper bound) breaks 75 RenoVisor tests whose capability probes build the boundary requests. An upper bound of 1 would also be wrong: condensing boilers on the lower heating value reach 105-109 %. Owner decision 2026-10-10: keep #909 at 'finite and > 0' and agree the mapping with the contract side first. Options: cap the floor at the maximum (eff_th_min = max(eff_th_max - 0.3, min(0.3, eff_th_max))) and state it in the contract; or narrow the boiler's allowed range in the request schema (e.g. 30-115 %); then enforce eff_th_min <= eff_th_max in the boiler config.

title: Model solar priority in the controllers: the collector charges above the backup's target, optionally holding the backup back, instead of both stopping at 60 degC
description:
Source: owner discussion 2026-10-10 on the part-load prototype (PRs #915-#918, roadmap/hydronic_part_load_spec.md) and hydronic stage C (#909, roadmap/hydronic_coupling_spec.md §5, §5.3, §5.5, D4).

## Problem

In the setups with a solar collector and a backup (household_gas_solar_thermal_building_sizer, household_heatpump_solar_thermal_building_sizer, and RenoVisor requests with solar_thermal_system), the solar collector and the backup charge the same hot-water cylinder to the same temperature. Neither controller knows about the other:

- **Solar controller** (SolarThermalSystemController, hisim/components/solar_thermal_system.py):
  - the pump switches on when the collector is warmer than the cylinder by its switch-on lift. That is decided on the cylinder's step mean, an owner exception to D4 from stage C;
  - the pump stops when the cylinder was above its 60 °C aim at the start of the step (decided on T0). On the step mean that stop has no fixed point: 21507 forced steps a year at 60 s.
- **Backup controllers** charge to about 60 °C as well:
  - GenericBoilerController: warm-water aim 60 °C, hysteresis 10 K, supply capped at 70 °C;
  - MoreAdvancedHeatPumpHPLibControllerDHW: t_max − 0.5 K, plus the energy manager's raise of up to +10 K on PV surplus;
  - ElectricHeatingController: aim 60 °C, hysteresis 15 K.

So at 60 s both run at the same time whenever both are on, until the cylinder reaches about 60 °C. The backup keeps the cylinder near 60 °C, and the collector often has nowhere to put its heat. Solar yield is therefore probably modelled too low even at 60 s. Real systems separate the two by control:

- **Different temperatures:** solar charges the cylinder up to its maximum (typically 80-90 °C, below a safety limit); the backup only tops up to a lower target (typically 55-60 °C), usually with its sensor in the upper part of the cylinder.
- **Solar priority:** the backup is held back while the collector delivers, or is expected to, with a minimum-temperature guard so the tap stays served.
- **Sensor heights:** they only matter once the cylinder is stratified (hisim-fxix.1).

## Owner decision (2026-10-10)

Priority between solar and backup is a **control strategy** and belongs in the **controllers, not in the physics**.
- The part-load mechanism (hisim-naze and the part-load spec) does not encode any priority: generators on the same store whose controllers are on with the same target share one part-load fraction, iterated against the store's end temperature.
- The prototype's "solar first" rule (the backup counting the solar inflow as running anyway) is to be removed from the physics.
- Because the controllers behave the same at every step length, the 60 s run stays the reference that coarse runs reproduce, whatever strategy the controllers implement.
- Order: do this AFTER the part-load iteration lands, so its effect is measured against an unchanged mechanism.

## Options to evaluate (the owner wants a good solution, not a fixed one)

1. **Raise the solar stop above the backup target:**
   - a configurable solar maximum (e.g. 80-85 °C) in SolarThermalSystemControllerConfig, with presets;
   - the backup keeps 60 °C;
   - the cylinder's mixing valve at the tap (stage C, §4.3) already serves the tap from a hotter cylinder;
   - standby losses rise, which is realistic.

   Check: the cylinder assembly's contract bounds, the generators' maximum supply temperatures, and the energy manager's raise interplay.
2. **Backup inhibition while the solar pump runs**, with a minimum-temperature guard (e.g. do not let the cylinder fall below 45 °C). Watch for fixed points: decide on T0 or on values that do not move within the iteration (D4); a decision on the step mean that its own effect changes can cycle, as the solar stop did.
3. **Both (1) and (2).**
4. **Later, with a stratified cylinder (hisim-fxix.1):** sensor heights for backup (top) and solar (bottom).

## Constraints and pitfalls from earlier work

- Controllers decide on the start-of-step temperature T0 (D4). The only exception is the solar pump's switch-on on the step mean. A stop or inhibition decided on the step mean can lose its fixed point.
- Stage C caps every backup's hot-water supply at its controller's set temperature and at its maximum supply temperature (§5); the cylinder conserves energy exactly per step.
- Since hisim-4g9.23 the simulator warm-starts every step. The energy manager's knife edge (hisim-4g9.28, hisim-4g9.31) still causes forced steps in heat-pump houses.
- The units-in-names rule (AGENTS.md) applies to every new field and output.

## Effects to expect and handle

- The 60 s results of the two solar twins change: re-bless the goldens in CI with golden-update.yml.
- RenoVisor solar requests change: post a heads-up issue on renovisorissues before merge.
- Reference values from stage C, to compare against:
  - gas + solar twin, full year at 900 s: collector 389 kWh;
  - RenoVisor mockup with solar_thermal_system: reported solar heat 197 kWh.
- Re-record the twins if a controller config field is added, and check the solar assembly (heating/solar_thermal) parameters and bounds.

## Done when

- The chosen strategy is configurable through controller config fields with presets, named with units.
- Collector yield, backup fuel or electricity, and unmet hot water at 60 s are reported before and after, with a physical justification of the new defaults.
- The part-load runs at 900 s and 3600 s still agree with the new 60 s reference within 1 %.
- Goldens are blessed in CI and the heads-up is posted.
